Tera R6 object, which serves as a template library with encapsulated methods
for rendering templates with a given context. Template syntax supports
additional logic, including built-in filters, tests, and functions, as well
as loops, conditions, and inheritance. Documentation for Tera's templating
syntax can be found at <https://keats.github.io/tera/>.
tera.author:
Kenneth Blake Vernon [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0098-5092>)

theoryforge.title: Systematic Theory Development
theoryforge.description:
Provides a rigorous, reproducible workflow for building,
developing and testing scientific theories represented as versioned,
machine-checkable objects. Functions read and validate theory objects,
score them against a versioned rigour checklist, screen constructs for
lexical redundancy, and emit byte-identical diagram intermediate
representations. The package is the feature-parity twin of a 'Python'
package of the same name, with behaviour pinned by a shared
specification so the two implementations produce identical verdicts.
theoryforge.author:
Pablo Bernabeu [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-1083-2460>)

tidycjk.title: Tidy Tools for Chinese, Japanese and Korean Text
tidycjk.description:
A tidy toolkit for text that is written in Chinese, Japanese or
Korean. Most text tooling in R assumes that words are separated by
whitespace, which CJK writing does not use, so ordinary summaries of a text
column either treat a sentence as one undifferentiated blob or split it into
isolated characters. Word segmentation is therefore a pluggable engine that
the caller names explicitly rather than a bundled dictionary, because where
a word ends is a fact about a language and not about Unicode. 'tidycjk'
classifies characters by Unicode block, reports which script and which
language a text is written in, measures how much of a text is CJK, and
turns those measurements into tibbles that slot straight into a
'tidyverse' workflow. It also measures display width in terminal columns,
pads and truncates to a width rather than to a character
count, and normalises fullwidth and halfwidth forms surgically -- including
composing halfwidth katakana voiced marks into single code points -- without
the collateral damage of a full 'NFKC' pass. Language detection deliberately
returns NA rather than guessing when a text is written in Han characters
only, because Japanese written without kana cannot be distinguished from
Chinese by script alone. Everything is derived from the Unicode
specification; the package makes no network requests and needs no compiled
code of its own.
tidycjk.author: Youzhi Yu [aut, cre]

tidygedcom.title: Read and Tidy 'GEDCOM' Genealogy Files
tidygedcom.description:
Reads and parses 'GEDCOM' (Genealogical Data Communication)
files, the standard interchange format exported by genealogical software,
and converts them into tidy data frames. Individuals, families, life
events, and parent-child links are extracted into rectangular structures
suitable for pedigree and kinship analysis. Additional helpers summarize
file contents, convert place coordinates, and repair malformed records.
Wikipedia family tree templates can be parsed into the same tidy
structure. For a discussion of these and related data structures
see [Hunter et al. (2026) <doi:10.1007/s10519-026-10259-z>].
tidygedcom.author:
S. Mason Garrison [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-4804-6003>),
Christian Waugh [aut, dtc] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-7871-5845>)

tiltdens.title: Tilted and Data-Sharpened Nonparametric Density Estimation
tiltdens.description:
High-order nonparametric density estimators built by perturbing a
conventional kernel estimator, either by re-weighting the observations
("tilting") or by moving them ("data sharpening"). The perturbation is
chosen so that the estimator inherits the fast convergence rate of an
infinite-order kernel estimator, such as the sinc or trapezoidal flat-top
estimator, while remaining a proper non-negative density without the
oscillatory tails those estimators suffer from. Two criteria are provided:
minimising the L2 distance to an infinite-order comparator, following
Doosti and Hall (2016) <doi:10.1111/rssb.12112>, and minimising a
cross-validation criterion that needs no comparator and is much faster,
following Doosti, Hall and Mateu (2018) <doi:10.1016/j.jspi.2017.12.003>.
tiltdens.author: Hassan Doosti [aut, cre, cph]

tmdbR.title: Modern 'R' Client for 'The Movie Database' API
tmdbR.description:
A modern, tested client for version 3 of 'The Movie Database'
('TMDB') API. It modernises the interface originally provided by the
legacy 'TMDb' package by Capozio (2020)
<https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=TMDb> while adding secure web
requests, bearer-token authentication, structured errors, retries, safe
query encoding, and automatic pagination.
tmdbR.author:
Gordon Kuzet [aut, cre, cph],
Andrea Capozio [ctb, cph] (Author of the legacy TMDb 1.1 package on
which the compatibility interface is based)

tradeIndices.title:
International Trade Intensity, Openness and Diversification
Measures
tradeIndices.description:
Calculates commonly used indicators for empirical international
trade analysis from user-supplied data. Measures include trade openness,
bilateral export and import intensity, the Herfindahl-Hirschman
concentration index, normalized and entropy-based diversification,
structural diversification relative to a benchmark, export similarity,
trade complementarity, revealed comparative advantage, and intra-industry
trade. Functions are vectorized where appropriate, validate economically
meaningful inputs, and require no external data service. The definition of
trade openness follows the World Bank indicator metadata
<https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/NE.TRD.GNFS.ZS>. Methodological
background for several trade indicators is provided by the World Bank's
World Integrated Trade Solution
<https://wits.worldbank.org/wits/wits/witshelp/Content/Utilities/e1.trade_indicators.htm>
and the World Trade Organization (2012, ISBN:9789287038128).
tradeIndices.author:
Chiranjit Mazumder [aut, cre],
Renjini V. R. [aut]

transfRgov.title:
Acquisition and Reading of Brazilian Federal Government Fund
Transfers
transfRgov.description:
Downloads, reads and organizes data on federal fund transfers
to Brazilian municipalities. Data are retrieved from the TransfereGov
"Fundo a Fundo" API, from the Portal da Transparência open data service
and from the Tesouro Transparente CKAN catalogue. The package offers one
reader per API endpoint, helpers that map SIAFI municipality codes to
IBGE codes, and routines that fetch the monthly transfer archives and
the tax waiver records published as open data.
transfRgov.author: Rodrigo Borges [aut, cre]

transittraj.title: Reconstruct and Visualize Transit Vehicle Trajectories
transittraj.description:
Today's public transit vehicles produce a large amount of automatic
vehicle location (AVL) data. This data is very useful for planning and
performance studies, but can be noisy, error-prone, and sparse. This package
provides tools for cleaning AVL point data and turning it into continuous,
differentiable, monotonic, and invertible vehicle trajectory functions,
based on the work of Robbennolt et al. (2025)
<doi:10.48550/arXiv.2509.00119> and
Huang et al. (2023) <doi:10.1109/ITSC57777.2023.10422524>.
transittraj.author:
Benjamin O'Brien [aut, cre, cph],
Lewis Lehe [aut]

trialdiff.title: Clinical Trial Data-Cut Change Detection and Impact Assessment
trialdiff.description:
A transparent, rule-based framework for detecting changes between
successive data cuts of clinical trial datasets, classifying those changes
into clinically meaningful categories, tracing user-defined data lineage,
and assessing which downstream analyses and outputs may be affected.
The package is designed to complement existing low-level data frame
comparison tools by adding clinical-trial-specific classification, lineage
and impact-assessment layers on top of deterministic comparison. The
rule-based classification is similar in spirit to the data validation
infrastructure of van der Loo and de Jonge (2021)
<doi:10.18637/jss.v097.i10>.
trialdiff.author: Hirujan Rangaraj [aut, cre]

tulpa.title:
Templated Unified Library for Posterior Approximation in
Bayesian Hierarchical Models
tulpa.description:
A general-purpose engine for fitting Bayesian hierarchical models
with spatial fields, temporal effects, spatially varying coefficients, and
multiple inference backends. Scalable spatial structure includes Hilbert
space approximate Gaussian processes (HSGP; Riutort-Mayol et al. 2023
<doi:10.1007/s11222-022-10167-2>), nearest-neighbor Gaussian processes
(NNGP; Datta et al. 2016 <doi:10.1080/01621459.2015.1044091>), intrinsic
conditional autoregressive models (ICAR; Besag, York, and Mollie 1991
<doi:10.1007/BF00116466>), the reparameterized Besag-York-Mollie model
(BYM2; Riebler et al. 2016 <doi:10.1177/0962280216660421>), and stochastic
partial differential equation fields (SPDE; Lindgren, Rue, and Lindstrom
2011 <doi:10.1111/j.1467-9868.2011.00777.x>). Temporal structure covers
random walks, autoregressive processes, and Gaussian processes. Inference
is tiered by correctness guarantee: exact Hamiltonian Monte Carlo with the
No-U-Turn sampler, Laplace and nested Laplace approximations with
hyperparameter integration (Rue, Martino, and Chopin 2009
<doi:10.1111/j.1467-9868.2008.00700.x>), and variational inference.
Model-specific packages plug observation likelihoods into the engine
through a templated C++ callback interface.
tulpa.author:
Gilles Colling [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-3070-6066>),
Frances Y. Kuo [ctb, cph] (Sobol direction numbers in
src/sobol_direction_numbers.h, BSD-3-clause),
Stephen Joe [ctb, cph] (Sobol direction numbers in
src/sobol_direction_numbers.h, BSD-3-clause)

tvbounds.title:
Sensitivity Analysis and Bounds under Total Variation
Neighborhoods
tvbounds.description:
Implements the sensitivity analysis framework of Palomba (2026)
"Sensitivity Analysis in Population Shares"
<https://filippopalomba.github.io/#jmp> for randomized experiments with
attrition, counterfactuals in structural models, and recentered
instrumental variables. Computes and plots sensitivity bounds together
with their confidence intervals and robustness summary measures.
tvbounds.author: Filippo Palomba [aut, cre, cph]

typedjson.title: Type-Faithful and Human-Readable JSON for R Values
typedjson.description:
Writing an R value as JSON that a human can read, and reading
it back unchanged. The 'jsonlite' package offers either a readable but
lossy pair of functions or a faithful but verbose one; this package
emits ordinary JSON for ordinary values and annotates only what JSON
cannot express, namely the distinction between integer and double,
typed missing values, non-finite numbers, attributes, and objects from
the S3, S4 and S7 systems.
typedjson.author:
Nicolas Bennett [aut, cre, cph],
YaoYuan [ctb, cph] (Author of the vendored yyjson library)

uSDT.title:
Hierarchical Signal Detection Theory Models for Unconscious
Processing
uSDT.description:
Fits hierarchical signal detection theory (SDT) models to paired
direct and indirect measures, the design used to test for unconscious
processing. Continuous indirect measures (typically response times) are
dichotomized with the within-subject median split of Meyen et al. (2022)
<doi:10.1037/xge0001065> so that both tasks are placed on a common
sensitivity scale. The package estimates a binomial probit mixed model in
which the two sensitivities are correlated random effects, and tests the
three hypotheses of interest: the group-level difference between
sensitivities, their latent correlation, and the latent regression of the
indirect on the direct measure, whose intercept is the test for
unconscious processing. Frequentist estimation uses 'lme4'.
uSDT.author:
Ricardo Rey-Sáez [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-6739-2035>),
Francisco Garre-Frutos [aut] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-9810-186X>),
Alicia Franco-Martínez [aut] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-9710-1240>),
Miguel Vadillo [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0001-8421-816X>)

undomanager.title: Manage the History of Any Object with Undo/Redo Operations
undomanager.description:
Track the history of any R object and move through it with undo
and redo operations. Anything can be stored, from a single number to a data
frame or an entire application state. A manager can restrict its history to
specific classes and cap how many items it keeps, and it can be reactive
to integrate with 'Shiny'.
undomanager.author: Dean Attali [aut, cre] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-5645-3493>)

uqsa.title: Uncertainty Quantification and Global Sensitivity Analysis
uqsa.description: In the field of systems biology, chemical reaction networks are modeled in various ways, two of those are: (i) stochastic simulations (e.g. Gillespie algorithm) and (ii) ordinary differential equations. In this package we use a simple tabular model description of reaction systems and automatically generate C code for either solver type. We use the ordinary differential equation solvers from the GNU Scientific Library and provide an interface that deals with lists of simulation experiments. Each simulation experiment contains both the data, and instructions for the model to replicate the data. We use approximate Bayesian computation methods (combined with Markov chain Monte Carlo and sequential Monte Carlo, particle filters) as well as classic methods such as Random Walk Metropolis (Gaussian transition kernel) and Simplified Manifold Metropolis adjusted Langevin algorithm for a Bayesian investigation of the model´s parameter space. Experiments can be evaluated in a sequence; intermediate probability densities are modeled using the 'VineCopula' package. The package is also intended to be useful in an HPC environment, with some functions that use 'pbdMPI' capabilities.
uqsa.author:
Alexandra Jauhiainen [aut],
Olivia Eriksson [aut, ctb, cph],
Federica Milinanni [aut],
Andrei Kramer [cre]

urbstatdata.title: Seven Data Sets for Urban and Built-Environment Statistics
urbstatdata.description:
Seven documented data sets from transport, traffic safety,
urban planning, construction and architectural engineering. The package
provides fixed, redistributable snapshots with consistent variable names.
Each help page records the source, licence, unit of observation,
transformations and limitations of its data set. Sources include Yeh
(2018) <doi:10.24432/C5J30W>, Tsanas and Xifara (2012)
<doi:10.24432/C51307>, Yeh (1998) <doi:10.24432/C5PK67>, Seoul Bike
Sharing Demand (2020) <doi:10.24432/C5F62R>, and Singh and Chaudhari
(2018) <doi:10.24432/C5P605>.
urbstatdata.author:
Mario Cools [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-3098-2693>)

uroscores.title: Scoring Tools for Urology and Pelvic Health Research Instruments
uroscores.description:
Scores standardized patient-reported instruments used in
urology and pelvic health research, including the International
Prostate Symptom Score (Barry et al., 1992), the Overactive Bladder
Symptom Score (Homma et al., 2006)
<doi:10.1016/j.urology.2006.02.042>, the O'Leary-Sant interstitial
cystitis indices, the short forms of the Urogenital Distress Inventory
and the Incontinence Impact Questionnaire (Uebersax et al., 1995)
<doi:10.1002/nau.1930140206>, the Sandvik incontinence severity index,
and the Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia Impact Index. Instruments are
declarative definitions read by a single scoring engine. Responses are
checked against the permitted value set of each item, missing items
follow the published rule for the instrument or return NA when none
was published, severity bands are assigned by membership, and
published minimal important difference statistics are included for
responder analyses.
uroscores.author: Muhammad Faiz Amirullah Nurhadi [aut, cre]

validateR.title: Simple Data Frame Validation and Quality Checks
validateR.description:
Checks a data frame for common data quality issues,
including missing values, outliers, duplicate rows, and type
inconsistencies. Results are returned as a structured
'validation_report' object with 'print' and 'plot' methods for
quick inspection.
validateR.author: Ugyen Norbu [aut, cre]

varmapack.title: Burn-in-Free Simulation and Analysis of Gaussian VARMA Models
varmapack.description:
Simulates Gaussian vector autoregressive-moving-average
time-series models without a burn-in period by drawing startup shocks from
their model-implied conditional distribution. Also provides model
test cases, autocovariances, spectral radii, and impulse responses.
varmapack.author: Kristján Jónasson [aut, cre]

vbpm.title: Variational Bayes Psychometric Models
vbpm.description:
Variational Bayes estimation for a family of psychometric
measurement models. Two models are provided. Variational Bayes factor
analysis (vbfa) is a regularized partially confirmatory factor model
spanning the confirmatory-exploratory continuum via spike-and-slab
priors on the loadings (Chen, Guo, Zhang, and Pan, 2021
<doi:10.1037/met0000293>; Chen, 2023 <doi:10.3758/s13428-022-01884-7>;
Jin and Chen, 2025 <doi:10.1080/10705511.2024.2432612>), with an optional
dynamic (warm-started) regularization path, an orthogonal bifactor
parameterization, and optional sparse residual (local dependence)
estimation through a graphical spike-and-slab prior solved by QUIC
(Jin, Chen, Yan, and Zhang, 2026 <doi:10.31234/osf.io/dehtv_v2>).
Regularized MIMIC (vbmimic) extends this to multiple-indicators
multiple-causes models, placing spike-and-slab priors on both the
measurement and the structural part (Jin and Chen, 2025
<doi:10.1080/00273171.2025.2483253>). Companion tools compute SEM-like
fit statistics, and sweep a factor-count window to report candidate fit,
criterion, and between-candidate loading-correspondence measurements
without selecting a count (Chen and Jin, 2026
<doi:10.48550/arXiv.2607.07159>). Data generators for either model family
are also provided.
vbpm.author:
Jinsong Chen [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0157-5469>),
Yi Jin [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-8604-5992>)

visATC.title: Visualise the Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) Hierarchy
visATC.description: Visualisation and subsetting of the World Health Organisation Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) classification system.
visATC.author: J Matthews [aut, cre, cph]

visual.kaito.title: Interactive 3D Visualizations for Group Comparisons
visual.kaito.description: Draws interactive, rotatable statistical visualizations in three dimensions, built on 'plotly'. Two families of plots are provided. Triaxial box plots (boxplot3d(), boxplot3d_interactive()) compare groups on three continuous variables at once, with Tukey, fixed-percentile, mean +/- SD, and letter-value box/whisker conventions, plus parametric and non-parametric significance testing (per-axis and joint 3D via MANOVA / PERMANOVA). Bivariate density plots (ttest_plot3d(), manova_plot3d()) compare two or more groups on two continuous variables as overlapping 3D density surfaces, reporting per-axis t-tests together with a joint Hotelling's T-squared test (two groups), or a one-way MANOVA omnibus test with Bonferroni, Tukey, Fisher's LSD, and Dunnett post-hoc comparisons (more than two groups). All plots include live, pre-computed controls (view, method, scale, transparency) so results can be explored interactively without re-running R code.
visual.kaito.author:
Armando González Sánchez [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-6182-1000>)

winn.title: White Noise Normalization for Mass Spectrometry Profiling Data
winn.description:
Provides a decision-guided workflow for correcting technical
variability in chemical profiling data. Tests for white noise identify
measured features that need correction while preserving those that
already pass. The workflow combines robust outlier adjustment, adaptive
drift detection, change-point segmentation, batch correction, and
probabilistic quotient normalization in a single pipeline or as modular
steps. It supports parameter tuning using pooled quality-control samples
as well as operation for studies without pooled controls.
winn.author: Tanmay Tanna [aut, cre, cph]

wishartinference.title: Bayesian Inference for the Wishart Distribution Parameters
wishartinference.description:
Posterior inference for the shape parameter alpha and mean
matrix mu in the model X_i ~ Wishart_p(2*alpha, Sigma), under both
an improper prior and a proper Gamma/inverse-Wishart prior. The
posterior mode is found via a Newton-within-EM algorithm and joint
samples are drawn via rejection sampling.
wishartinference.author:
Philip Everson [aut],
Hanqi Shi [aut, cre]

winning.title: Contest Win Probabilities and Ability Calibration
winning.description:
Solves the horse race problem in both directions. Infers
relative ability from win probabilities (or betting dividends) for
contests whose entrants share a common performance distribution,
with dead heats handled exactly, by the lattice fixed-point
algorithm of Cotton (2021) <doi:10.1137/19M1276261>. Also computes
all N win probabilities of a factor-structured Gaussian race
(multinomial probit with low-rank-plus-diagonal covariance) in one
shared-lattice pass of O(Q*N*L) operations, and inverts observed
shares to abilities by a damped Newton method with analytic slopes.
A dependency-free base-R port of the reference python package
'winning'. Performances are times: lowest wins.
winning.author: Peter Cotton [aut, cre]

wowi.title: Detect Spatial Clusters of High Rates of Acute Malnutrition
wowi.description:
Utilities for detecting statistically significant
spatial clusters of high acute malnutrition rates using a Bernoulli
spatial scan statistic, implemented via the 'SaTScan' software
<https://www.satscan.org/>.
wowi.author:
Tomás Zaba [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-7079-3574>)

xaci.title: Actuarial Climate Index
xaci.description:
Computes the Actuarial Climate Index (ACI) and its components
(temperature, precipitation, drought, wind, sea level) from gridded climate
data ('NetCDF') and tide gauge records. Implements the methodology described
in Garrido, Milhaud & Olympio (2025) <https://hal.science/hal-04491982v2>
for a French/European actuarial climate index, building on the American
Academy of Actuaries framework, to any country in the world.
xaci.author:
Xavier Milhaud [aut, cre, ctb],
Dabakh Kane [ctb],
Esteban Mauboussin [ctb]

xaiHydro.title: Explainable AI Tools for Hydro-Climate Modelling
xaiHydro.description:
Provides a unified workflow for applying Explainable Artificial
Intelligence (XAI) methods to hydro-climate predictive models. Functions
implement a permutation-based Monte Carlo SHAP estimator (Strumbelj and
Kononenko (2014) <doi:10.1007/s10115-013-0679-x>; Lundberg and Lee (2017)
<doi:10.48550/arXiv.1705.07874>), a self-contained locally weighted linear
surrogate LIME (Ribeiro et al. (2016) <doi:10.1145/2939672.2939778>),
and Partial Dependence Plots with Accumulated Local Effects (Friedman (2001)
<doi:10.1214/aos/1013203451>; Apley and Zhu (2020)
<doi:10.1111/rssb.12377>) with hydrology-specific visualisations and
interpretation utilities. Supports any model object compatible with the
'DALEX' explainer interface (Biecek (2018)
<doi:10.18637/jss.v097.i01>), including random forests, gradient
boosting, and neural networks trained on streamflow, drought indices,
flood risk, or evapotranspiration data. Hydrology-standard performance
metrics Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency (NSE, Nash and Sutcliffe (1970)
<doi:10.1016/0022-1694(70)90255-6>) and Kling-Gupta Efficiency (KGE,
Gupta et al. (2009) <doi:10.1016/j.jhydrol.2009.08.003>) are
computed alongside standard regression metrics. Designed to accompany
the book chapter: Islam, S., Dheeraj, A., Ali, S., Kaushal, R. and
Venkatesh, G. (2026). Explainable Artificial Intelligence for
Hydro-Climatic Modelling: Methods, Applications, and Implementation
Using the xaiHydro R Package. In Chandniha, S. K. et al. (Eds.),
Hydro-Climate Analytics: Remote Sensing, AI and Geospatial Modelling.
Springer.
xaiHydro.author:
Sadikul Islam [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-2924-7122>),
Shakir Ali [aut],
Rajesh Kaushal [aut]

xmlrectr.title: Rectangle Arbitrary 'XML' into Analysis-Friendly Tables
xmlrectr.description:
Converts arbitrary 'XML' into canonical node tables and analysis-friendly
rectangular outputs without requiring a vocabulary-specific parser. Supports
conservative structure proposals, explicit reusable profiles, advisory 'XSD'
inspection, bounded streaming, 'CSV' and 'Parquet' output, an analyst-oriented
single-table projection, and record-level parallel execution with automatic
scheduling. The native implementation uses 'libxml2' for structural acceleration
while the 'R' implementation remains the semantic reference.
xmlrectr.author: Lorenzo Isella [aut, cre]

xnicher.title: Estimates Ecological Niche Models Using Ellipses
xnicher.description:
Ecological niche model estimation using ellipsoidal geometry
under an M hypothesis.  Fits nine likelihood families
(presence-only, weighted, inverse-probability-weighted, skew-normal,
skew-normal-weighted, skew-t, skew-t-weighted, ncst, and
ncst-weighted) via multi-start optimisation with Sobol sequences.
Methods for the optimisation of ellipses parameters are as described
in Jimenez et al. (2022) <doi:10.1016/j.ecolmodel.2021.109823>.
xnicher.author:
Angel Robles [aut, cre],
Laura Jimenez [aut, ctb] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-4674-4270>)

xplus.title:
Positive and Unlabeled Learning from Unbalanced Cases and Sparse
Structures
xplus.description:
Provides PLUS-derived extensions for positive and unlabeled (PU)
learning from unbalanced cases and sparse structures, based on Zhou et al.
(2022) <doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009956>. Iteratively relabels unlabeled
observations via penalised logistic regression and pseudo-label updates,
then refits a final sparse model.
Includes weighted bootstrap sampling, convergence diagnostics, prediction,
coefficient extraction, and assessment utilities.
xplus.author:
Angel Robles [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-4674-4270>)

xplaineff.title: Decomposing Global Feature Effects Based on Feature Interactions
xplaineff.description:
Implements the GADGET (Generalized Additive Decomposition of Global
EffecTs) algorithm for interpretable machine learning. The package
recursively partitions the feature space to minimize heterogeneity of
feature effects (e.g., Accumulated Local Effects or Partial Dependence),
producing a tree of regions where effects are more stable. It supports
both ALE and PD strategies, works with 'mlr3' learners and provides visualization of the interaction
tree and regional effect plots. The method is described in Herbinger, J.,
Wright, M. N., Nagler, T., Bischl, B., and Casalicchio, G. (2024),
"Decomposing Global Feature Effects Based on Feature Interactions"
<https://jmlr.org/papers/volume25/23-0699/23-0699.pdf>.
xplaineff.author:
Zizheng Zhang [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0009-4252-8018>),
Coco Bögel [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0009-0002-0683-4957>),
Giuseppe Casalicchio [aut] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-5324-5966>),
Bernd Bischl [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0001-6002-6980>)

xtifedml.title:
Double Machine Learning for Static Panel Models with Interactive
Fixed Effects
xtifedml.description: Implements partially linear panel regression (PLPR) models with interactive fixed effects, high-dimensional confounding variables, and an exogenous treatment variable within the double machine learning framework. Estimates the structural parameter (treatment effect) in static panel data models with interactive fixed effects using the approach established in Chen et al. (2026) <doi:10.48550/arXiv.2608.01137>. Builds on the object-oriented package 'DoubleML' (Bach et al., 2024) <doi:10.18637/jss.v108.i03> and 'xtdml' (Polselli, 2025) <doi:10.48550/arXiv.2512.15965>, using the 'mlr3' ecosystem.
xtifedml.author:
Binzhi Chen [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-5094-7740>),
Annalivia Polselli [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0002-7579-7926>)

zot.title: Access 'Zotero' Libraries
zot.description:
Interface to the 'Zotero' reference manager <https://www.zotero.org>
through its public web API and local client database. Provides paginated
reads, versioned writes, read-only local queries, batch plans and resumable
ledgers, bibliographic comparison, metadata mapping, file attachment, and
optional semantic-index queries.
zot.author:
Alejandro Verri Kozlowski [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-8535-1170>)

ASmiR.title: Prediction of Abiotic Stress-Specific miRNAs in Plants
ASmiR.description:
Provides functions for predicting plant microRNAs (miRNAs)
associated with cold, drought, heat, and salt stress using the ASmiR
machine learning framework. Implements PseKNC feature generation and
stress-specific support vector machine models described by Pradhan et
al. (2023), "ASmiR: a machine learning framework for prediction of
abiotic stress-specific miRNAs in plants", Functional & Integrative
Genomics, 23(2), article 92, <doi:10.1007/s10142-023-01014-2>.
ASmiR.author:
Upendra Kumar Pradhan [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-8768-879X>),
Prabina Kumar Meher [aut]

AURMC.title: Area Under the Repeated Measures Curve
AURMC.description:
Estimates and compares areas under curves formed by repeatedly
measured outcomes observed subject to censoring and a terminal event.
Implements Kaplan-Meier adjustment for censoring, influence-function
standard errors, Wald inference, and multiplier perturbation inference,
with utilities for interpolation, simulation, tabulation, and plotting.
For additional details, see: McCaw ZR, Armbruster S, Tian L, Claggett BL,
Fitzmaurice G, Foà A, Pfeffer MA, Wei LJ (2026)
<doi:10.1016/j.jchf.2026.103013>.
AURMC.author:
Zachary McCaw [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-2006-9828>)

AccumulatR.title: Simulation and Likelihood Tools for Evidence-Accumulation Models
AccumulatR.description:
Toolbox for designing, simulating and fitting custom racing evidence-accumulation
models to behavioral data. Users define a model in terms of accumulators, pooled
channels, logical response rules, and timing dependencies. This allows more direct
embedding of psychological hypotheses into the model. With that model you can
simulate decision-making data and evaluate the likelihood of observed responses
under alternative parameter values. The user-facing interface stays in R, while the
simulation and likelihood calculations are handled in C++ for speed.
AccumulatR.author: Niek Stevenson [aut, cre]

AdaptiveGlasso.title: Adaptive Graphical Lasso for Sparse Network Estimation
AdaptiveGlasso.description:
Implements an adaptive graphical lasso method for sparse
precision matrix and network estimation. The method combines ridge
stabilization, cross-validated regularization, an initial graphical
lasso estimate, and adaptive edge-specific penalties to estimate
sparse conditional dependence structures. The method supports
settings where the sample size is smaller than, equal to, or larger
than the number of variables.
AdaptiveGlasso.author:
Elizabeth B. Amona [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-7575-788X>)

AgroMetIndices.title:
Agrometeorological Indices for Daily, Monthly, and Seasonal Time
Scales
AgroMetIndices.description:
Provides methods for calculating agrometeorological indices from
daily weather data at daily, monthly, and user-defined seasonal time
scales. The package includes temperature, rainfall, growing degree days,
heat and cold stress, wet and dry spells, extreme rainfall, and seasonal
completeness indices, along with functions for meteorological data quality
assessment and crop-season definition. For method details see
<doi:10.1002/wcc.147> and <doi:10.1038/s41598-026-55293-3>.
AgroMetIndices.author:
RN Singh [aut],
Sonam Sah [aut, cre],
Santosha Rathod [aut],
Prabhat Kumar [aut],
Sudhir Kumar Mishra [aut],
Gaurav Chaturvedi [aut]

AlphaSDM.title: Species Distribution Models on 'AlphaEarth' Satellite Embeddings
AlphaSDM.description:
Fits species distribution models and maps habitat suitability
at up to 10 m resolution from occurrence records alone, using the
'AlphaEarth' Foundations satellite embeddings (Brown et al. 2025)
<doi:10.48550/arXiv.2507.22291>. The embeddings, 64 values per pixel per
year from a geospatial foundation model, replace environmental layers, so
none need to be sourced or aligned. Provides tools to format occurrence
records, place pseudo-absences, train and evaluate an ensemble of machine
learning models, and export habitat-suitability rasters. Sampling, model
training and prediction all run on 'Google Earth Engine', which requires a
free account for noncommercial use.
AlphaSDM.author: James Longo [aut, cre, cph]

ApproxOp.title: A Unified Framework for Positive Linear Approximation Operators
ApproxOp.description:
Provides a unified computational framework for defining,
evaluating, analyzing, comparing, and visualizing positive linear
approximation operators. The package supports classical and generalized
discrete operators, ordinary and central moments, numerical moment
verification, approximation error analysis, convergence studies,
parameter studies, and user-defined operators. The implemented framework
is related to classical and generalized approximation operators described
in Szász (1950) <doi:10.6028/JRES.045.024>, Sucu and Varma (2015)
<doi:10.1016/j.amc.2015.08.077>, and Aliaga and Aslan (2026)
<doi:10.1002/mma.70924>.
ApproxOp.author: Edmond Aliaga [aut, cre]

Applr.title: Visualize and Explain Linear Models
Applr.description:
Tools for visualizing and explaining linear models fit with lm().
Draws 2D slices of higher-dimensional models in base graphics and as a
'ggplot2' layer, offers an interactive 'plotly' 3D scatter with a fitted
surface for two-predictor models, and renders model equations as plain
text or 'LaTeX'.
Applr.author:
Cameron McClellan [aut],
James Beeson [aut, cre],
Garrett Saunders [ths]

BBMBC.title:
Beta-Binomial Models for Immune Cell Frequencies and Power
Calculations
BBMBC.description:
Provides tools to model overdispersed immune cell frequencies using Beta-Binomial generalized linear models.
Originally designed for memory B cells, the framework generalizes to evaluate rare
cellular immune responses across vaccinology, immuno-oncology, and related fields. Includes
method-of-moments dispersion estimation, likelihood ratio testing
across experimental arms, and Monte Carlo simulation to
calculate statistical power and Type I error rates. The methodologies
are directly motivated by the analysis of immunology data in
"Vaccination with mRNA-encoded membrane-anchored HIV envelope trimers
elicited tier 2 neutralizing antibodies in a phase 1 clinical trial"
(Parks et al. 2025) <doi:10.1126/scitranslmed.ady6831>.
BBMBC.author: Andrew Shin [aut, cre]

BDIB.title:
Bayesian Dynamic Information Borrowing for Longitudinal Data
with Informative Dropout
BDIB.description:
Implements 'BDIB' (Bayesian dynamic information borrowing) for
longitudinal outcomes with informative dropout. The package provides the
mixture prior for longitudinal data borrowing (MLB) and the self-adapting mixture
prior for longitudinal data information borrowing (SLB). Both methods use a
shared-parameter model for outcomes and dropout.
BDIB.author: Saijun Zhao [aut, cre]

BMeRL.title: Bivariate Median Residual Life Estimation
BMeRL.description:
Nonparametric estimation of the bivariate median residual life
function of Kayid et al. (2020) for complete and right-censored paired
lifetimes. Order-restricted estimation for two groups is also provided, following
Khan and Ghebremichael (2026). For censored data the bivariate survival function is estimated by the
method of Lin and Ying (1993). Simultaneous confidence intervals are
obtained by the percentile bootstrap approach of Mandel and Betensky
(2008), and the estimated functions can be drawn as surface plots. See
the accompanying vignette 'BMeRL' for a detailed introduction.
Kayid, M., Shafaei Noughabi, M., and Abouammoh, A. M. (2020)
<doi:10.1007/s00357-018-9300-z>; Khan, R. A., and Ghebremichael, M.
(2026) <doi:10.1002/bimj.70112>; Lin, D. Y., and Ying, Z. (1993)
<doi:10.1093/biomet/80.3.573>; Mandel, M., and Betensky, R. A. (2008)
<doi:10.1016/j.csda.2007.07.005>.
BMeRL.author:
Ruhul Ali Khan [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-1173-8345>),
Musie Ghebremichael [aut] (Project PI)

BayesAiken.title:
Bayesian Content Validity Coefficients with Credibility
Intervals
BayesAiken.description:
Bayesian inference for the six rating coefficients proposed by
Aiken (1985) <doi:10.1177/0013164485451012> and Aiken (1989)
<doi:10.1177/0013164489492003>: V (content validity), H (homogeneity),
C (congruence), R (repeatability), A (rater agreement) and I (item
coherence). All six are expressed as functionals of the population
distribution of rating categories, so a single Dirichlet-Multinomial model
yields their full posterior by push-forward. This treats each judge as one
categorical observation and avoids the pseudo-replication of Beta-Binomial
formulations. R is modelled on the c-by-c joint table because it is not a
functional of the marginal distribution. Provides classical estimates with
the correct parity correction, highest density and equal-tailed
credibility intervals, posterior threshold probabilities, prior
sensitivity analysis and a friendly step-by-step verbose report.
BayesAiken.author:
Jose Ventura-Leon [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-2996-4244>)

BayesRE.title: Bayesian Multiple Linear Regression Estimation for Crop Yield
BayesRE.description:
Implements Bayesian multiple linear regression models for estimating
crop yield response to climatic variables. Posterior predictions and regional
sensitivity coefficients are returned and can be visualised with built-in
plotting utilities. Methods are based on Stan (Carpenter et al. (2017)
<doi:10.18637/jss.v076.i01>) and Bayesian workflow described in Gelman et al.
(2013, ISBN:9781439840955).
BayesRE.author:
Prakash Kumar [aut, cre],
Himadri Sekhar Roy [aut],
Ranjit Kumar Paul [aut],
Md. Yeasin [aut],
Neeraj Budhlakoti [aut],
Sunil Kumar Yadav [aut],
Amrit Kumar Paul [aut]

BiGaRx.title: Unified Classical and Canonical Biplots
BiGaRx.description:
Classical and canonical biplots computed from a single singular
value decomposition (SVD) engine. Includes the two biplots of Gabriel
(1971) <doi:10.1093/biomet/58.3.453>: the GH-biplot, named after its row
markers G and column markers H, which preserves the column metric
(covariances and correlations between variables), and the JK-biplot, named
after its row markers J and column markers K, which preserves the row
metric (distances between individuals). Also includes the HJ-biplot of
Galindo (1986)
<https://upcommons.upc.edu/entities/publication/e17797dd-e20b-4fe5-b34a-f4cde41695ed>,
which combines the row markers J and the column markers H so that rows
and columns are both represented with maximum quality. Options include
configurable preprocessing, supplementary rows and columns, quality of
representation, contributions, goodness of fit, bootstrap confidence
intervals following Nieto, Galindo, Leiva and Vicente-Galindo (2014)
<doi:10.15446/rce.v37n2spe.47944>, and imputation of missing values by
iterative low-rank approximation following Gabriel and Zamir (1979)
<doi:10.1080/00401706.1979.10489819>. The canonical biplot, also known as
the multivariate analysis of variance (MANOVA) biplot, follows Amaro,
Vicente-Villardon and Galindo (2004)
<https://www.redalyc.org/pdf/339/33908807.pdf>. It is available for one-way
designs and for two-way designs with total, row, column and interaction
biplots. It comes with multivariate tests, pairwise comparisons with
Hotelling's T-squared statistic, log-ratio transformations for
compositional data and confidence regions for the group means. The
regions are circles or the ellipses of Krzanowski (1989)
<doi:10.1093/biomet/76.1.107>, computed consistently in the scale of the
within-groups covariance matrix. Plots use base graphics or 'ggplot2'.
BiGaRx.author:
Kleber Garzón [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0009-4378-3002>),
Roxana Barrezueta [aut] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0007-1591-1121>)

BiasedMatch.title: Biased Matching for Two-Urn Sampling Problems
BiasedMatch.description:
Tools for the two-urn biased sampling problems of Puza and
Bonfrer (2018) <doi:10.1080/03610926.2017.1300282>. Two overlapping sets
of items are sampled without replacement, with items common to both sets
given a selection weight favouring their inclusion. The package computes
the probability mass function, mean and variance of the number of matching
items using the univariate and bivariate Wallenius' non-central
hypergeometric distributions, performs maximum likelihood and Bayesian
inference for the bias parameter, and provides Metropolis-Hastings
algorithms for hierarchical extensions.
BiasedMatch.author:
Andre Bonfrer [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-3061-7103>),
Borek Puza [aut]

BioFTF.title: Biodiversity Assessment Using Hill-Number Functional Tools
BioFTF.description:
Tools for biodiversity assessment through Hill-number diversity
profiles treated as functions of the order q. The package computes the
profiles of Hill (1973) <doi:10.2307/1934352>, their analytical first and
second derivatives, curvature, radius of curvature, arc length, cumulative
integral functions, profile areas, area-based rankings and relative changes
over time, together with static and interactive three-dimensional
biodiversity surfaces. The functional approach follows Di Battista, Fortuna
and Maturo (2017) <doi:10.1016/j.ecolind.2016.10.032>, Maturo and
Di Battista (2018) <doi:10.1016/j.ecolind.2017.08.016> and Maturo (2018)
<doi:10.1016/j.ecolind.2018.03.013>.
BioFTF.author:
Fabrizio Maturo [aut, cre],
Francesca Fortuna [aut],
Tonio Di Battista [aut]

BoxDensityPlot.title: Multi-Trait Density and Boxplot Visualization
BoxDensityPlot.description:
Reads wide-format phenotypic data (one row per genotype or
sample, one column per trait) from CSV or 'Excel' files, reshapes it to
long format, and produces faceted figures that combine a mirrored
density curve with a boxplot for each trait. Density curves can be
drawn on the left, right, or both sides of the box, and figures can be
saved automatically at publication resolution.
BoxDensityPlot.author:
Prakash Kumar [aut, cre],
Himadri Sekhar Roy [aut],
Ranjit Kumar Paul [aut],
Md. Yeasin [aut],
Paritosh Kumar ICAR-NIASM [aut],
Amrit Kumar Paul [aut]

BreedReliabR.title:
Decision Reliability for Genotype Advancement under Prediction
and Target Environment Uncertainty
BreedReliabR.description:
A model-agnostic research layer for genotype advancement decisions
from externally fitted genomic prediction models. It propagates full joint
coefficient prediction-error covariance together with finite sampling from
a specified target population of environments to calculate conditional
advancement probabilities, expected selected-set reliability, and the
relative contributions of prediction and target-environment uncertainty.
It also compares uncertainty formulations and reports geometric support
diagnostics. Probabilities are conditional on supplied inputs and are not
guaranteed to be calibrated in new populations or environments.
BreedReliabR.author:
Ashutosh Sawarkar [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1016-8822>),
Santosh Patil [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-5370-3522>)

BvCh.title:
Bivariate Chen Distribution: Density, Survival, Hazard, Plots
and Estimates
BvCh.description:
Probability density, survival and hazard functions, random
generation, graphical displays and maximum likelihood estimation for
bivariate Chen type models. Three constructions are covered: the
Bivariate Chen distribution with a singular component
on the diagonal, the Bivariate Extended Chen distribution, and the
Bivariate Inverse copula Chen distribution obtained through an inverse
copula with Chen marginals. Univariate Chen density, distribution,
quantile, survival, hazard and random generation routines are obtained
from the 'reliaR' package.
BvCh.author:
Mukul Bijalwan [aut] (ORCID iD: https://orcid.org/0009-0001-3040-6912),
Puneet Kumar Gupta [aut, cre] (ORCID iD:
https://orcid.org/0000-0002-3458-5655)

CAs.title: Creating Covering Arrays
CAs.description:
Implements covering arrays, as proposed in
Groemping (2025) <doi:10.1109/ICSTW64639.2025.10962463>.
Uniform and mixed-level covering arrays are created and
can be assessed for their coverage properties.
The mathematical background of the constructions is provided
in the technical reports Groemping (2026)
<https://www1.bht-berlin.de/FB_II/reports/Report-2026-001.pdf>
for the uniform arrays and Groemping (2025)
<https://www1.bht-berlin.de/FB_II/reports/Report-2025-001.pdf>
for the mixed-level constructions. The post-processing method
by Nayeri, Colbourn, and Konjevod (2013)
<doi:10.1016/j.ejc.2012.07.017> is also
provided. In addition, there are preliminary tools for the
creation of sequence covering arrays.
CAs.author: Ulrike Groemping [aut, cre]

CORAtool.title: Combinational Regularity Analysis
CORAtool.description:
Searches configurational data for causes that are each an
insufficient but non-redundant part of an unnecessary but sufficient
(INUS) condition for their effect, so that cause-effect relations are
marked by conjunctivity and disjunctivity. The method, Combinational
Regularity Analysis (CORA), borrows its Boolean minimisation algorithms
from switching circuit analysis. Truth tables are minimised either with the
classical Quine-McCluskey algorithm over positive and don't care terms or
with McCluskey's modified algorithm over positive and negative terms, and
the resulting prime implicant charts are solved with Petrick's method.
Multi-value conditions and structures with simple as well as complex
effects are supported, together with a configurational data-mining search
and two-level logic diagrams. The package is an R port of the 'Python'
packages 'CORA' and 'LOGIGRAM' described in Sebechlebská, Mkrtchyan
and Thiem (2023) <doi:10.21105/joss.05019>; it computes in
plain R and requires no 'Python' installation. It is an independent
implementation and is not endorsed by the authors of the original
packages.
CORAtool.author:
Young Chan [aut, cre, cph] (Author of the R implementation),
Zuzana Sebechlebská [cph] (Copyright holder of the original Python
implementation),
Lusine Mkrtchyan [cph] (Copyright holder of the original Python
implementation),
Alrik Thiem [cph] (Copyright holder of the original Python
implementation)

CUNYsports.title:
Accessible Collegiate Athletics Data from the City University of
New York (CUNY)
CUNYsports.description:
Provides access to collegiate athletics data from the City University
of New York (CUNY), the largest urban public university system in the United
States. Includes tools for discovering and retrieving sports data from an
included SQLite database. The data covers individual CUNY schools, players,
games, seasons, and other aspects of CUNY athletics, providing accessible datasets for
teaching, student learning, and sports analytics.
CUNYsports.author:
Christian Martinez [aut, cre] (GitHub: martinezc1, ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0005-6026-6454>)

ClimateAnomaly.title: Rainfall and Temperature Anomaly Indices for Climate Analysis
ClimateAnomaly.description:
Computes rainfall anomaly indices and a standardised temperature
anomaly from monthly or annual precipitation and temperature data supplied
by the user. The rainfall indices are the Rainfall Anomaly Index (RAI; Van
Rooy, 1965), the Modified Rainfall Anomaly Index (MRAI) and the Standardized
Rainfall Anomaly Index (SRAI) of Ekpetere (2025)
<doi:10.1016/j.jenvman.2025.124160>, the Simplified Standardized
Precipitation Index (SSPI) of Raziei (2021)
<doi:10.1016/j.jhydrol.2021.126761>, and the Standardized Precipitation
Index (SPI; McKee et al., 1993). The temperature anomaly is a z-score
computed within each calendar month. All indices are computed group-wise,
so the user can stratify by any combination of spatial units (state,
district, grid cell) and calendar month, and each value can be classified
into a descriptive severity class.
ClimateAnomaly.author:
Md Yeasin [aut],
Ranjit Kumar Paul [aut, cre],
Pushkar Bora [aut]

ConvergeR.title: Whitfield Convergence Score and Seurat Metadata Association
ConvergeR.description:
Calculates the convergence score defined by Whitfield et al. 2026
<doi:10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-25-4403>. It allows visualization of this score
alongside qualitative and quantitative Seurat object metadata via barplots
and density curves, and runs appropriate statistical tests for associations.
ConvergeR.author:
Paul de Boissier [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-2246-1580>)

CoopPostman.title: Optimal Routing and Cost Allocation for the Chinese Postman Game
CoopPostman.description:
Solves the Chinese Postman Problem (CPP) using Dijkstra's algorithm
for shortest paths, Edmonds' Blossom algorithm (1965) for minimum weight
perfect matching, and Fleury's algorithm for Eulerian circuit generation.
Additionally, computes the cooperative gamma-rule cost allocation proposed
by Hamers, Klijn, Suijs, and Tijs (1999) <doi
:10.1016/S0377-2217(98)00346-6>
for weakly Eulerian networks.
CoopPostman.author: Maria Gabriela Perez [aut, cre]

CoxRMSTSimpson.title: Restricted Mean Survival Time from Cox Models
CoxRMSTSimpson.description:
Calculates restricted mean survival time from predicted Cox
proportional hazards survival curves using composite Simpson's rule
and provides plots with shaded areas under the survival curves.
Includes simulated survival data for reproducible examples.
CoxRMSTSimpson.author: Ian Forde [aut, cre]

DetectOutlier.title: Detect Outliers in Data Frames and Export Results
DetectOutlier.description:
Identifies potential outliers in numeric columns of a data frame
using the interquartile range (IQR), defined as the difference between
the third and first quartiles. Values below the first quartile minus
1.5 times the IQR or above the third quartile plus 1.5 times the IQR are
flagged as potential outliers. The package can export rows containing
outliers to comma-separated values (CSV) files and create 'Excel'
workbooks with outlier values highlighted and a summary of outlier counts.
DetectOutlier.author:
Prakash Kumar [aut, cre],
Himadri Sekhar Roy [aut],
Ranjit Kumar Paul [aut],
Md. Yeasin [aut],
Paritosh Kumar ICAR-NIASM [aut],
Amrit Kumar Paul [aut]

DiagnostySize.title: App for Calculating the Sample Size in a Diagnostic Study
DiagnostySize.description: We developed a 'shiny' app for the optimal sample size calculations for diagnostic accuracy studies proposed in Stark and Zapf (2020) <doi:10.1177/0962280220913588>, and Stark et al. (2022) <doi:10.1186/s12874-022-01564-2>, so people without programming skills can use this approach as well. Until now, this approach was just available via 'R' scripts. This app, 'DiagnostySize', lets users apply the optimal sample size calculation approach, ensuring that no endpoint (sensitivity or specificity) is overpowered. Within the app, users can run the optimal sample size and power calculations for different study designs through a user interface.
DiagnostySize.author:
Jana Wiesner [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0001-7031-7850>),
Maria Stark [ctb] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1463-0885>)

DistLagHet.title: Treatment Effect Estimation in Complex Designs
DistLagHet.description:
Implements estimation methods for treatment effects in complex
designs under parallel-trends assumptions. Based on the methodology of
de Chaisemartin and D'Haultfoeuille (2025)
<doi:10.48550/arXiv.2508.07808>.
Provides three model specifications: base model with K lags, full dynamics
model using all available periods, and interactions model with lag interaction
terms. Includes C++ optimizations for faster bootstrap estimation.
DistLagHet.author:
Clement de Chaisemartin [aut],
Xavier D'Haultfoeuille [aut],
Henri Fabre [cre, ctb]

DistributionalDDA.title: Distributional Data Analysis in Bayes Spaces
DistributionalDDA.description:
Statistical analysis of data sets whose observations are whole
probability distributions, using Bayes space calculus. Distributions
(provided as samples, histograms or density functions) are treated as
elements of a Hilbert space, so that operations such as mean, variance,
distance, principal component analysis and clustering carry over to
densities. Reference measures defining the geometry of the space can be
chosen and combined. The methodology was first published with peer review by
van den Boogaart, Egozcue and Pawlowsky-Glahn (2014) <doi:10.1111/anzs.12074>.
DistributionalDDA.author:
Ivana Pavlu [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0001-9322-246X>),
Raimon Tolosana-Delgado [aut] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-9847-0462>),
Matthias Templ [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-8638-5276>),
K. Gerald van den Boogaart [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-4646-943X>)

DoExp.title: Design of Experiments with Hasse Diagrams and Anatomy Tables
DoExp.description:
Constructs Hasse diagrams and anatomy tables from structural
formulas and experimental data sets. Hasse diagrams may display sources
of variation and their degrees of freedom for general experimental
structures. For orthogonal designs, the package can also compute core
matrices associated with quadratic forms for sums of squares and
contributions to the expected mean squares. Anatomy tables display the
degrees of freedom and A-efficiencies associated with the sources of
variation.
DoExp.author:
Leonardo Peressim [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-5378-6903>),
Renata Sermarini [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0001-6425-9626>)

DynMSR.title:
Connect Systems Biology and Pharmacology Formats to Simulation
Backends
DynMSR.description:
Provides a convenient R interface for systems-biology and
systems-pharmacology models in Heta, SBML (Systems Biology Markup
Language), and DynMS (Dynamic Model Specification) formats.
DynMS JSON files are loaded directly; Heta projects and SBML files
are converted to DynMS by an optional compatible installation of
'heta-compiler'. Models can be validated, selected from a platform, and
generated or built for simulation with 'mrgsolve' as a backend.
DynMSR.author: Evgeny Metelkin [aut, cre]

Dynet.title: Tidy Temporal Network Analysis
Dynet.description:
Building, analysis and visualisation of temporal networks.
Supports several formats of relational data: interval data with
explicit start and end times, contact data of instantaneous events,
threaded interactions such as forum or chat data, and co-presence
logs. Every analysis returns a tidy data frame carrying proper vertex
labels. Metrics cover time-varying centrality, graph-level structure,
edge formation and dissolution, burstiness, time-respecting paths,
reachability and mixing. Offers a wide variety of network
visualisations and animations, as well as plots of temporal network
metrics across time.
Dynet.author: Mohammed Saqr [aut, cre, cph]

EDI.title: Experimental Design and Inference
EDI.description:
Implements a comprehensive suite of experimental designs, both
fixed (e.g., block, stratified, matched-pair, cluster, factorial, and
mixed-integer-programming-based optimal designs) and sequential
(including matching-on-the-fly designs, biased coin designs, and
covariate-adaptive urn designs that assign treatment one
subject at a time while maintaining covariate balance), for
continuous, incidence, count, proportion, survival, and ordinal response
types. For each design and response type combination, provides the
corresponding inference procedures, including exact, asymptotic,
distribution-free, and resampling-based (bootstrap, jackknife, and
randomization) methods, so that estimation and testing are always
matched to how the data were generated. An 'InferenceSuite' facility
runs all applicable inference procedures for a given design and
response type at once and reports a single Cauchy-combined p-value
summarizing their evidence. A built-in simulation framework
supports power analysis and operating-characteristic studies across
designs, response types, and inference procedures, with optional
parallelization via 'mirai'. Missing covariate data is
handled automatically via built-in imputation. Core numerical routines
are implemented in C++ via 'Rcpp' for speed on large designs and
simulation studies. Machine-specific tuning for optimization is
included.
EDI.author:
Adam Kapelner [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-5985-6792>)

EMDSSAForecast.title:
Hybrid EMD-SSA Forecasting with Artificial Neural Networks for
Time Series
EMDSSAForecast.description:
Implements a hybrid empirical mode decomposition, singular
spectrum analysis, and artificial neural network forecasting
framework for time series data. The framework extracts the trend
from the first intrinsic mode function using singular spectrum
analysis, forecasts the extracted trend and remaining
decomposition components using artificial neural networks, and
combines the component forecasts to obtain the final forecast.
For methodological details, refer to Kumar et al. (2026)
<doi:10.1007/s10791-026-10076-2>.
EMDSSAForecast.author:
Prabhat Kumar [aut, cre],
Girish Kumar Jha [aut],
Rajeev Ranjan Kumar [aut],
Santosha Rathod [aut],
R N Singh [aut]

ERA5Flux.title:
Improve the Utility of ERA5-Land Data at AmeriFlux Site
Locations
ERA5Flux.description:
Collection of tools useful for workflows involving ERA5-Land and
AmeriFlux data. Includes functions for downloading ERA5-Land data based on
AmeriFlux sites, formatting the downloaded data to match AmeriFlux
standards, merging both datasets together to ensure consistent
timestamps, and blending them to create a single gap-filled time series.
For more details, visit the Climate Data Store's catalogue entry for ERA5-Land
at <https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/datasets/reanalysis-era5-land>
and the AmeriFlux homepage at <https://ameriflux.lbl.gov>.
ERA5Flux.author:
Angel Chen [aut, cre] (angelchen7.github.io),
Sam Jurado [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0009-0005-1902-4066>),
David E Reed [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-8892-1423>),
Ammara Talib [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0003-3259-0220>),
Junna Wang [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0003-3885-846X>),
Boya Zhang [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-6860-2054>),
Sparkle L Malone [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0001-9034-1076>),
National Science Foundation [fnd] (NSF 2047687),
Yale School of the Environment [fnd],
Yale Center for Natural Carbon Capture [fnd],
Malone Disturbance Ecology Lab [cph]

ET0RadModels.title: Evapotranspiration Estimation Using Radiation-Based Models
ET0RadModels.description:
Provides functions to estimate daily reference evapotranspiration
(ET0) using 10 radiation-based empirical models, with the Food and
Agriculture Organization (FAO) Penman-Monteith method included as the
standard reference for model comparison. Includes statistical evaluation
metrics, such as Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE), root mean square error
(RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), and mean bias error (MBE), and
visualization tools (scatter plots and Taylor diagrams). Based on
Singh et al. (2026) <doi:10.1016/j.ejrh.2026.103925>.
ET0RadModels.author:
Ajay N. Satpute [aut],
Samir Barman [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-8181-8346>),
Amit Kumar Singh [aut],
Avijit Ghosh [aut],
Gaurendra Gupta [aut]

ET0TempModels.title: Evapotranspiration Estimation Using Temperature-Based Models
ET0TempModels.description:
Provides functions to estimate daily reference evapotranspiration
(ET0) using 10 temperature-based empirical models, with the Food and
Agriculture Organization (FAO) Penman-Monteith method included as the
standard reference for model comparison. Includes statistical evaluation
metrics, such as Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE), root mean square error
(RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), and mean bias error (MBE), and
visualization tools (scatter plots and Taylor diagrams). Based on
Singh et al. (2026) <doi:10.1016/j.ejrh.2026.103925>.
ET0TempModels.author:
Ajay N. Satpute [aut],
Samir Barman [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-8181-8346>),
Amit Kumar Singh [aut],
Avijit Ghosh [aut],
Gaurendra Gupta [aut]

ET0MassModels.title: Evapotranspiration Estimation Using Mass Transfer-Based Models
ET0MassModels.description:
Provides functions to estimate daily reference evapotranspiration
(ET0) using 10 mass transfer-based empirical models, with the Food and
Agriculture Organization (FAO) Penman-Monteith method included as the
standard reference for model comparison. Includes statistical evaluation
metrics, such as Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE), root mean square error
(RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), and mean bias error (MBE), and
visualization tools (scatter plots and Taylor diagrams). Based on
Singh et al. (2026) <doi:10.1016/j.ejrh.2026.103925>.
ET0MassModels.author:
Ajay N. Satpute [aut],
Samir Barman [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-8181-8346>),
Amit Kumar Singh [aut],
Avijit Ghosh [aut],
Gaurendra Gupta [aut]

EZRShiny.title: Build Consistent 'shiny' App Layouts with Less Code
EZRShiny.description:
Short, consistent wrappers around 'shiny', 'bslib' and 'shinyjs'
for building multi-page 'shiny' apps. One function call builds the page
with a navigation bar, logo, title and dark mode switch. Tab functions nest
pages up to three levels deep, with optional sidebars. Input functions
create full-width inputs with optional information tooltips, and helpers
switch buttons on and off and show or hide tabs from the server. Includes
a starter app template and an example app that explores the Titanic
passenger data.
EZRShiny.author:
Daniella DeWeerd [aut, cre, cph],
Van Andel Institute [cph, fnd]

EmiStatR.title:
A Simplified and Scalable Urban Water Quality Model for
Simulation of Combined Sewer Overflows
EmiStatR.description: Provides a fast and parallelised calculator to estimate combined sewage water emissions. It supports the planning and design of urban drainage systems without extensive simulation tools. The methods are described in Torres-Matallana et al. (2018) <doi:10.3390/w10060782>.
EmiStatR.author:
J.A. Torres-Matallana [aut, cre],
K. Klepiszewski [aut],
U. Leopold [ctb],
G. Schutz [ctb],
G.B.M. Heuvelink [ctb]

EnvRtype.title: Envirotyping for Quantitative Genetics and Plant Breeding
EnvRtype.description:
An enviromics toolkit for genotype-by-environment analysis and
envirotype-informed genomic prediction. Collects worldwide daily and hourly
weather from 'NASA POWER', soil profiles from 'SoilGrids', elevation and
bioclimatic layers from 'WorldClim', agro-ecological zones from 'FAO GAEZ',
and downscaled 'CMIP6' climate scenarios, with checkpointed retrieval that
can resume after an interrupted run. Derives agro-meteorological parameters
(solar radiation, evapotranspiration, thermal time, atmospheric demand),
runs a FAO-56 single crop coefficient soil water balance, and maps daily
weather onto crop developmental stages. Builds environmental covariable
matrices, envirotype typologies and frequency matrices, mega-environment
clusters, historical risk profiles and target population of environments
weights. Reduces interval-resolved envirotypes by principal component
analysis, delineates soil zones with Gaussian mixture models, and constructs
linear, Gaussian and arc-cosine environmental relatedness kernels. Fits
Bayesian reaction-norm kernel models and predicts trained genotypes at
untested locations and planting dates, with coverage diagnostics, spatial
mapping and planting-window optimisation. Simulation functions generate
multi-environment trials and enviromes with known architecture for power
analysis. Methods are described in Costa-Neto, Galli, Carvalho, Crossa and
Fritsche-Neto (2021) <doi:10.1093/g3journal/jkab040>, and build on the
Bayesian genotype-by-environment kernel sampler of Granato, Cuevas,
Luna-Vazquez, Crossa, Montesinos-Lopez, Burgueno and Fritsche-Neto (2018)
<doi:10.1534/g3.118.200435>.
EnvRtype.author:
Germano Costa-Neto [aut, cre],
Fernanda Pontes [aut]

EventStudy.title: Event Study Analysis
EventStudy.description:
Financial event study analysis. Implements the classical event
study methodology of MacKinlay (1997) <https://www.jstor.org/stable/2729691>
with multiple return models: market model, market adjusted, comparison
period mean adjusted, Fama and French three-factor (1993)
<doi:10.1016/0304-405X(93)90023-5> and five-factor (2015)
<doi:10.1016/j.jfineco.2014.10.010>, Carhart (1997) four-factor
<doi:10.1111/j.1540-6261.1997.tb03808.x>, generalized autoregressive
conditional heteroskedasticity (GARCH; Bollerslev, 1986)
<doi:10.1016/0304-4076(86)90063-1>, rolling window, and dynamic conditional
correlation GARCH (DCC-GARCH; Engle, 2002) <doi:10.1198/073500102288618487>.
Provides parametric and non-parametric test statistics, including the
standardized cross-sectional test of Boehmer, Musumeci and Poulsen (1991)
<doi:10.1016/0304-405X(91)90032-F> and its cross-correlation adjustment by
Kolari and Pynnonen (2010) <doi:10.1093/rfs/hhq072>; buy-and-hold abnormal
returns (Barber and Lyon, 1997) <doi:10.1016/S0304-405X(96)00890-2>;
volume and volatility event studies; cross-sectional regression; intraday
event studies; panel difference-in-differences event studies with the
estimators of Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021)
<doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2020.12.001>, de Chaisemartin and D'Haultfoeuille
(2020) <doi:10.1257/aer.20181169>, and Borusyak, Jaravel and Spiess (2024)
<doi:10.1093/restud/rdae007>; synthetic control methods (Abadie, Diamond
and Hainmueller, 2010) <doi:10.1198/jasa.2009.ap08746>; wild bootstrap
inference; multiple testing corrections; power analysis via simulation;
data download helpers; automated reporting; and visualization tools.
Results can be exported to comma-separated values (CSV), 'Excel', or
'LaTeX'.
EventStudy.author: Simon Mueller [cre, aut]

FrailtyPackPlus.title: Shared, Correlated, Additive, and Zero-Inflated Frailty Models
FrailtyPackPlus.description:
Fits and compares shared, correlated, additive, zero-inflated promotion
cure-rate, and k-out-of-M one-shot device frailty survival models under Bayesian
Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) and Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) frameworks.
Supports ten baseline hazard distributions (Weibull, Exponential, Generalized
Exponential, Exponential Power, Linear Failure Rate, Generalized Log-Logistic,
Generalized Weibull, Generalized Rayleigh, Weighted Exponential, Extended Weibull)
and eight frailty distributions (Gamma, Inverse Gaussian, Positive Stable,
Compound Poisson, Compound Negative Binomial, Generalized Lindley, Weighted Lindley,
Mixture of Inverse Gaussians). Implements reversed hazard rate (RHR) models for
bivariate left-censored survival data, additive shared frailty models under
random right censoring, and one-shot device reliability analysis. Provides
goodness-of-fit testing, information criteria (AIC, BIC, AICc, HQIC, DIC, EAIC,
EBIC, LPML), convergence diagnostics (Geweke, Gelman-Rubin, Heidelberger-Welch),
Bayes factors, residual analyses, and diagnostic visualizations. Methodologies are
based on Hanagal and Dabade (2013) <doi:10.1016/j.spl.2013.07.015>, Hanagal and
Dabade (2013) <doi:10.1080/03610918.2012.661909>, Hanagal and Dabade (2015)
<doi:10.1080/03610926.2013.804561>, Hanagal and Bhambure (2015)
<doi:10.3233/MAS-140308>, Hanagal and Bhambure (2016)
<doi:10.1080/03610926.2014.901380>, Hanagal, Pandey, and Ganguly (2017)
<doi:10.1080/03610918.2015.1085559>, Hanagal and Pandey (2018)
<doi:10.1080/03610926.2018.1549256>, Hanagal (2020)
<doi:10.1080/03610926.2020.1736305>, Tyagi et al. (2021)
<doi:10.1007/s40314-021-01666-5>, Pandey, Hanagal, Tyagi, and Gupta (2021)
<doi:10.1142/S0218539321500406>, Tyagi, Pandey, and Chesneau (2022)
<doi:10.1007/s42519-021-00241-9>, Pandey, Hanagal, and Tyagi (2022)
<doi:10.2478/stattrans-2022-0048>, Tyagi, Pandey, and Chesneau (2022)
<doi:10.1007/s13571-022-00278-1>, Tyagi, Pandey, Hanagal, and Chesneau (2024)
<doi:10.1080/03610918.2024.2391874>, Kiprotich et al. (2025)
<doi:10.1080/02664763.2025.2560510>, Assuncao et al. (2026)
<doi:10.1002/bimj.70162>, Chen et al. (1999) <doi:10.1080/01621459.1999.10474198>,
Dunn and Smyth (1996) <doi:10.1080/10618600.1996.10474708>, Ling et al. (2021)
<doi:10.3390/math9233032>, Yu, So, and Balakrishnan (2025)
<doi:10.1016/B978-0-44-331694-4.00006-2>, Balakrishnan, Ling, and So (2021,
ISBN:978-1-119-77795-3), and McGilchrist and Aisbett (1991)
<doi:10.2307/2532138>.
FrailtyPackPlus.author:
Shikhar Tyagi [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-1606-0844>)

FuzzyRandom.title: Level-Wise Statistics for Fuzzy Random Variables
FuzzyRandom.description:
Level-wise statistical methods for fuzzy random variables,
implementing the Puri-Ralescu framework. Provides level-wise empirical
distribution functions, moments, covariance and correlation, a level-wise
Kolmogorov-Smirnov goodness-of-fit test, an approximate fuzzy normal
distribution with simulation, and level-wise central limit theorem and law
of large numbers inference. The package only depends on base R.
FuzzyRandom.author:
Gunjan Aggrwal [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0004-3213-4086>),
Mukul Bijalwan [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0009-0001-3040-6912>),
Mukul Jain [aut]

GarrettRank.title: Garrett Ranking Analysis and Visualization
GarrettRank.description:
Performs Garrett ranking analysis of respondent-ranked items such as
constraints, problems, factors, or priorities. The package converts
respondent rankings into Garrett scores, calculates mean Garrett scores
and final ranks and provides methods for summarizing,tabulating and
visualizing ranking results. It also provides Kendall's coefficient of
concordance for assessing the degree of agreement among respondents.
Garrett ranking does not accommodate tied ranks and Kendall's coefficient
of concordance is likewise computed for untied ranking data.For more details see
Garrett and Woodworth (1969) <https://books.google.com/books?id=aoqSmQEACAAJ> and
Buragohain and Dubey (2021) <doi:10.5958/2454-552X.2021.00055.4>.
GarrettRank.author:
Blesson B. Varghese [aut, cre],
Adarsh V S [aut],
Bhavana Sajeev [aut],
Azhanuo Rutsa [aut],
Joe Shiney M A [aut]

GeoIndexR.title:
Computation of Spectral and Geospatial Indices from
Multispectral Raster Data
GeoIndexR.description:
A unified, fast, and extensible framework for calculating spectral
and geospatial indices from multispectral raster datasets (e.g., NDVI - Normalized
Difference Vegetation Index, NDWI - Normalized Difference Water Index, MNDWI -
Modified Normalized Difference Water Index, NDBI - Normalized Difference Built-up
Index, SAVI - Soil Adjusted Vegetation Index, EVI - Enhanced Vegetation Index,
GNDVI - Green Normalized Difference Vegetation Index, NDMI - Normalized Difference
Moisture Index, BSI - Bare Soil Index). Designed around 'terra' 'SpatRaster'
objects, it supports multi-band rasters, automatic band resolution, sensor
presets (Sentinel-2, Landsat-8/9), customizable index parameters, vectorized
computations, and comprehensive validation. Methods based on Rouse et al. (1973)
, McFeeters (1996) <doi:10.1080/01431169608948714>,
Xu (2006) <doi:10.1080/01431160600589179>, Zha et al. (2003) <doi:10.1016/S0034-4257(03)00087-7>,
Huete (1988) <doi:10.1016/0034-4257(88)90106-X>, Gitelson et al. (1996)
<doi:10.1016/S0034-4257(96)00072-7>, Wilson and Sader (2002) <doi:10.1016/S0034-4257(01)00318-2>,
and Rikimaru et al. (2002).
GeoIndexR.author: Mamadou Sow [aut, cre]

GreenManureR.title: Green Manure Decomposition, Nutrient Release and Crop Response
GreenManureR.description:
Tools for analysing green manure and cover crop experiments,
for example with Mucuna, sunhemp and dhaincha. Fits single-pool,
double-pool and asymptotic litterbag decomposition models and ranks
them by the corrected Akaike information criterion, estimates the time
to 50 percent mass loss with Monte-Carlo confidence intervals, and
quantifies nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium and other nutrient release
over time. Further functions compute nutrient inputs, crop uptake,
apparent nitrogen recovery and fertilizer nitrogen replacement value,
estimate residual effects of green manures on succeeding kharif and
rabi crops, link decomposition, nutrient release and crop response in
a joint analysis, and generate standardized tables, diagnostic plots
and a Word report.
GreenManureR.author:
Anbukkani Perumal [aut, cre, cph],
Ramachandran S [aut, cph]

Gtheory4LLM.title: Generalizability Theory for LLM Subjective Tasks
Gtheory4LLM.description:
Studies the reliability and generalizability of subjective
judgments produced by large language models (LLMs), including annotation,
rating, and structured LLM-as-a-judge tasks. Specifies evaluator, prompt,
generation, and repeated-run facets through crossed or explicitly nested
random sources with configurable item interactions. Fits univariate models,
joint Gaussian models, and joint discrete models for binary, ordinal, and
unordered categorical outcomes, with source-specific covariance. Gaussian
models use exact balanced likelihood; discrete models use a dense
first-order Laplace approximation with Gaussian latent random effects.
Supported balanced decision studies compare evaluator, prompt, and
replication allocations using observed Gaussian or explicitly requested
latent binary and ordinal reliability, with random or fixed facets after
Brennan (2001). Gaussian fits report asymptotic Wald standard errors for
their variance components and delta-method intervals for the coefficients;
discrete fits report point estimates only. Provides fixed-layout Gaussian
batch projections, bounded cost-aware allocation comparisons, and Gaussian
simulation-based pilot precision planning. Scalar nominal reliability and
joint Gaussian-discrete fitting are not implemented. Includes three publicly
archived LLM annotation datasets covering hate-speech, mental-health,
and drug-review tasks. Discrete fitting is limited to small models; the
preflight report describes supported designs and computational limits.
Generalizability coefficients follow the variance-decomposition framework
of Brennan (2001) <doi:10.1007/978-1-4757-3456-0>.
Gtheory4LLM.author: Jin Liu [aut, cre, cph]

HMMscpg.title:
Hidden Markov Models and Shifted Compound Poisson-Gamma Renewal
Process
HMMscpg.description:
Provides functions to define, simulate and fit hidden Markov models,
hidden semi-Markov models, and their time-varying versions, to incompletely
observed point process records. Such data arise when some events of an
underlying point process are not recorded or are otherwise missing. The
models treat the number of missing events between each pair of consecutively
observed events of a point process record as a hidden process. The number of
missing events may be fixed or modelled as a random variable whose
distribution can vary over time. When the number of missing events is fixed,
the observed event times can be modelled as a compound gamma renewal process.
When it is random, the observed process is represented by a shifted compound
Poisson-gamma renewal process, which may also depend on time, leading to a
time-dependent shifted compound Poisson-gamma renewal process. These
modelling frameworks are described in detail in Shahzadi, Wang, Parry and
Bebbington (2023) <doi:10.1007/s10463-022-00843-5> and Shahzadi, Wang, Parry
and Bebbington (2026) <doi:10.1007/s11634-025-00632-x>. The model parameters
are estimated through direct nonlinear numerical optimization of the
corresponding likelihood function, and each fit reports whether the change
points of its time-dependent components are identified by the data. The
package also provides methods for assessing model adequacy through residual
analysis. In addition, it calculates and plots the most probable sequences of
hidden states, allowing users to examine changes in the underlying
missing-event process over time.
HMMscpg.author:
Amina Shahzadi [aut, cre],
Ting Wang [aut]

IFARIMA.title:
Intuitionistic Fuzzy Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average
Model
IFARIMA.description: The Intuitionistic Fuzzy Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average model offers advanced time series forecasting by integrating intuitionistic fuzzy sets with ARIMA. It enhances prediction accuracy by handling uncertainties and hesitations more effectively than traditional models, making it ideal for complex, real-world data applications. The package has been developed using the algorithm of Yolcu and Yolcu (2023) <doi:10.1016/j.eswa.2022.119336>.
IFARIMA.author:
Anita Sarkar [aut],
Ankit Kumar Singh [aut],
Md Yeasin [aut, cre],
Ranjit Kumar Paul [aut],
Amrit Kumar Paul [aut],
Pushkar Bora [aut]

IFFuzzyStats.title: Intuitionistic Fuzzy Statistics
IFFuzzyStats.description:
Provides constructors and arithmetic for intuitionistic fuzzy values
(intuitionistic fuzzy value, IFV) for intuitionistic fuzzy sets
(Atanassov (1986) <doi:10.1016/S0165-0114(86)80034-3>), including
aggregation operators of Xu (2007) <doi:10.1109/TFUZZ.2006.890678> and
Xu and Yager (2006) <doi:10.1080/03081070600574353>: intuitionistic fuzzy
weighted averaging (IFWA), intuitionistic fuzzy weighted geometric (IFWG),
intuitionistic fuzzy ordered weighted averaging (IFOWA), intuitionistic
fuzzy ordered weighted geometric (IFOWG), intuitionistic fuzzy hybrid
averaging (IFHA), intuitionistic fuzzy hybrid geometric (IFHG), and
Einstein operators; entropy (Szmidt and Kacprzyk (2000)
<doi:10.1016/S0165-0114(98)00402-3>; Vlachos and Sergiadis (2007)
<doi:10.1016/j.patrec.2006.07.004>) and distance and similarity measures,
including Ye (2011) <doi:10.1016/j.mcm.2010.07.022> cosine similarity and
Hamming, Euclidean and Hausdorff distances; intuitionistic fuzzy c-means
and k-means clustering; approximate reasoning via compositional inference;
and multi-criteria decision support via intuitionistic fuzzy Technique for
Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (IF-TOPSIS)
(Boran et al. (2009) <doi:10.1016/j.eswa.2009.03.039>) and score ranking.
All computations use only base R with fully vectorised implementations.
IFFuzzyStats.author:
Mukul Bijalwan [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0001-3040-6912>),
Gunjan Aggrwal [aut],
Mukul Jain [aut]

INLAcircular.title: Bayesian Joint Circular Regression Using 'INLA'
INLAcircular.description:
Provides a Bayesian regression framework for joint models with
circular responses and covariates using integrated nested Laplace
approximations, following Ye, Van Niekerk and Rue (2026)
<doi:10.48550/arXiv.2602.08413>. The package supports link-adjusted von
Mises likelihoods, shared latent predictors, structured latent effects, and optional
LKJ-based multivariate covariance models. It also provides compiled
circular densities and d/p/q/r penalized-complexity priors for von Mises,
cardioid, and wrapped Cauchy concentration parameters as developed by
Ye, Van Niekerk and Rue (2026) <doi:10.1177/1471082X261453677>.
INLAcircular.author:
Xiang Ye [aut, cre, cph],
Janet Van Niekerk [aut],
Haavard Rue [aut, cph],
Gerard Jungman [ctb, cph] (Bessel routines adapted from the GNU
Scientific Library),
Peter John Acklam [ctb] (Normal quantile approximation)

IncAAM.title:
Bayesian Age-at-Maturity Analysis from Increment-Width Growth
Series
IncAAM.description:
