Bayesian hierarchical nonlinear mixed-effects analysis for
estimating age at sexual maturity from annual increment-width growth
series. The method estimates age at maturity using tangent-ratio and
jerk approaches and provides a posterior threshold-crossing ogive
with an estimated A50. Methodological details and applications are described in
Campana, Smoliński, Morrongiello and Black (2026, in press).
IncAAM.author:
Steven Campana [aut, cre],
Szymon Smoliński [aut],
Bryan Black [aut],
John Morrongiello [aut]

InterconectaR.title: Psychological Network Analysis and Psychometric Insights
InterconectaR.description:
Estimates psychological networks by group for research in
the social sciences and complements them with psychometric modeling. It
summarises centrality and bridge centrality indices, evaluates the
stability of edges and centrality from bootstrap results, refines
items by the stability of exploratory graph analysis (EGA), and plots
networks with the variance explained of each node. It also estimates
an a priori sample size for EGA through Monte Carlo simulation and
includes an interactive application to plan the sample size of a
network study. Methods follow Epskamp, Borsboom
and Fried (2018) <doi:10.3758/s13428-017-0862-1> and Golino and
Epskamp (2017) <doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0174035>.
InterconectaR.author:
José Ventura-León [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-2996-4244>)

KOTORY.title:
Robust Three-Group Tests for Heteroscedasticity in Linear
Regression
KOTORY.description:
Tests for heteroscedasticity in the linear regression model that
sort the data by a regressor, split them into three equal parts and compare
the error scale of the parts. The ordinary least squares version 'kah3.test()'
refers the ratio of the largest to the smallest residual mean square to its
exact null distribution, Hartley's maximum F-ratio with three groups; the
robust version 'kah.robust.test()' replaces the mean squares by least trimmed
squares scales, so that outliers neither create nor hide heteroscedasticity,
and refers the ratio to a maximum F-ratio with simulated effective degrees of
freedom, to a Monte Carlo reference or to a residual bootstrap. The
distribution, density, quantile and random generation functions of the
maximum F-ratio are provided, together with 'run.all.het()', which runs the
proposed tests next to the Goldfeld-Quandt, Breusch-Pagan, White and robust
modified Goldfeld-Quandt tests in one call. For more details see Hartley
(1950) <doi:10.1093/biomet/37.3-4.308>, Goldfeld and Quandt (1965)
<doi:10.1080/01621459.1965.10480811> and Rousseeuw (1984)
<doi:10.1080/01621459.1984.10477105>.
KOTORY.author:
Ahmed El-Kotory [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0009-0000-1485-0768>),
Ebrahim Khaled Ebrahim [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0006-7839-8778>)

KeyNubLicDongle.title: Client for the 'KeyNub' USB License Dongle
KeyNubLicDongle.description:
Verifies that a 'KeyNub' USB license dongle is genuine, reads and
writes the license records it holds, reads and increments its monotonic
counters, and encrypts data so that only a dongle can decrypt it. The work
is done by the vendor's native library, which the package loads at run
time; the package installs without it and reports where it looked. Runs on
Windows, Linux and macOS.
KeyNubLicDongle.author:
Andreas Breitschopp [aut, cre],
KeyNub [cph]

LAGOtrials.title: Learn-as-You-Go Adaptive Trial Optimization
LAGOtrials.description:
Optimizes interventions for adaptive "Learn-As-you-GO" (LAGO)
trials, in which the intervention package is updated between stages using
accumulating data. Given data from completed stages, lago_optimization()
fits the outcome model (via 'stats' generalized linear models or, for
clustered designs, cluster-robust variance) and computes the cost-optimal
recommended intervention for the next stage that is expected to reach a
target mean outcome and/or a desired statistical power. get_confidence_set()
constructs confidence sets for the optimal intervention, and visualize_cost()
and lago_report() summarize the cost surface and results. Methods are
described in Nevo, Lok and Spiegelman (2021) <doi:10.1214/20-aos1978> and
Bing, Spiegelman, Nevo and Lok (2025) <doi:10.1093/biomtc/ujaf061>.
LAGOtrials.author:
Ante Bing [aut, cre],
Minh Bui [aut],
Jingyu Cui [aut],
Mike Bostock [cph] (Author of the bundled D3 v7 library,
inst/js/d3.v7.min.js)

LMDT.title: Local Manifold Dispersion Test for Heteroskedasticity
LMDT.description:
Implements the Local Manifold Dispersion Test (LMDT) for
detecting complex, non-linear, and high-dimensional heteroskedasticity
in linear regression models. LMDT measures the spectral smoothness
(Dirichlet energy) of robust log-dispersion residuals over a self-tuning
k-nearest neighbors graph Laplacian, as formulated in Jabbar (2026).
The test statistic is asymptotically distribution-free with respect to error
kurtosis and accommodates high-dimensional covariates (p > 50) via
Gavish-Donoho optimal hard thresholding and supervised metric learning.
LMDT.author: Ahmed Sattar Jabbar [aut, cre]

LatencyA.title:
Latency Analysis in Epidemiological Studies Using Weighted
Cumulative Exposures
LatencyA.description:
Implements weighted cumulative exposure Cox proportional hazards
models for latency analysis with repeatedly measured, time-varying
exposures. Instead of entering every lagged exposure as a separate and
highly correlated covariate, the lag-specific log hazard ratios are
constrained to follow a smooth function of the time since exposure,
parameterized by natural cubic splines or polynomials, so that the
susceptible window of an exposure can be identified from the estimated
lag-risk curve. Functions are provided to fit models with a
prespecified number of knots or polynomial degree, to select the number
of knots by a grid search or the spline terms by a stepwise search using
the Akaike or Bayesian information criterion, and to extract
lag-specific log hazard ratios with their variances. For the
data-driven model selection procedures, inference is based on a cluster
bootstrap that resamples subjects, which can be run sequentially or in
parallel. The methods are described in Guo, Qian, Wang, Wang, Rosner and
Wang (2026) "Taking Into Account the Susceptible Window for Exposures in
Cox Proportional Hazards Model: A Way Using Splines to Model the Lag-Risk
Relationship" <doi:10.1002/sim.70755>.
LatencyA.author:
Fuyu Guo [aut, cre],
Zihan Qian [aut],
Molin Wang [aut]

MAC.address.title: Find, Validate and Identify Device MAC Addresses
MAC.address.description:
Tools to work with MAC (Media Access Control) addresses: list the
MAC addresses of the local network interfaces and of the neighbors in the
ARP cache on Linux, macOS and Windows, extract MAC addresses from free
text, validate and normalize their notation, check the multicast and
locally administered bits, generate random addresses, derive IPv6
interface identifiers (modified EUI-64), and identify the manufacturer using the public IEEE (Institute of
Electrical and Electronics Engineers) MA-L, MA-M and MA-S registries
<https://regauth.standards.ieee.org/standards-ra-web/pub/view.html#registries>.
MAC.address.author: Enrique Pérez Herrero [aut, cre]

MCAtools.title:
Multiple Correspondence Analysis Toolkit (Phi-Divergence
Framework)
MCAtools.description:
A toolkit for performing Multiple Correspondence Analysis
(MCA) based on the phi-divergence framework of Cressie and Read
(1984) <doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1984.tb01318.x>. Provides
implementations for MCA computation mca_analysis(), visualization
plot_mca(), and symbolic equation generation
generate_mca_equation(), designed for interpretability,
flexibility, and analytical consistency with generalized
divergence measures.
MCAtools.author:
Awa Traoré [aut],
Assi Lazare N'GUESSAN [aut],
MOUSSA Kouamé Richard [aut],
Nona Servais KAMDEM SIMO [aut, cre],
Muhamad Setyawan Bahari [aut]

MixedDiversityAnalysis.title: Analysis and Visualization of Mixed-Trait Dissimilarity
MixedDiversityAnalysis.description: Provides methods for analysing datasets containing quantitative, qualitative, binary, and ordinal traits. Computes mixed-trait dissimilarities and performs hierarchical clustering using multiple linkage methods. Supports principal coordinates analysis (PCoA), cluster evaluation, trait contribution analysis, and graphical visualization. The package facilitates mixed-trait diversity assessment and characterization of crop germplasm. For more detail see Gower (1971) <doi:10.2307/2528823> and Jukanti et al. (2026) <doi:10.1007/s44187-025-00715-w>.
MixedDiversityAnalysis.author:
Santosha Rathod [aut],
Prabhat Kumar [aut, cre],
A. K. Jukanti [aut],
Radha Upadhyay [aut],
Prashantkumar S Hanjagi [aut],
Basavaraj PS [aut],
R. N. Singh [aut],
Anil Kumar [aut]

MultinomFourier.title:
p-Values of Multinomial Goodness-of-Fit Tests by Fourier Series
Inversion
MultinomFourier.description:
Computes p-values of multinomial goodness-of-fit tests based on an
additive statistic: the log-likelihood ratio, Pearson's chi-squared, the
Cressie-Read power divergence, and the exact multinomial test. The main
function, pval_fourier(), writes the p-value as a Fourier series in the
moment-generating function of the statistic and sums it until an adaptive
stopping rule is met, which makes small p-values of large instances
computationally feasible. The function pval_exact() computes the exact p-value by
branch pruning with bounds from a dynamic program, and pval_flexible()
chooses between the two according to the size of the instance.
MultinomFourier.author:
Charles Thraves [aut],
Pablo Rivas [aut, cre],
Felipe Subiabre [aut]

MultipleSystemsEstimation.title: Methods for Multiple Systems Estimation
MultipleSystemsEstimation.description:
Methods for multiple systems estimation using
Poisson log-linear models, with particular attention to sparse capture
data, model selection and its associated uncertainty, and Bayesian
thresholding of interaction effects. The package implements and extends methodology
from Silverman (2020) <doi:10.1111/rssa.12505>,
Chan, Silverman and Vincent (2021)
<doi:10.1080/01621459.2019.1708748>, and Silverman, Chan and Vincent
(2024) <doi:10.1007/s11222-023-10346-9>.
MultipleSystemsEstimation.author:
Bernard W. Silverman [aut, cre],
Lax Chan [ctb],
Kyle Vincent [ctb]

NSCA.title: Necessary and Sufficient Condition Analysis
NSCA.description:
Tests whether a condition is both necessary and sufficient for an
outcome, that is, whether the outcome cannot be reached without the
condition and is guaranteed in its presence. Such a claim implies that two
diagonally opposite corners of the condition-outcome scatter plot contain
no observations. The package estimates both boundaries with the same data,
scope and frontier technique, reports the effect size and permutation test
of each, and indicates joint support only when both components are
supported. The two components are summarized by the weaker effect, a
balanced combination and the proportion of the scope that the two claims
jointly rule out. A dual-threshold table gives, for each outcome level, the
condition level it requires, the level sufficient for it, and the interval
between them. Results can be compared with regression slopes. The package
also provides plots, influential-case diagnostics, scope-sensitivity and
resampling checks, and simulation and power analysis for planning studies.
The two sides are estimated with the 'NCA' and 'SCAtools' packages.
NSCA.author: Young Chan [aut, cre]

NormGen.title:
An Efficient and Precise Quantile Mapping for Normal
Pseudo-Random Number Generation
NormGen.description:
High-performance pseudo-normal random generator using an
optimized quantile mapping algorithm. It provides fast generation of
normal pseudo-random numbers based on precise mathematical
approximations. The package features Rnorm() for efficient
single-threaded generation and parallel_Rnorm(), a high-performance,
multithreaded variant powered by 'RcppParallel' and Intel 'TBB'.
Package compilation flags are optimized to support multi-core parallel
processing. Renamed parallel_Rnorm() to PRnorm() for brevity.
NormGen.author: Piotr Sulewski [aut, cre]

OECDdata.title: Fast and Friendly Access to OECD Data
OECDdata.description:
Discover, describe, compare and import statistical datasets from
the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development ('OECD') via its
public Statistical Data and Metadata eXchange ('SDMX') Representational
State Transfer ('REST') API <https://sdmx.oecd.org/public/>. Adapts the
discovery workflow of 'eurodata' to OECD-native names, catalogue-resolved
short codes and dataset-scoped metadata. Uses SDMX REST version 2 by
default, streamed downloads, native 'data.table' parsing, defensive
metadata resolution, caching and bounded HTTP retries. Includes an
explicit version 1 transport for interoperability.
OECDdata.author: Alek Rutkowski [aut, cre, cph]

OceanTracer.title: Marine Source Unmixing Toolkit
OceanTracer.description: Reconstructs the provenance of particulate matter and marine sediments by 'unmixing' isotopic and elemental signatures. Provides a specialized toolkit for marine biogeochemistry, coastal tracing, and oceanographic sediment transport following the step-by-step procedure described in Cepeda 'et' 'al.' (2026) <doi:10.1002/lom3.70083>, which is tested using artificial mixtures.
OceanTracer.author:
Esther Cepeda [aut, cre],
Maarten Wynants [aut],
Ivan Lizaga [aut, ths, ldr],
Samuel Bodé [ctb],
Pascal Boeckx [ctb],
Jan Vanaverbeke [ctb],
Ulrike Braeckman [ctb],
Margarita Villalonga [ctb],
Aiming Liang [ctb],
Borja Latorre [ctb],
Leticia Gaspar [ctb],
Ana Navas [ctb],
Vince Q Vu [ctb]

OptimalFactor.title:
Item Selection in Factor Analysis by Boosting and Specification
Search
OptimalFactor.description:
Provides an iterative optimization algorithm for exploratory
and confirmatory factor analysis that follows a boosting approach
inspired by machine learning. It uses a composite fit index whose
weights adapt to the degrees of freedom and the sample size, following
Kenny and McCoach (2003) <doi:10.1207/S15328007SEM1003_1> and Shi, Lee
and Maydeu-Olivares (2019) <doi:10.1177/0013164418783530>. It detects
and removes problematic items (Heywood cases, cross-loadings, low
loadings) with greedy or global search strategies, checks interfactor
correlations, and supports ordinal data with WLSMV estimation and
several rotation methods. A heuristic specification search for
confirmatory models (MacCallum, 1986 <doi:10.1037/0033-2909.100.1.107>)
explores move, drop and covariance operations across seed
configurations. It also evaluates the resampling stability of the item
selection, the recovery of a known or theoretical structure, and offers
an optional conceptual analysis of removed items through a large
language model service.
OptimalFactor.author:
Jose Ventura-Leon [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-2996-4244>)

PBGoF.title: Goodness-of-Fit Tests for Skew-Normal and Skew-t Models
PBGoF.description:
Provides precomputed-quantile goodness-of-fit tests for
skew-normal distributions, parametric-bootstrap tests for skew-normal and
skew-t distributions, robust fitting, and graphical diagnostics.
Package methods and documentation are described by Li, Xu, and Khang
(2026) <https://github.com/Divo-Lee/PBGoF>.
PBGoF.author:
Hongxiang Li [aut, cre],
Chenglin Xu [aut],
Tsung Fei Khang [aut]

PDRobust.title: Robust Longitudinal Effects Under Truncation by Death
PDRobust.description:
Implements principal-stratification methods for estimating
time-specific and pooled heterogeneous treatment effects in longitudinal
studies where outcomes may be truncated by death. Supports continuous and
binary outcomes, explicit data validation and standardization, and
covariate-dependent treatment effects. Fits propensity-score,
principal-score, and outcome models and provides subject-level bootstrap
inference, covariate-balance diagnostics, principal-stratum summaries,
treatment-group-specific survival odds ratios, and outcome-noise
sensitivity analysis. Methodological background is provided in
<doi:10.48550/arXiv.2608.06654>.
PDRobust.author:
Huan Wang [aut, cre],
Yilin Zhang [aut]

PICOTsize.title: Sample Size Calculation for PICOT-Based Study Designs
PICOTsize.description:
Provides sample size calculators for the study designs
covered by the PICOT framework, including cross-sectional,
case-control, cohort, superiority, non-inferiority, and
equivalence clinical trials, and diagnostic test accuracy
studies, following Bhardwaj et al. (2024)
<doi:10.4103/jfmpc.jfmpc_1675_23>. Calculations are performed
using the 'epiR' package as a validated computational backend.
Includes a 'shiny' application with a PICOT-based design
wizard, an interactive sensitivity plot, and automatically
generated Methods-section text for manuscripts.
PICOTsize.author: Atefeh Rashidi Pour [aut, cre]

POEMED.title: Power Enhancement for High-Dimensional Mediation Analysis
POEMED.description:
Provides powerful global tests for high-dimensional mediation
analysis with heterogeneous (and even contrasting) mediation effects,
for continuous, binary, and count outcomes. The power enhancement (PE)
idea augments a Wald test on the total indirect effect with a component
that captures marginal signals from individual mediators, so that active
mediators are detected even when their individual indirect effects
cancel and the total indirect effect is zero. The package also
identifies which individual mediators are active with familywise error
rate or false discovery rate control. The methods implement Yu and
Kelley (in press), "Power Enhancement in High-Dimensional Heterogeneous
Mediation Analysis" (Journal of the American Statistical Association);
the package also simulates mediation data under the homogeneous,
heterogeneous, and contrasting patterns that the article studies, ships
its empirical health-expenditure data as a benchmark and reruns that
empirical analysis, and runs the designs of its Monte Carlo size and
power studies. The name, 'POEMED', from POwer-Enhanced MEDiation,
encodes the method. Every estimation and testing function returns a
tidy 'data.frame' that prints with sensible rounding and composes with
the broader R ecosystem.
POEMED.author:
Xiufan Yu [aut],
Ken Kelley [aut, cre] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-4756-8360>)

PairedRand.title: Paired Randomization Functions
PairedRand.description: Provides tools for generating simulated study data, creating matched participant pairs using optimal nonbipartite matching, randomizing participants within pairs into study groups, and assessing post-randomization balance using descriptive summary statistics and standardized mean differences. The matching methodology is based on Lu et al. (2011) <doi:10.1198/tast.2011.08294>.
PairedRand.author:
Milan Bimali [aut, cre],
Kamal Joshi [aut],
Miaolei Bao [aut]

PheValuator.title: Rapid Phenotype Evaluation
PheValuator.description:
Evaluates phenotype algorithms by developing a diagnostic
prediction model using a set of noisy positives and noisy negatives.
It can then apply the model to a large cohort
to create a set of subjects each with a predicted probability for the
health outcome of interest.  This cohort can then be used to evaluate
phenotype algorithms through the calculation of the necessary performance
characteristics - sensitivity, specificity, and positive and negative
predictive value. Based on work by Swerdel (2022) <doi:10.1016/j.jbi.2022.104177>
and Swerdel (2019) <doi:10.1016/j.jbi.2019.103258>.
PheValuator.author:
William J. O'Brien [aut, cre],
Joel Swerdel [aut],
Martijn Schuemie [aut]

PortinariColors.title: Color Palettes Inspired by the Paintings of Candido Portinari
PortinariColors.description:
Color palettes inspired by paintings of Candido Portinari held by
the Sao Paulo Museum of Art (MASP) and by his Guerra (War) and Paz (Peace)
panels at the United Nations Headquarters. Provides qualitative, diverging
and sequential palettes for discrete and continuous data, ready-made
'ggplot2' color and fill scales, and a colorblind-safety check that
simulates protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia following Machado,
Oliveira and Fernandes (2009) <doi:10.1109/TVCG.2009.113>.
PortinariColors.author: Rafa Lopes [aut, cre]

PrismR.title: Pre-Modeling Statistical Audit Framework
PrismR.description:
Introduces a statistical validation layer between data
preprocessing and predictive modeling. Evaluates the statistical
readiness of tabular datasets through data quality assessment,
leakage detection, transformation analysis, and feature stability.
PrismR.author:
Arshit Choudhary [aut, cre, cph],
Vanshika Sharma [aut, ctb],
Amrit Pal [ths]

RASbound.title:
Bounded RAS / Biproportional Matrix Balancing with Cell-Level
Constraints
RASbound.description:
Implements the RAS method for adjusting a matrix to match
target row and column totals. In RAS, a matrix A is multiplied on the
left by a diagonal matrix R and on the right by a diagonal matrix S,
which gives the method its name. It is also known as biproportional
matrix balancing, iterative proportional fitting (IPF) or raking.
The package extends it with lower and upper bounds on individual cells.
Provides several algorithmic variants for handling bound violations:
hard cell-freezing with simultaneous, sequential, or hybrid fixation;
two dependency-free clamp-and-compensate heuristics (proportional
redistribution and iterative renormalization); and a naive
unconstrained-recompute baseline; together with thin wrapper functions
exposing equivalent bounded-calibration methods from the 'survey'
package under a common interface.
Intended for updating or regionalizing input-output tables, social
accounting matrices (SAMs), and other applications where classic RAS/IPF
is used but cell-level plausibility ranges must be respected.
References:
Deming and Stephan (1940) <doi:10.1214/aoms/1177731829>
Deville, Saerndal and Sautory (1993) <doi:10.1080/01621459.1993.10476369>
Acknowledgements:
The author wishes to thank Conselleria de Educacion, Cultura y Universidades,
Generalitat Valenciana (grant CIAICO/2023/031) for supporting this research.
RASbound.author:
Jose M. Pavía [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0129-726X>)

RBMRB.title:
Interface to the Biological Magnetic Resonance Data Bank
('BMRB')
RBMRB.description:
A comprehensive interface to the Biological Magnetic Resonance
Data Bank ('BMRB') <https://bmrb.io>, mirroring all functionality of the
'PyBMRB' 'Python' package (v3.0). Provides four modules: (1) 'ChemicalShift'
for fetching per-entry  chemical shift data from the 'BMRB' 'REST' 'API'
or local 'NMR-STAR' files; (2) 'ChemicalShiftStatistics' for database-wide
statistical queries; (3) Spectra for simulating '1H-15N' 'HSQC', '1H-13C'
'HSQC', '1H-1H' 'TOCSY', and generic 2D 'NMR' spectra as interactive plots;
and (4) Histogram for chemical shift distribution visualizations with
optional filtering by pH, temperature, and ambiguity code.
All interactive plots are rendered via 'plotly'.
Uses the 'BMRB' REST API v2 <https://api.bmrb.io/v2/>.
RBMRB.author:
Kumaran Baskaran [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0418-0286>)

RCPA4.title:
Data and Functions for "An R Companion to Political Analysis,
Fourth Edition"
RCPA4.description: Provides teaching-oriented functions and datasets for "An R Companion to Political Analysis, Fourth Edition" (forthcoming 2026). Functions produce readable tables and graphics for descriptive statistics, data transformation, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, comparisons, cross-tabulation, and linear and logistic regression. Sampling weights are supported where appropriate, and analysis functions return reusable results for further examination. The package also includes curated political datasets designed for classroom instruction and independent practice. See Edwards and Pollock (forthcoming 2026) <https://www.poliscidata.com/textbooks/r_companion_4e.php>.
RCPA4.author:
Barry C. Edwards [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0005-6699-3820>),
Philip H. Pollock III [ctb]

RDML7.title:
Read, Write, Validate, and Analyze Real-Time PCR Data in the
'RDML' Format
RDML7.description:
Reads, writes, validates, converts, and manipulates quantitative
polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) data through the Real-Time PCR Data
Markup Language ('RDML') application programming interface (API), using
'S7' objects. Includes an extensible file-format registry, vendor and
tabular-data importers, 'RDES' import and export, fluorescence-table
helpers, semantic validation, and compatibility wrappers for the
historical 'RDML' API.
RDML7.author:
Konstantin A. Blagodatskikh [cre, aut],
Stefan Roediger [ctb],
Michal Burdukiewicz [ctb],
Andrej-Nikolai Spiess [ctb]

RDelta.title: Parse and Query DELTA-Format Taxonomic Descriptions
RDelta.description:
Provides an R interface to the 'tDelta' C++ library for parsing
DELTA (DEscription Language for TAxonomy) format files <https://freedelta.sourceforge.net>.
Supports loading character lists, item descriptions, and specifications, with efficient
searching and matching of items based on character values. It also supports
the generation of identification keys, diagnoses, natural-language descriptions,
and clustering and ordination analyses by means of the DELTA programs 'CONFOR',
'KEY', and 'DIST'.
RDelta.author:
Mauro Cavalcanti [aut, cre] (Original tDelta C++ library by Denis
Ziegler),
Edinaldo Nelson dos Santos Silva [ctb]

RQK.title: Rational Quadratic Kriging
RQK.description:
Fits the rational quadratic kriging models of Song and Joseph
(2026) <doi:10.48550/arXiv.2610.18077> for deterministic and noisy
responses using a rational quadratic kernel with anisotropic factor
weights. Provides leave-one-out tuning, fast 'C++' prediction routines,
and conformal prediction intervals. This work is supported by a U.S. NSF
grant DMS-2310637.
RQK.author:
Difan Song [aut, cre],
V. Roshan Joseph [aut]

RTFBoost.title: Robust Tree-Based Boosting for Functional Regression
RTFBoost.description:
Implements a family of robust tree-based boosting methods for
functional regression, including procedures based on least absolute
deviation, M-estimation, and MM-estimation. The package also includes a non-robust tree-based boosting method introduced in Ju X and Salibian-Barrera M. (2024) <doi:10.1007/s00180-023-01364-2>. Functions are provided
for model fitting and prediction in regression settings with functional
predictors.
RTFBoost.author:
Xiaomeng Ju [aut, cre],
Matias Salibian-Barrera [aut]

RTrino.title: 'DBI' Backend for 'Trino'
RTrino.description:
A 'DBI' compliant backend for 'Trino' <https://trino.io>, the
distributed SQL query engine (successor of 'PrestoSQL'). Connects to a
'Trino' cluster over its HTTP REST API, executes queries with automatic
pagination, maps 'Trino' types to R types, and integrates with 'dplyr'
through 'dbplyr' SQL dialects. Supports basic, JSON Web Token (JWT)
bearer and OAuth2 client credentials authentication, as well as custom
certificate authorities.
RTrino.author: Luis A Casas Ballestas [aut, cre, cph]

RWInfoLSTM.title: Random Walk-Informed LSTM for Time Series Forecasting
RWInfoLSTM.description:
Implements a Random Walk (RW)-informed Long Short-Term Memory
(LSTM) network for univariate time series forecasting. The LSTM is
trained on the full series with a composite loss that blends the usual
mean squared error (MSE) between predictions and observations with the
MSE between predictions and the fitted Random Walk, weighted by a
parameter lambda (0 gives a standard LSTM, 1 gives a fully RW-guided
LSTM). The Random Walk, either simple or with drift, is selected
automatically by its in-sample root mean squared error (RMSE), and the
lambda value with the lowest training RMSE is retained. The LSTM
hyperparameters can be supplied manually or tuned by grid search, and
functions for out-of-sample forecasting, accuracy measures and plots
are provided. The methodology is motivated by hybrid forecasting
framework proposed by Yeasin and Paul (2024)
<doi:10.1007/s11227-023-05542-3>.
RWInfoLSTM.author:
Md Yeasin [aut],
Ranjit Kumar Paul [aut, cre],
Pushkar Bora [aut]

RecoverMetricsR.title: Quantifying Post-Fire Spectral Recovery Metrics
RecoverMetricsR.description:
Computes pixel-wise metrics describing post-disturbance
spectral recovery from a yearly spectral-index time series. Metrics
include disturbance magnitude (DM), an ordinary least squares (OLS)
recovery slope, early- and late-period recovery rates, recovery-rate
change, Relative Recovery Indicator (RRI), Ratio of Eighty Percent
(R80P), and Year-on-Year recovery (YrYr). The RRI, R80P, and YrYr
metrics are based on approaches described by Frazier et al. (2018)
<doi:10.1016/j.rse.2017.11.007>. Threshold-based recovery-time
approaches have been used to quantify post-fire vegetation recovery
from spectral time series by Chompuchan and Lin (2017)
<doi:10.1016/j.ecolind.2017.04.038>. Exponential recovery
formulations have also been applied to post-fire vegetation time
series by Gouveia et al. (2010) <doi:10.5194/nhess-10-673-2010>.
Parametric recovery models, including exponential, logistic, and
Gompertz formulations, are provided to characterize nonlinear
post-disturbance recovery trajectories.
RecoverMetricsR.author:
Hammadi Achour [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-6364-3789>),
Amal Daboussi [aut],
Wahbi Jaouadi [aut]

ReguGLH.title: General Linear Hypothesis Tests via Spectral Shrinkage
ReguGLH.description:
Implements high-dimensional general linear hypothesis tests using
ridge, reciprocal cubic polynomial, and user-defined analytic spectral
regularizers. Provides prior-based shrinkage selection and Gaussian
maximum calibration for composite tests. Implements the methods of
Li, Aue and Paul (2020), "High-dimensional general linear hypothesis
tests via non-linear spectral shrinkage", Bernoulli, 26(4), 2541-2571
<doi:10.3150/19-BEJ1186>.
ReguGLH.author: Haoran Li [aut, cre]

ResistantProcrustes.title: Resistant Procrustes Methods for Multivariate Data
ResistantProcrustes.description: Provides resistant alternatives to the standard Procrustes analysis for comparing multivariate datasets, including seven resistant Procrustean methods and their associated permutation tests, as well as the standard Procrustes analysis and its permutation tests. Methods are based on Tang and Jackson (2026) "Improving and evaluating resistant alternatives to Procrustes analysis for multivariate dataset matching" <doi:10.1002/env.70073>.
ResistantProcrustes.author: Xiaozhuo Tang [aut, cre]

RidgeLRGLH.title:
Ridge-Regularized Largest Root Tests for General Linear
Hypotheses
RidgeLRGLH.description:
Tests general linear hypotheses in high-dimensional multivariate
regression using a ridge-regularized largest root statistic. Estimates the
population spectral distribution by linear programming and computes
Tracy-Widom centering and scaling constants. Supports fixed, Bayesian, and
minimax regularization choices. Implements the methods of Li (2025)
<doi:10.48550/arXiv.2504.15510>.
RidgeLRGLH.author: Haoran Li [aut, cre]

SINT.title: Simulation and Analysis of Social Influence Network Models
SINT.description:
Tools for specifying, analyzing and simulating models of social
influence network theory based on the Friedkin-Johnsen model, Friedkin
and Johnsen (1990) <doi:10.1080/0022250X.1990.9990069>, which includes the
consensus model of DeGroot (1974) <doi:10.1080/01621459.1974.10480137> as
a special case. Equilibrium opinions, total influence matrices and
convergence diagnostics are computed in closed form, also for signed
networks with antagonistic ties, Altafini (2013)
<doi:10.1109/TAC.2012.2224251>. Simulations allow influence weights and
susceptibilities to depend on time and on the state of the system, and can
couple latent opinions with manifest responses through logistic or
threshold response functions, whose results are aggregated into collective
outcomes by quota rules.
SINT.author:
Giulio Vidotto [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-3854-5087>)

SNPAssayR.title: SNP Genotyping Assay Design and Visualization
SNPAssayR.description:
Designs cleaved amplified polymorphic sequence (CAPS), derived
CAPS (dCAPS), conventional amplification refractory mutation system
(ARMS) and tetra-primer ARMS assays for single-locus, biallelic single
nucleotide polymorphisms. Evaluates sequence-compatible primer binding,
reconstructs ideal polymerase chain reaction products and computes
theoretical complete restriction digestion and conditional genotype
profiles. Transparent preference ranking, scientific visualizations and
reproducible exports retain assumptions, missing specificity evidence and
bounded search limitations. An optional offline 'shiny' interface uses the
independently available analysis functions. Predictions do not establish
experimental amplification, digestion efficiency or genome-wide specificity.
Implements perfect-match nearest-neighbor thermodynamics from SantaLucia
(1998) <doi:10.1073/pnas.95.4.1460>, single-substitution site-creation
dCAPS based on Neff et al. (1998) <doi:10.1046/j.1365-313X.1998.00124.x>,
and conditional ARMS designs based on Newton et al.
(1989) <doi:10.1093/nar/17.7.2503> and Ye et al.
(2001) <doi:10.1093/nar/29.17.e88>.

SWORD.title: Support Vector Machine Weighted Oblique Random Decision Forests
SWORD.description:
Implements SWORD (Support vector machine Weighted Oblique Random
Decision forests), a random forest method for regression based on TORS
(Tree Oblique for Regression with weighted SVM) oblique regression trees. At each internal node a
Weighted-SVM classifier with a linear kernel defines the oblique splitting
hyperplane as a sparse linear combination of predictors. The C++
coordinate-descent solver provides fast training. Variable importance is
computed via OIW-VI (Oblique Impurity-Weighted Variable Importance).
Provides tree fitting (TORS), forest fitting (SWORD), prediction, and
variable importance (VI_SWORD). Parallel tree fitting is supported via the
'future'/'furrr' framework.
The SWORD method is described in Carta and Frigau (accepted, in press)
'Oblique Random Forests for Regression via Weighted Support Vector Machine',
Advances in Data Analysis and Classification.
The TORS algorithm is described in Carta and Frigau (2025)
<doi:10.1007/s00180-025-01647-w>. The weighted SVM is based on
Yang, Song and Cao (2005) <doi:10.1109/IJCNN.2005.1555965> and the
'WeightSVM' package by Xu et al. (2024)
<doi:10.32614/CRAN.package.WeightSVM>.
SWORD.author:
Andrea Carta [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-4077-1822>),
Luca Frigau [aut]

SeqNet.title: Generate RNA-Seq Data from Gene-Gene Association Networks
SeqNet.description: Methods to generate random gene-gene association networks and simulate RNA-seq data from them, as described in Grimes and Datta (2021) <doi:10.18637/jss.v098.i12>. Includes functions to generate random networks of any size and perturb them to obtain differential networks. Network objects are built from individual, overlapping modules that represent pathways. The resulting network has various topological properties that are characteristic of gene regulatory networks. RNA-seq data can be generated such that the association among gene expression profiles reflect the underlying network. A reference RNA-seq dataset can be provided to model realistic marginal distributions. Plotting functions are available to visualize a network, compare two networks, and compare the expression of two genes across multiple networks.
SeqNet.author:
Tyler Grimes [aut, cre],
Somnath Datta [aut]

SpectralMM.title: Spectral Majorization for Statistical Estimation
SpectralMM.description:
Fits generalized linear, asymmetric and robust regression models
using spectral majorization and iterative quadratic subproblem solvers.
A shared C++ computational core supports dense and sparse designs, automatic
intercepts, optional Wald inference and detailed iteration diagnostics.
Native code is compiled automatically during package installation.
SpectralMM.author: Xun-Jian Li [aut, cre]

SurveySolutionsAPIv2.title:
Comprehensive API Access to Your 'Survey Solutions' Server Using
'httr2'
SurveySolutionsAPIv2.description:
A comprehensive suite of functions for interfacing
with the 'Survey Solutions' APIs
(<https://demo.mysurvey.solutions/apidocs/index.html> and
<https://docs.mysurvey.solutions/>). It supports all the
current POST, GET, and PATCH requests of the 'REST' API and extends
its capabilities by integrating selected 'GraphQL' API queries and
mutations when 'REST' API equivalents are not available. Designed for
ease of use, it includes several convenience functions to streamline
operations. The package ensures that data retrieved from the API is
automatically transformed into a single, easy-to-use data frame or
data table, optimizing it for subsequent analysis and processing.
Additionally, it is specifically designed to facilitate seamless
integration into 'shiny' applications, enhancing the interactive web
application development experience. Built on the robust 'httr2'
package, this version supersedes the previous 'httr'-based
implementation. Recognizing the needs of large-scale data operations
such as censuses, the package also incorporates features for
parallel processing, enhancing its efficiency and scalability.
SurveySolutionsAPIv2.author: Michael Wild [aut, cre, cph]

SyncER.title: Synchronicity Testing for Event Records
SyncER.description: Evaluation of synchronous deposition across different event records using a log-ratio approach, and syncing age-depth models based on the availability of isochrons. Following the methodology of Wils & Ramisch (2026) <doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67943-7>. The synthetic example dataset used in the examples, tests and vignette is distributed separately in the companion data package 'SyncERdata'.
SyncER.author: Katleen Wils [aut, cre]

SynthesizerPlus.title:
Synthetic Data Generation with Copulas, Evaluation and
Multi-Format I/O
SynthesizerPlus.description:
Generates synthetic versions of numeric, categorical, mixed-type
and time-series data. Marginal distributions are modelled with
interpolated empirical quantile functions and dependence with Gaussian or
Student-t copulas (Sklar, 1959). Discrete and categorical variables enter
the copula through the distributional transform (Ruschendorf, 2009,
<doi:10.1016/j.jspi.2009.05.030>), and their latent correlations are
estimated by maximum likelihood as polychoric (Olsson, 1979,
<doi:10.1007/BF02296207>) and polyserial (Olsson, Drasgow and Dorans,
1982, <doi:10.1007/BF02294164>) correlations. Missing values are
modelled by missingness indicators inside the copula, so that
missingness may depend on other variables. Supports stratified models,
a closeness parameter with calibration to a target distance or
disclosure-risk level, chunked generation of very large data sets,
copula vector-autoregressive and bootstrap time-series synthesis,
augmentation of small training sets for machine learning, and random
generation from multivariate distributions and elliptical and
Archimedean copulas. Fidelity, utility and disclosure risk are assessed
with marginal distances, association matrices, propensity score
mean-squared error (Snoke et al., 2018, <doi:10.1111/rssa.12358>),
confidence-interval overlap, correct attribution probability and
distance to closest record, with 'ggplot2' visualisations. Data can be
read from and written to CSV, TSV, RDS, RData, Parquet, Feather, HDF5,
JSON, NDJSON, Excel, SPSS, Stata, SAS and fst files. The
empirical-quantile and copula approach builds on ideas of the
'synthesizer' package by Mark van der Loo.
SynthesizerPlus.author: Bogdan Oancea [aut, cre, cph]

TEMPO.title: Tools for Romania's National Institute of Statistics Tempo Data
TEMPO.description:
Find, inspect and download statistical tables from the Romanian
National Institute of Statistics' TEMPO Online database. Tables can be
listed and searched in Romanian or English, their structure inspected
before downloading, and whole tables or filtered selections retrieved
either as data frames or as CSV files that are kept up to date between
sessions.
TEMPO.author:
Marian Necula [aut, cre],
Bogdan Oancea [aut],
Ana Maria Tiru [aut]

TSGenerator.title: 'Copernicus' HR-VPP Vegetation Time-Series Processing
TSGenerator.description:
Provides tools for acquiring, extracting, quality-assessing, and
analysing vegetation time series derived from 'Copernicus' High Resolution
Vegetation Phenology and Productivity (HR-VPP) products. Supports Seasonal
Trajectories (ST) and Vegetation Phenology and Productivity (VPP) products
through native R access to 'WEkEO', geospatial processing, product-quality
assessment, temporal completeness analysis, missingness modelling, and
integrated graphical workflows. Selected functions from 'TSGenerator' 1.x are
retained to support migration and legacy workflows.
TSGenerator.author:
Alexey Valero-Jorge [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-5993-7346>),
M. Auxiliadora Casterad Seral [aut] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-4458-6966>),
Jose-Tomas Alcala Nalvaiz [aut] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-7549-8825>)

TTM.title: Terminal Trend Models on the Retrospective Time Scale
TTM.description:
Fits retrospective-time longitudinal models for terminal trend
analysis using weighted generalized estimating equations and related joint
modeling tools. The package provides functions to estimate spline-based
baseline and treatment effect trajectories on the retrospective time scale,
obtain pointwise confidence intervals, and visualize fitted trajectories.
TTM.author:
Tingchang Wang [aut],
Zhigang Li [aut, cre]

ThesiStats.title: Statistical Tools for Quantitative Theses
ThesiStats.description:
Provides helpers for the analyses that quantitative theses in
the social and behavioral sciences repeat: renaming and scoring items,
recoding Likert responses, cleaning sociodemographic variables written
in Spanish (age, academic term, degree and university), descriptive
statistics, univariate and multivariate normality checks, omega
reliability from ordinal confirmatory factor models, correlation
matrices in table format, and two-group or several-group comparisons
with effect sizes.
ThesiStats.author:
José Ventura-León [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-2996-4244>)

TrendSLR.title:
Estimating Trend, Velocity, and Acceleration from Sea Level
Records
TrendSLR.description:
Provides tools for analysing annual average ocean water level time series,
estimating mean sea level trends, velocities, and accelerations using Singular
Spectrum Analysis (SSA). The detailed methodology for resolving mean sea level
with improved temporal resolution follows Watson (2018)
"Improved Techniques to Estimate Mean Sea Level, Velocity and Acceleration from
Long Ocean Water Level Time Series to Augment Sea Level (and Climate Change)
Research" <https://unsworks.unsw.edu.au/entities/publication/5e835c87-aa0a-4457-807e-29d354e91d45>.
Additional methodological developments and applications are described in Watson (2020)
"Status of Mean Sea Level Rise around the USA" <doi:10.3390/geohazards2020005>
and Watson and Lim (2020) "An Update on the Status of Mean Sea Level Rise around
the Korean Peninsula" <doi:10.3390/atmos11111153>. Includes multiple gap-filling
methods for incomplete records, diagnostic tools for inspecting SSA components,
and plotting functions for generating publication-quality screen and file outputs.
TrendSLR.author: Phil Watson [aut, cre]

UMDA.title: Univariate Marginal Distribution Algorithm
UMDA.description: Implements the Univariate Marginal Distribution Algorithm (UMDA), an Estimation of Distribution Algorithm (EDA) for continuous optimization problems. The method iteratively selects the best individuals from a population, estimates an independent marginal probability distribution for each decision variable, and generates new candidate solutions by sampling from the estimated distributions. This process allows the probability model to adapt toward promising regions of the search space. The implementation supports normal, triangular, histogram-based, and uniform probability distributions, together with an optional explicit exploration strategy for the initialization of the population. The implemented explicit exploration strategy in this package is described in Salinas Gutierrez and Muñoz Zavala (2023) <doi:10.1016/j.asoc.2023.110230>.
UMDA.author:
Rogelio Salinas Gutiérrez [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1669-4460>),
Juan Alberto Dávila del Alto [aut, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0007-2798-6251>),
Jhon Daniel Aguilar Payares [aut, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0009-6509-4486>),
Jonathan Michell Jauregui Carranza [aut, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0005-2688-8065>),
Hiram Efraim Macias Ruelas [aut, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0009-3847-159X>),
Byron Axel Morales Gutiérrez [aut, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0006-3446-3830>),
María Fernanda Nieto Guerrero [aut, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0000-1738-1733>),
Manuel Alonso Segoviano Baltazar [aut, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0007-1494-7472>),
Pedro Abraham Montoya Calzada [aut, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0002-3497-210X>)

UlavalSSD.title: Quebec Data and Tools for Introductory Data Science
UlavalSSD.description:
Historical weather observations and food-establishment conviction
records from Quebec for teaching data import, missing values, exploratory
analysis and reproducible reporting. Includes bilingual prompts and feedback
for a penguin data-cleaning exercise, and an optional static R code-style
diagnostic based on 'lintr', as described by Hester and others (2025)
<doi:10.21105/joss.07240>. Data are distributed as fixed teaching snapshots
and require no network access during use.
UlavalSSD.author: Aurélien Nicosia [aut, cre]

VCFArrow.title:
Fast and Memory-Efficient Manipulation and Conversion of VCF
Files
VCFArrow.description:
Reads Variant Call Format (VCF) files into an S4 object whose
genotypes are stored on disk as an 'Apache Arrow' dataset and loaded
lazily, allowing large datasets to be processed with little memory.
Provides functions to filter variants and samples, subset and merge
datasets, compute summary statistics and diagnostic plots, write VCF
files, and convert data to input formats of population genetic and
phylogenetic software such as 'STRUCTURE', 'ADMIXTURE', 'PLINK',
'EIGENSTRAT', 'Arlequin', 'GENEPOP', 'BayeScan', 'TreeMix', 'SNAPP'
and 'adegenet'.
VCFArrow.author:
Tomas Hrbek [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-3239-7068>)

VasGBIF.title:
Fast and Easy Compilation of Vascular Plants Occurrence Records
from 'GBIF'
VasGBIF.description: 'GBIF' <https://www.gbif.org/> hosts over 500 million occurrence records of tracheophyte (vascular plants). However, dealing with them typically involves lots of workflows and time, posing significant challenges for researchers. To address these limitations, we present 'VasGBIF', a fast and easy 'R' package to parse and merge enormous tracheophyte records.
VasGBIF.author: Yuxuan Wang [aut, cre] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0009-0003-7817-748X>)

XSLmodels.title: Run and Optimize Cross-Situational Word Learning Models
XSLmodels.description:
A collection of cognitive models of cross-situational word
learning, together with methods and datasets for fitting and
cross-validating them against experimental and corpus data, and for
plotting the results.
XSLmodels.author:
George Kachergis [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-4153-4167>),
Mika Braginsky [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0001-9039-3220>),
Kevin Liang [aut]

acpbvar.title: Bayesian Structural VARs with Asymmetric Conjugate Priors
acpbvar.description:
Implements Bayesian estimation of structural Vector Autoregressions
in the asymmetric A-form of Chan (2022) <doi:10.3982/QE1381>, with an
asymmetric Minnesota prior whose own-lag and cross-lag hyperparameters
are selected by empirical Bayes via the closed-form marginal likelihood. Exact
equation-by-equation posterior simulation in the structural form
(independent Normal-Inverse-Gamma draws) provides posterior draws of
the reduced-form parameters; structural identification through sign
restrictions follows the algorithm of Rubio-Ramirez, Waggoner and Zha (2010)
<doi:10.1111/j.1467-937X.2009.00578.x>.
Impulse responses, posterior bands, and acceptance diagnostics are computed
from the accepted draws.
acpbvar.author: Federica Ursillo [aut, cre]

actisomni.title: Create Sleep Measures of Actigraphy and Activity Analysis
actisomni.description:
Estimates sleep from wrist accelerometry and epoch-level activity
data. Implements sleep-period-time guiders based on angle changes, posture,
least-active periods, sustained inactivity, low activity, and diary or
fixed time windows; combines guider windows with sustained-inactivity bouts
to produce sleep/wake labels and consensus estimates. Provides diary
helpers, and interfaces to the 'asleep' and 'sleeper' machine-learning
estimators. The angle-based and
sustained-inactivity methods are described by van Hees et al. (2015)
<doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0142533> and van Hees et al. (2018)
<doi:10.1038/s41598-018-31266-z>; the model estimators are described by
Yuan et al. (2024) <doi:10.1038/s41746-024-01065-0> and
Sundararajan et al. (2021) <doi:10.1038/s41598-020-79217-x>.
actisomni.author:
John Muschelli [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-6469-1750>)

actiplot.title: Plotting Minute-Level Activity Data
actiplot.description:
Provides 'ggplot2' plots for minute-level activity data,
including step counts and activity counts. Time series can be displayed
over the full recording period or aligned by time of day and
faceted into one row per date.  Includes example activity data
described by Chadwell et al. (2019) <doi:10.1038/s41597-019-0211-6>.
actiplot.author:
John Muschelli [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-6469-1750>)

actuarialfitdist.title: Actuarial Severity Fitting with Limits and Deductibles
actuarialfitdist.description:
Fits actuarial claim severity distributions to ground-up loss data while
accounting for deductible truncation, policy-limit censoring, observation weights,
optional severity scaling variables, and fixed parameters. Supports single-family
and spliced body-tail models, candidate-model comparison, limited expected values,
loss elimination ratios, increased limits factors, deductible and limit rating
factors, valuation or depreciation adjustments, simulation, diagnostics, and
uncertainty estimation. The package is designed for property and casualty
actuarial applications in which analysts fit ground-up severity and translate the
fitted distribution into pricing factors for limits, deductibles, and valuation
provisions. For background on statistical severity modeling, see Klugman,
Panjer, and Willmot (2019, ISBN:9781119523789),
"Loss Models: From Data to Decisions", 5th edition.
actuarialfitdist.author: Greg Sollenberger [aut, cre, cph]

adlaplace.title: Laplace Approximations Using Automatic Differentiation
adlaplace.description:
Computes Laplace-approximate maximum likelihood for hierarchical
and latent Gaussian models. A formula interface specifies observation
densities (e.g. Gaussian, negative Binomial), fixed effects, and random
terms (independent effects, smoothing terms). Customized response
distributions and models for random effects can be specified through a
low-level interface or by writing interoperable packages. Derivatives
are computed using automatic differentiation with 'CppAD', and used in
trust region optimization to find modes of random effects. Derivatives
of the Laplace approximation of the log-likelihood are computed using
third order contractions and is compatible with custom atomics. The
approach follows Kristensen, Nielsen, Berg, Skaug, and Bell (2016)
<doi:10.18637/jss.v070.i05>.
adlaplace.author: Patrick Brown [aut, cre, cph]

aersn.title:
Affine-Equivariant Adjusted-Range Self-Normalization for
Time-Series Inference
aersn.description:
Tuning-free inference on fixed-dimensional parameters of
dependent time series using affine-equivariant adjusted-range
self-normalization. The centered partial-sum path of estimated
influence contributions is normalized by its increment hull, the
convex hull of all path increments. The gauge of the hull provides
an asymptotically pivotal test statistic and an affine-equivariant
confidence region without estimating the long-run covariance matrix,
and its support function gives simultaneous confidence intervals for
linear contrasts. For a single parameter the construction reduces
exactly to adjusted-range self-normalization, whose limiting
distribution is available in closed form. The Brownian reference law
is simulated on a grid matched to the sample size or a supplied
common variance-accumulation profile; inference for dependent
observations remains asymptotic. Five further methods are provided
for comparison on the same estimate and influence contributions:
componentwise adjusted ranges after lag-zero partial prewhitening,
quadratic self-normalization following Shao (2010)
<doi:10.1111/j.1467-9868.2009.00737.x>, kernel long-run covariance
estimation with automatic bandwidth selection following Andrews
(1991) <doi:10.2307/2938229> and Newey and West (1994)
<doi:10.2307/2297912>, Bartlett fixed-b inference following Kiefer
and Vogelsang (2005) <doi:10.1017/S0266466605050565>, and the
equal-weighted cosine method of Lazarus, Lewis, Stock and Watson
(2018) <doi:10.1080/07350015.2018.1506926>. Model interfaces are
provided for sample means, linear regression, smooth generalized
method of moments, and conditional likelihood scores; other
estimators are handled through user-supplied influence
contributions. The methods follow Hong, Lin, Linton, Newey and Sun
(2026), Cambridge Working Papers in Economics No. 2678
<https://www.janeway.econ.cam.ac.uk/publication/affine-equivariant-adjusted-range-self-normalization>
and, for the scalar case, Hong, Linton,
McCabe, Sun and Wang (2024) <doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2023.105603>.
aersn.author:
Yongmiao Hong [aut],
Zhuo Lin [aut],
Oliver Linton [aut],
Whitney K. Newey [aut],
Jiajing Sun [aut, cre]

agriEquity.title: Equity and Sustainability Assessment of Agricultural Subsidies
agriEquity.description:
An integrated framework for evaluating whether agricultural
support measures reach smallholders, women farmers and resource-poor
regions, and at what productivity and environmental cost. It provides
survey-weighted benefit incidence analysis by landholding class, gender,
region or income quantile; concentration, Kakwani and Reynolds-Smolensky
progressivity measures (Kakwani, 1977) <doi:10.2307/2230485> with
bootstrap confidence intervals; multi-dimensional equity scorecards with
parity ratios and Theil decomposition of benefit inequality; effects of
subsidies on income inequality and Foster-Greer-Thorbecke poverty
(Foster, Greer and Thorbecke, 1984) <doi:10.2307/1913475>;
budget-neutral reallocation of a subsidy budget under alternative
allocation rules, including a welfare-optimal allocation that combines
diminishing productivity returns, Atkinson (1970)
<doi:10.1016/0022-0531(70)90039-6> inequality aversion and
environmental damage costs; and productivity-equity-sustainability
trade-off frontiers. Simulated farm-household data illustrate the
workflow.
agriEquity.author: Anbukkani Perumal [aut, cre, cph]

agriTradeRisk.title: Agricultural Export Competitiveness and Risk Analysis
agriTradeRisk.description:
An integrated and reproducible workflow for analysing the
competitiveness and risk of agricultural and horticultural exports. It
measures destination and product concentration (Herfindahl-Hirschman,
entropy and equivalent-number indices), revealed comparative advantage
(Balassa, 1965) <doi:10.1111/j.1467-9957.1965.tb00050.x> and its
symmetric form, relative unit values, and constant market share
decomposition of export growth. It tests vertical price transmission
between export and domestic prices with Engle-Granger cointegration
(Engle and Granger, 1987) <doi:10.2307/1913236> using MacKinnon (2010)
critical values and symmetric or asymmetric error correction models. It
quantifies exchange-rate exposure of a multi-currency export portfolio
(volatility, diversification ratio, risk contributions and value at
risk), screens destination markets with composite entry-risk scores,
and identifies risk-efficient destination mixes by mean-variance
portfolio optimisation (Markowitz, 1952) <doi:10.2307/2975974>.
Simulated example data for Indian mango, grape, pomegranate and
processed horticultural exports illustrate the workflow.
agriTradeRisk.author: Anbukkani Perumal [aut, cre, cph]

aidR.title: Reading and Standardizing Automated Insulin Delivery Data
aidR.description:
Parses the native exports of several automated insulin delivery
(AID) platforms into a common, platform-independent format for continuous
glucose monitoring (CGM), basal, bolus, carbohydrate, and self-monitored
blood glucose (SMBG) data. Additional functions check completeness, filter,
produce visualizations, and convert the data to other formats.
aidR.author:
Madleina Caduff [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-8941-4274>),
Aritz Lizoain [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0009-0004-5516-2573>),
Diabetes Center Berne (DCB) [cph, fnd]

aidatabroker.title: Read Open Data on the AI Training Data Market
aidatabroker.description:
Downloads the open datasets published by 'AIData.Broker' on the
market for AI training data: public prices, licensing deals, buyers,
vendors, lawsuits and related tables, each row with its source, from
<https://aidata.broker/datasets>. The data are licensed CC BY 4.0.
aidatabroker.author: Yuma Heymans [aut, cre]

ambs.title: Bayesian Alpha-Mixture Survival Models
ambs.description:
Implements Bayesian estimation for alpha-mixture survival models
with right-censored data. Weibull-Weibull, Gamma-Weibull, and
Lognormal-Lognormal component specifications are supported, with all
component parameters treated as unknown. The package provides
identifiability handling, adaptive Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling,
convergence diagnostics, model comparison criteria, and posterior
survival, hazard, and density estimation. The methodology extends the
framework described by Luan et al. (2026) <doi:10.3390/math14101772>.
Danish Ezwan, David Goldberg, and Ting Huang contributed equally to the
package.
ambs.author:
Zhexuan Yang [aut, cre],
Danish Ezwan [ctb],
David Goldberg [ctb],
Ting Huang [ctb]

anotherSAS7bdat.title: Read 'SAS' Data in Chunks and Convert to 'Parquet'
anotherSAS7bdat.description:
Reads 'SAS' 'sas7bdat' files through a persistent native reader.
Processes configurable chunks without reopening the input or restarting
the parser between chunks. Supports uncompressed, run-length encoded,
and Ross Data Compression data through the bundled 'ReadStat' library.
Also streams native decoded batches directly to 'Parquet' through the
'Arrow' C Data Interface and the optional 'arrow' package, without
constructing R data frames.
anotherSAS7bdat.author:
Jianyun Wu [aut, cre],
Evan Miller [aut, cph] (Author of included ReadStat code)

apsimwise.title: Unified Access to the APSIMWISE Ecosystem
apsimwise.description:
Provides a unified interface to R packages supporting the
Agricultural Production Systems sIMulator (APSIM), crop modelling,
weather analysis, and agricultural decision support. It simplifies
installation and loading of related packages and provides consistent
user-facing functions across multiple crop types.
apsimwise.author: Bangyou Zheng [aut, cre]

aquats.title: Robust Ecological and Fisheries Data Analysis and Visualization
aquats.description:
A comprehensive statistical and visualization toolkit tailored
for observational data in fisheries science and aquatic ecology. Provides
streamlined workflows for univariate and factorial analysis of variance
(ANOVA), analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), multivariate analysis of
variance (MANOVA), permutational multivariate analysis of variance
(PERMANOVA), similarity percentages (SIMPER), generalized linear models,
non-linear morphometric regressions, two-group hypothesis testing, and
chi-square tests. Features multivariate ordination methods including
non-metric multidimensional scaling (NMDS), principal component analysis
(PCA), redundancy analysis (RDA), distance-based redundancy analysis
(db-RDA), and hierarchical cluster dendrograms. Computes alpha diversity
metrics, species accumulation curves, water quality index (WQI) values,
heavy metal ecotoxicological contamination indices, correlation heatmaps,
and Mantel test network linkages. Offers specialized environmental
visualizations including Sankey diagrams, Likert plots, circular bar
charts, and longitudinal time-series with uncertainty ribbons.
Methodological formulations for multivariate permutation tests follow
Anderson (2001) <doi:10.1111/j.1442-9993.2001.01070.pp.x>. Ecological
community dissimilarity transformations follow Legendre and Gallagher
(2001) <doi:10.1007/s004420100716>, and ecotoxicological contamination
index models follow Tomlinson et al. (1980) <doi:10.1007/BF02414780>.
aquats.author:
Ataher Ali [aut, cre] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0009-0008-8780-0903>),
Mohammed Shahidul Alam [aut] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-2740-5908>)

aradR.title: Modern R Client and Toolkit for the Czech National Bank ARAD API
aradR.description:
Provides a reliability-first interface to the public Czech National Bank
ARAD API for discovering indicators, browsing human-readable metadata,
retrieving and validating time series, working with dimensions and
snapshots, reshaping data, and building reproducible data workflows. The
package is designed for robust handling of long requests, parsing
diagnostics, missing values, retries, caching, and automated tests.
aradR.author:
Simona Malovana [aut, cre],
Petr Bouchal [ctb] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0471-716X>)

ardea.title: Infrastructure for Interacting with GPUs
ardea.description: Compiling, managing, and dispatching functions to GPUs. Will compile tooling for successfully detected frameworks, currently limited to: 'OpenCL' (<https://www.khronos.org/opencl/resources>), 'CUDA' (<https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/>), and 'Metal' (<https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal>).
ardea.author:
Nicholas Cooley [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-6029-304X>)

awscrt.title: Hardware-Accelerated 'CRC Checksums' from the AWS Common Runtime
awscrt.description:
Computes 'CRC32', 'CRC32C' and 'CRC64NVME' 'checksums' using the
'aws-checksums' library from the 'AWS' Common Runtime, with runtime
dispatch to hardware instructions ('SSE4.2', 'PCLMULQDQ', 'AVX-512',
'ARMv8' 'CRC' and 'PMULL') and a portable software fallback.
awscrt.author:
Dyfan Jones [aut, cre],
Amazon.com, Inc. or its affiliates [cph] (Author of the bundled
aws-checksums and aws-c-common libraries)

b3gbi.title: General Biodiversity Indicators for Biodiversity Data Cubes
b3gbi.description:
Calculate general biodiversity indicators from species
occurrence cubes, such as those produced by the 'GBIF' (Global
Biodiversity Information Facility) occurrence cube service
<https://techdocs.gbif.org/en/data-use/data-cubes>. Indicators include
observed and coverage-based rarefied species richness and Hill numbers
(via 'iNEXT'), evenness, rarity, taxonomic distinctness, occupancy,
turnover and sample completeness, and can be calculated over time (time
series) or space (maps), with bootstrap confidence intervals. Cubes using
the EEA reference grid, MGRS, the extended quarter-degree grid (EQDGC) or
ISEA3H grids are supported. For details see Dove (2026)
<doi:10.21105/joss.10963>.
b3gbi.author:
Shawn Dove [aut, cre] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0001-9465-5638>),
Ward Langeraert [ctb] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-5900-8109>),
Peter Desmet [ctb] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-8442-8025>),
University of Giessen [cph],
European Union [fnd] (Horizon Europe Research and Innovation Programme,
grant 101059592)

ballast.title: Stress-Test a Pre-Specified Mixed Model for Repeated Measures
ballast.description:
Refits one pre-specified mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM)
under families of data and analytic perturbations (covariance structure,
degrees-of-freedom method and variance estimator, covariate set, analysis
population, alternative analysis data sets, leave-one-out deletions, crossed
specification grids, re-randomisation tests, delta-adjusted and
reference-based multiple imputation, and alternative estimators) and judges
every refit against the pre-specified estimate, confidence interval and
p-value. Classifies the result as robust, sensitive or fragile, with a
separate flag for marginal significance, and estimates by simulation the
probability that a planned design gives a significant and robust result.
Fitting uses 'mmrm' (Sabanes Bove et al., 2024,
<https://openpharma.github.io/mmrm/>) with 'SAS' 'PROC MIXED' conventions
for the least-squares-mean contrast,
Kenward-Roger adjustment and the corrected Akaike criterion. Reference-based
multiple imputation follows Carpenter, Roger and Kenward (2013)
<doi:10.1080/10543406.2013.834911> and was checked against 'rbmi'
(Gower-Page, Noci and Wolbers, 2022) <doi:10.21105/joss.04251>.
ballast.author:
Adam Sullivan [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-9429-3611>),
Nathan Hogan [ctb] (validation of the SAS reference results),
Capricor Therapeutics [fnd]

bartisan.title: Generalized Bayesian Additive Regression Trees
bartisan.description:
Fits Bayesian additive regression trees (BART) models for
likelihoods outside the conditionally conjugate Gaussian case, using the
Laplace-approximation reversible-jump sampler of Linero (2025)
<doi:10.1080/01621459.2024.2337156>. Supported response families include
Gaussian, binomial, Poisson, negative binomial, gamma, beta, ordered beta,
ordinal (cumulative link), multinomial, zero-inflated counts, a Tweedie
compound Poisson for a non-negative response with a point mass at zero,
accelerated failure time and proportional hazards models for right-censored
survival data, location-scale regression, and a Dirichlet process mixture
for the error distribution. Decision rules may be hard, as in standard BART, or
soft, as in the SoftBart model of Linero and Yang (2018)
<doi:10.1111/rssb.12293>, which yields smoother fits. The interface follows
that of glm(), so that a model is specified with a formula, a data frame,
and a family.
bartisan.author:
Noah Greifer [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-3067-7154>),
Antonio R. Linero [ctb, cph] (Author of FlexBart, the reference
implementation of Linero (2025), from which the MCMC engine is
adapted)

betbetter.title: Access the Bet Better Open Sports Model API
betbetter.description:
Retrieves published statistical model estimates for upcoming
sporting fixtures from the Bet Better open API, covering Australian
rules football, baseball, basketball, American football, ice hockey,
association football, tennis and mixed martial arts. For each rated
selection the interface returns the model's estimated probability that
the selection occurs, together with the decimal odds implied by that
probability. No registration or authentication is required. Bookmaker
prices are not published by the API and are therefore not available
through this package.
betbetter.author: Edward Glush [aut, cre]

bmetapred.title: Bayesian Meta-Prediction in the Presence of Prediction Error
bmetapred.description:
Fits pseudo-Bayesian Model Averaging (pBMA) and Bayesian Stacking ensembles of linear
meta-models while explicitly accounting for the prediction errors of the individual models,
building on the Bayesian Stacking of predictive distributions framework of Yao et al. (2018) <doi:10.1214/17-BA1091>.
When native uncertainty estimates are unavailable, it provides tools to estimate heteroscedastic
errors via Local Polynomial Regression (LOESS). The meta-model space is explored using exhaustive
search, a Markov Chain Monte Carlo Model Composition (MC3) algorithm following Madigan and
Raftery (1994) <doi:10.1080/01621459.1994.10476894> when pBMA is selected, or a tabu-guided heuristic search with parallel tempering when bayesian stacking is selected, all powered by 'brms' (Bürkner, 2017
<doi:10.18637/jss.v080.i01>).
bmetapred.author:
Jorge Piqueras Marqués [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-6812-2106>),
Anabel Forte Deltell [aut] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-9534-1817>),
Joaquin Martinez Minaya [ctb] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1016-8734>)

bones.title: Content-Shaped Loading Placeholders for 'shiny' Outputs
bones.description:
Shows a grey placeholder in the shape of the content while a
'shiny' output loads, in place of a spinner. The user can thus see what
is coming, and not only that something happens. The shape comes from
the type of the output. The placeholder keeps the space of the content,
so the page does not move when the content arrives. When an output
calculates again, the old content stays on the screen, dimmed, and a
placeholder does not replace it.
bones.author: Tanmay Chanda [aut, cre, cph]

boltzrosen.title: Boltzmann-Rosenbrock Distribution and Associated Copula
boltzrosen.description: Provides the probability density function, cumulative distribution function, quantile function, and random sample generation for the Boltzmann-Rosenbrock distribution. The package also includes functions for the marginal distributions of X and Y, the mutual information between the two components, and the copula associated with the distribution, including its density, distribution function, and sampling routines. The use of Boltzmann distribution in objective functions, such as the Rosenbrock function, is described in Segovia-Domínguez, I., Valdez, S.I. and Hernández-Aguirre, A. (2014) <doi:10.5220/0005079902510258>.
boltzrosen.author:
Rogelio Salinas Gutiérrez [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1669-4460>),
Jhon Daniel Aguilar Payares [aut, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0009-6509-4486>),
Alejandro Fausto Cortés Salinas [aut, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0000-2536-2663>),
Sofía Isabel Soledad Limón [aut, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0003-5743-5689>),
Rogelio Emiliano Salinas Gutiérrez [aut, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0008-4581-5656>),
Juan Pablo Salinas Muñoz [aut, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0005-4544-1584>),
Pedro Abraham Montoya Calzada [aut, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0002-3497-210X>)

boundedHill.title: Bayesian Logistic Regression with Lower and Upper Asymptotes
boundedHill.description: Fits Bayesian logistic regression models in which the success probability rises or falls between a lower and an upper asymptote instead of between 0 and 1, for binomial outcomes including binary data. The success probability equals the lower asymptote plus the difference between the two asymptotes multiplied by the logistic function of a linear predictor. The lower and upper asymptotes can be either estimated or fixed. With a single predictor such as log dose, this is the four-parameter logistic (Hill) model. Posterior computation is a full Gibbs sampler that requires no tuning.
boundedHill.author:
Minji Lee [aut, cre, cph],
Chang Hyeong Lee [aut, cph],
Ryung S. Kim [aut, cph]

brapiR2.title:
A Tidyverse-Native Client for the 'BrAPI' v2 (Breeding API)
Specification
brapiR2.description:
Provides pipe-friendly, stateless read access to the Breeding
API ('BrAPI') v2.1 specification, an open community standard for plant
breeding data interchange maintained by the BrAPI project
<https://brapi.org>. Wraps 32 of the 37 'BrAPI' v2.1 entities across all
four modules, Core, Germplasm, Phenotyping, and Genotyping, covering 49
of the specification's 138 retrieval ('GET' and search) endpoints and
returning tidy tibbles ready for analysis. Write and update endpoints
are out of scope by design. Features include automatic pagination, async
search handling, response caching, parallel batch fetching, and
convenience functions for genomic selection workflows (e.g. dosage
matrix extraction). Designed for plant breeders and bioinformaticians
who need programmatic access to plant breeding databases that
implement the 'BrAPI' v2 specification.
brapiR2.author:
Joash Joshua Ayo [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0007-1642-0172>),
David Waring [rev] (David reviewed the package (v. 0.1.0) for rOpenSci,
see <https://github.com/ropensci/software-review/issues/792>),
Jenna Hershberger [rev] (Jenna reviewed the package (v. 0.1.0) for
rOpenSci, see
<https://github.com/ropensci/software-review/issues/792>)

brochure.title: Multipage 'Shiny' Apps
brochure.description:
Build natively multi-page 'Shiny' applications, serving
content on several endpoints instead of a single page. Pages are
declared with their own user interface and server function and are
dispatched by URL with 'routr', including parameterised routes.
Redirections, request and response middleware, and helpers to read and
set cookies are also provided.
brochure.author:
Colin Fay [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-7343-1846>)

brvmr.title: Free Access to BRVM Stock Market Data
brvmr.description:
Light client to read prices, indices and dividends of the
Bourse Regionale des Valeurs Mobilieres (BRVM, West African stock
exchange) from the public mirror 'harzat/brvm-data-public' of BRVMetrics.
The package ships no data: it is downloaded at call time. Data remain the
property of their sources (BRVM, SikaFinance, RicheBourse), with no
guarantee of accuracy. This is not investment advice.
brvmr.author: Zabaly Noumoutchè [aut, cre] (alias Harzat)

cafast.title: Fast Companions to the 'CAs' Package for Covering Arrays
cafast.description:
Compiled implementations and generalizations of selected
functions of the 'CAs' package by Ulrike Groemping for covering
arrays. The package provides a C version of the search for the
largest set of rows that can be made constant by permuting symbols,
the power construction of Colbourn and Torres-Jimenez (2010)
<doi:10.1090/conm/523/10309> for any strength, number of columns and
number of levels, a counting kernel that tabulates value tuples for
every set of t columns, and fast versions of the flexible-value tools
and of the randomized post-optimization of Nayeri, Colbourn and
Konjevod (2013) <doi:10.1016/j.ejc.2012.07.017>. Each function was
tested against its 'CAs' counterpart, and the remaining differences
are documented.
cafast.author: Christopher Smolen [aut, cre]

cam2model.title: Preprocessing Trap Camera Data for Machine Learning Models
cam2model.description:
Provides tools for preprocessing camera trap
image data to prepare it for training machine learning models. It automates tasks
such as extracting EXIF metadata, processing and analyzing image attributes,
selecting relevant images (e.g., daytime photos), sampling subsets, and managing
file organization. These features streamline the workflow for ecological research
and wildlife monitoring projects. Additionally, the package includes tools for
generating exploratory visualizations and creating annotation datasets.
cam2model.author:
Edlin Guerra-Castro [aut, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-3529-4507>),
Arturo Sanchez-Porras [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1691-286X>)

camplet.title: Seasonal Adjustment via the CAMPLET Method
camplet.description:
Seasonal adjustment with CAMPLET (Abeln and Jacobs (2023)
<doi:10.1007/978-3-031-22845-2>), a transparent, adaptive method that
corrects for seasonality and outliers via arithmetic-progression
updates, without model identification or optimisation, and without
revising earlier adjusted values when new observations arrive. A pure R
port of the original 'Excel' 'VBA' implementation, validated against
its output.
camplet.author:
Barend Abeln [aut] (CAMPLET method and original VBA implementation),
Herbert Kruitbosch [aut, cre]

caplime.title: Conic Adaptive Piecewise Local Explanations
caplime.description:
Provides educational, base-R implementations of a ridge-penalized
piecewise hinge regression model and local surrogate explanations for
numerical prediction functions. Includes simplified variants inspired by
local interpretable model-agnostic explanations (LIME) and a simplified
bandwidth selection variant (OPTILIME), plus exploratory stability diagnostics.
caplime.author:
Nurgül Gökgöz Küçüksakallı [aut, cre] (affiliation: Department of
Biomedical Engineering, Middle East Technical University),
Vilda Purutçuoğlu [aut] (affiliation: Department of Statistics, Middle
East Technical University)

caples.title: Fast, Plain-English Readouts for A/B/n Tests
caples.description:
Sizes and reads out A/B/n tests on conversion rates in a few
function calls. Supports unequal traffic splits, multiple treatment arms
with multiplicity correction, sample ratio mismatch checks, achieved
minimum detectable effects, and plain-English summaries.
caples.author: Robin Mahachi [aut, cre]

catchmentACS.title: Isochrone-Based Area-Weighted ACS Aggregation
catchmentACS.description:
Computes American Community Survey (ACS) estimates for the
area within a given drive time of each of a set of points, such as the
locations of pre-kindergarten classrooms. Such an area is called an
isochrone. The drive-time areas come from a routing service, either the
'Open Source Routing Machine' ('OSRM', <https://project-osrm.org/>) or
'openrouteservice' (<https://openrouteservice.org/>), and the ACS 5-year
estimates of census tracts come from the Census Bureau
(<https://www.census.gov/data/developers.html>) through the 'tidycensus'
package, one state at a time. The tracts that
overlap an area are combined by area weighting, which uses two weights:
the share of each tract's area that lies inside, for counts and rates,
and each tract's share of the overlapping area, for the medians and
per-person values of three ACS tables (median household income, median
home value, and per capita income). A median or per-person value from
any other table is added up like a count. Counts, medians, per-person
values, and five rates are returned with a margin of error at a chosen
confidence level, 90 percent by default, and with a record of the
settings, inputs, and package versions behind the run. The five rates
are the poverty rate, the shares of households receiving Supplemental
Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits and Supplemental Security
Income, the unemployment rate, and the labor force participation rate.
The margins of error of counts and rates use the approximation formulas
in chapter 8 of U.S. Census Bureau (2020) "Understanding and Using
American Community Survey Data: What All Data Users Need to Know"
<https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/library/handbooks/general.html>.
For a count the formula for a sum is applied to the weighted tract
estimates, with the weights treated as fixed. For a rate the default is
the formula for a ratio. Its margin of error is at least as wide as that
of the formula for a proportion, which the handbook gives for ratios
whose numerator is part of the denominator, as it is in all five rates.
The margins of error of medians and per-person values are an
approximation made by the package.
catchmentACS.author:
JoonHo Lee [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4019-8703>)

causaljudgment.title: Computational Models of Causal Judgment
causaljudgment.description:
Provides computational implementations of models of causal judgment, including the Counterfactual Effect Size (CES) model of Quillien and Lucas (2023) <doi:10.1037/rev0000428>
