and the Necessity-Sufficiency (NS) model of Icard, Kominsky and Knobe (2017) <doi:10.1016/j.cognition.2017.01.010>.
The package represents causal structures as binary Structural Causal Models and
analytically computes causal judgments from counterfactual probability distributions.
causaljudgment.author: Tadeg Quillien [aut, cre]

ccva.title:
Climate Change Vulnerability Assessment with Constrained Latent
Models
ccva.description:
A general framework for climate change vulnerability assessment
(CCVA) of any species and any dataset. Variables are tagged as exposure,
sensitivity or adaptive capacity; each component is computed from its own
predictors by a chosen method; and the three components are combined into
vulnerability. Methods range from the rule-based framework of Foden et
al. (2013) <doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0065427> and the conventional
weighted index of Ofori et al. (2017) <doi:10.1038/s41598-017-13245-y>
to shape-constrained additive models ('scam'), latent-variable
structural equation models
('lavaan') in which vulnerability is inferred from observable proxies,
and penalised regression ('glmnet') for high-dimensional predictors.
Missing traits and outcomes are handled by full-information maximum
likelihood.
Ecological knowledge enters as explicit constraints on predictors, on
each component's role and on the links between components. Diagnostics,
validation against observed outcomes, bootstrap and weight-based
uncertainty, calibrated risk predictions and plots for every step are
included.
ccva.author: Hassan Doosti [aut, cre, cph] (affiliation: Macquarie University)

cdiscdata.title: Versioned CDISC Standards Reference Data
cdiscdata.description:
Provides versioned reference data for the standards of the
Clinical Data Interchange Standards Consortium (CDISC)
<https://www.cdisc.org/standards>: the CDISC Controlled Terminology (CT)
for the Study Data Tabulation Model (SDTM) and the Analysis Data Model
(ADaM); variable metadata for the SDTM model and for the families of the
SDTM Implementation Guide (SDTMIG), the Standard for Exchange of
Nonclinical Data Implementation Guide (SENDIG), and the ADaM
Implementation Guide (ADaMIG); the Clinical Data Acquisition Standards
Harmonization (CDASH) model and implementation guide; the Questionnaires,
Ratings, and Scales (QRS) supplements; and the Define-XML schemas, written
in the Extensible Markup Language (XML) Schema Definition (XSD) language,
with Extensible Stylesheet Language Transformations (XSLT) stylesheets
for them. A validity-date design stores every historical CT version
compactly, without duplicating rows. Intended as a shared data
dependency for pharmaverse-aligned packages <https://pharmaverse.org>.
cdiscdata.author:
Bill Denney [aut, cre] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-5759-428X>),
Clinical Data Interchange Standards Consortium (CDISC) [cph]
(Define-XML schema files in inst/extdata/schema (MIT License)),
Lex Jansen [cph] (Define-XML stylesheets in inst/extdata/stylesheet
(MIT License)),
National Cancer Institute Enterprise Vocabulary Services [dtc] (CDISC
Controlled Terminology (public domain))

cdtr.title: Constrained Delaunay Triangulation with Refinement
cdtr.description:
Binding to the 'CDT' header-only C++ library: constrained and
conforming Delaunay triangulation, Ruppert refinement by area or minimum
angle (Ruppert, 1995, <doi:10.1006/jagm.1995.1021>), resolution of crossing
constraints, and topological region depth per triangle. Aimed at replacing
'RTriangle' in 'anglr'.
cdtr.author:
Michael Sumner [aut, cre],
Leica Geosystems Technology AB [cph] (Copyright holder of the bundled
'CDT' C++ library),
CDT Contributors [ctb, cph] ('CDT' C++ library,
https://github.com/artem-ogre/CDT),
William C. Lenthe [ctb, cph] (Robust geometric predicates
(predicates.h))

cellsynth.title: Cell-Wise Synthetic Copies of De-Identified Tables
cellsynth.description:
Turns de-identified tables ('Excel' workbooks or delimited
text files) into synthetic counterparts with the same layout, the same
identifiers and the same data-entry quirks. Every non-identifier cell,
missingness included, is censored once per sweep and redrawn by copying
the raw value of a donor drawn from a classification and regression
tree leaf fitted on the rest of the table, in the spirit of the
sequential tree-based synthesis of Reiter (2005) "Using CART to
generate partially synthetic public use microdata", Journal of Official
Statistics 21(3):441-462, and Nowok, Raab and Dibben (2016)
<doi:10.18637/jss.v074.i11>. Identifiers are kept so that tables stay
joinable, and columns of other tables can condition the synthesis so
cross-table associations survive a later join. Synthetic copies are
intended for developing and testing analysis code; they are not an
anonymisation method.
cellsynth.author: Marton Kiss [aut, cre]

censusindia.title: Census of India Data, 1901-2011, with Boundaries and Projections
censusindia.description:
Tables from every decennial Census of India from 1901 to 2011:
population time series, Primary Census Abstracts at state, district and
sub-district level, mother tongue tables, Scheduled Caste and
Scheduled Tribe populations, and the 1931 caste tables by religion,
together with Ministry of Health and Family Welfare population
projections to 2036. Historical series are drawn
from Jolad and Singh (2026) <doi:10.7910/DVN/ON8CP8>. Census variables
can be returned with state or district boundaries of the matching
census year attached for mapping. Boundary files and the largest
village-level tables are downloaded on first use and cached locally.
censusindia.author:
Saket Choudhary [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-5202-7633>)

cepip.title: Cell Explanatory Power with Inflection Point (CEP-IP) with CMRF
cepip.description:
Implements the cell explanatory power with inflection point
(CEP-IP) framework for single-cell co-expression analysis. A generalized
additive model (GAM) fitted by restricted maximum likelihood (REML) with
a penalized residual sum of squares (PRSS) search over the basis
dimension relates a gene of interest to the mean of its partner genes.
Cells are ranked by their explanatory power, and the inflection point is
the first negative-to-positive zero crossing of a residual GAM. Optional
extensions are the Spearman-Kendall cell-level score (SKCS) and the
copula monotone recovery filter (CMRF), which recovers cells near the
module through a tolerance band and a repeated stratified k-fold
cross-validation gate. Downstream helpers give per-donor module
fractions, paired donor-level differential expression and donor-level
association models. CEP-IP is described in Wong (2026)
<doi:10.1016/j.cmpb.2026.109372>.
cepip.author:
Kah Keng Wong [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-7359-6202>)

charr.title: String Processing Reimagined for 'ALTREP' Strings
charr.description:
An experimental fork of 'stringr'. The functions and semantics
are the same, apart from differences between 'ICU' and Unicode versions,
but everything is optimized around 'ALTREP' strings (custom
high-performance string storage), allowing for faster and more efficient
operation.
charr.author:
Travers Ching [aut, cre, cph],
Hadley Wickham [ctb, cph] (Author of stringr, of which charr is a fork),
Posit Software, PBC [ctb, cph] (Copyright holder of stringr),
Unicode, Inc. and others [ctb, cph] (ICU4C source code and data
(Unicode License v3)),
Marek Gagolewski [ctb, cph] (Author of stringi; stringi implementation
used by charr),
R Consortium [fnd] (Infrastructure Steering Committee grant: Universal
ALTREP Interoperability for Strings)

citesperu.title: Peruvian Species Checklists from CITES Publications
citesperu.description:
Provides tools and official datasets for working with Peruvian fauna
and flora checklists published by the Ministry of the Environment (MINAM)
under the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of
Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES). Includes official datasets for fauna (2018,
2019, 2023) and flora (2018), with tools for reproducible data preparation,
checklist queries, scientific name matching and summaries by appendix
and taxonomic group.
citesperu.author:
Paul E. Santos Andrade [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-6635-0375>)

citydistR.title: City-Adaptive Distance Modelling Utilities
citydistR.description:
Tools for distribution-aware and city-adaptive analysis of
learning-based road-network distance estimates. Provides detour-factor
diagnostics, a Topological Predictability Index, upper-tail summaries,
modular robust losses, hybrid objective components, adaptive validation
weights, and multi-criteria model evaluation. The functions are designed
as reusable building blocks rather than a fixed model specification.
citydistR.author: Elif Kozan [aut, cre, cph]

cldreducer.title: Reduce Compact Letter Displays
cldreducer.description:
Reduces compact letter displays (CLDs) of all pairwise
comparisons. A CLD gives two groups a common letter exactly when they are
not significantly different. The package finds a display with the fewest
letter assignments that keeps every one of these relationships. This is the
assignment-minimum clique covering problem of Ennis, Fayle, and Ennis
(2012) <doi:10.1145/2133803.2275596>, solved as a mixed-integer linear
program with 'HiGHS'. Among the displays with the fewest assignments, it
returns one fixed canonical display, so the result does not depend on the
solver. The package includes the wheat yield example of Piepho (2004)
<doi:10.1198/1061860043515>.
cldreducer.author:
John Ennis [aut, cre],
Aigora [cph, fnd]

climabr.title: Interface for Accessing Weather Data from Climatempo
climabr.description: Provides functions for downloading meteorological data from the CLIMATEMPO (<https://www.climatempo.com.br/>) web platform through web scraping, designed for ecological and environmental analyses.
climabr.author:
Jhonatan Rafael Zárate-Salazar [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-9251-5340>),
Omar E. Benites-Alfaro [ctb] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-6852-9598>),
Eduardo V. da Silva Oliveira [ctb] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-4858-3930>),
Sidney F. Gouveia [ctb] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-4941-7440>)

cndplantanalysis.title: Compositional Nutrient Diagnosis for Plant Tissue Analysis
cndplantanalysis.description:
Provides an implementation of Compositional Nutrient Diagnosis (CND) for plant tissue tests.
Computes scale invariant simplex filling values(Rd), row-centered log-ratios (CLR), iterative database
partitioning via Cate-Nelson procedures, cubic polynomial regression of cumulative variance ratio functions to
determine inflection point yield cutoffs, critical CND nutrient imbalance thresholds (r^2) using the chi-square distribution,
diagnostic standardized indices (Ix) and automated Cate Nelson scatter partitioning. Includes linear, non-linear, cumulative variance,
chi-square and quadrant plotting functions.Methodology and theoretical frameworks are grounded in Parent and Dafir (1992)
<doi:10.21273/JASHS.117.2.239> and Khiari et al. (2001) <doi:10.2134/agronj2001.934802x>.
cndplantanalysis.author:
Blesson B. Varghese [aut, cre],
Rohith A K [aut],
Anjali S. [aut],
Aliya Shirin K S [aut],
Hilal Mohamed [aut]

coiR.title: Analysis of Canopy Openness Index from Fisheye Images
coiR.description:
Tools to estimate the Canopy Openness Index (COI) from
hemispherical (fisheye) canopy photographs. The package imports canopy
images, crops them to the circular area delimited by the fisheye lens,
binarizes them to separate sky from vegetation pixels, and computes the
index as the proportion of sky pixels in the cropped image. Canopy
openness is a measure related to canopy closure, canopy cover and
understorey illumination, as discussed in Jennings, Brown and Sheil
(1999) "Assessing forest canopies and understorey illumination: canopy
closure, canopy cover and other measures" <doi:10.1093/forestry/72.1.59>.
Example canopy images are included so users can test the workflow.
coiR.author: Edson Nilton de Moura Silva-Júnior [aut, cre]

coldstart.title:
Calibrating Generated Items Before Pretesting with Predicted
Priors
coldstart.description:
Predicts Rasch item difficulty from item features (text
embeddings from any model, template family, content metadata) by ridge
regression (Hoerl and Kennard, 1970, <doi:10.1080/00401706.1970.10488634>)
with honest out-of-sample uncertainty, uses the predictions as robust
informative priors to calibrate new items from small pretest samples,
in the spirit of using collateral information in calibration (Mislevy,
Sheehan and Wingersky, 1993, <doi:10.1111/j.1745-3984.1993.tb00422.x>),
plans the pretest sample size needed for a target precision, and
diagnoses item families whose predictions cannot be trusted.
coldstart.author:
Daniel Edi [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-5475-819X>)

contentiousR.title: Contentious Politics and Civil Conflict Research
contentiousR.description:
Constructs reproducible country-year panels for research on
contentious politics and civil conflict, as described in Guseinov (2026)
<doi:10.2139/ssrn.7506799>. Functions build state panels keyed by
Correlates of War or Gleditsch-Ward country codes and join curated
socioeconomic, leadership, democracy, conflict, protest, and
revolutionary-episode data on that common key, with diagnostics and
plots for comparing source coverage. Bundled sources include Gapminder;
the Nonviolent and Violent Campaigns and Outcomes (NAVCO) 2.1 data,
Chenoweth and Shay (2019) <doi:10.7910/DVN/MHOXDV>; the Social Conflict
Analysis Database, Salehyan et al. (2012)
<doi:10.1080/03050629.2012.697426>; the Uppsala Conflict Data Program
and Peace Research Institute Oslo (UCDP/PRIO) Armed Conflict Dataset,
Gleditsch et al. (2002) <doi:10.1177/0022343302039005007>; and the Major
Episodes of Contention data, Chenoweth and Kang (2026)
<doi:10.1093/jopres/xjaf008>. Varieties of Democracy (V-Dem) indicators
require the optional 'vdemdata' package, which is not on CRAN and can be
installed from <https://github.com/vdeminstitute/vdemdata>.
contentiousR.author:
Ruslan Guseinov [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0000-1156-9495>)

controlledburn.title: Sparse Geometry Rasterization with Exact Coverage Fractions
controlledburn.description:
Rasterize polygon, line, and point geometry without
materializing any pixel values. For polygons it computes exact coverage
fractions for polygon-grid intersections, returning sparse tables:
run-length encoded interior cells and individually weighted boundary
cells. The scanline algorithm is O(perimeter) in both time and memory,
using the scan line fill attributed to Wylie et al. (1967)
<doi:10.1145/1465611.1465619>. Exact coverage fractions use the
exactextract algorithm by Daniel Baston, vendored from the
'exactextractr' package <doi:10.32614/CRAN.package.exactextractr>.
Derived from the 'fasterize' package by Noam Ross.
controlledburn.author:
Michael Sumner [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-2471-7511>),
Noam Ross [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-2136-0000>),
EcoHealth Alliance [cph] (Original fasterize scanline logic),
Jim Hester [ctb] (Wrote CollectorList.h for early version),
Daniel Baston [cph] (exactextract C++ algorithm (vendored)),
ISciences, LLC [cph] (exactextract C++ algorithm (vendored))

convertxlsform.title: Convert an 'XLSForm' to a 'Word' or PDF Document
convertxlsform.description:
Converts 'XLSForm' questionnaires, as used by 'Open Data Kit'
('ODK') and 'KoboToolbox', into formatted paper versions for interviewing
and review. See <https://xlsform.org> for the 'XLSForm' standard. Output
is a 'Word' document ('.docx') or, optionally, a PDF produced from that
'Word' document with 'LibreOffice'. Supports multilingual forms, nested
question numbering, skip logic display, and question and choice media.
convertxlsform.author: Masud Rahman [aut, cre, cph]

corridoR.title:
Migration Corridors and Genetic Range Shifts from Landscape
Genetic Data
corridoR.description:
Models genetic connectivity along migration corridors and
forecasts how it shifts under climate change, following Maier et al.
(2022) <doi:10.1038/s41437-022-00561-x>. Least cost corridors are built
from accumulated cost surfaces and used as weights to summarize raw
environmental layers between sites; each group of environmental features
can choose its own corridor bandwidth; and pairwise predictions of
differentiation and directional migration are mapped back onto the
landscape as magnitude and net-direction surfaces. Includes readers for
common genotype formats (STRUCTURE, GENEPOP, VCF, GenAlEx, FSTAT and
PLINK files, and 'adegenet' objects), pairwise fixation indices, and the
directional differentiation of Sundqvist et al. (2016)
<doi:10.1002/ece3.2096>.
corridoR.author:
Paul A. Maier [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0851-8827>)

creditratingsystem.title: Offline Credit Risk Modelling, Calibration and Validation
creditratingsystem.description:
Native credit risk calculations, statistical
estimation, calibration, validation and cash flow simulation using local
structured data. Methods cover consumer and business lending with
explicit modelling assumptions, diagnostics and reproducible reference data.
creditratingsystem.author:
RiskDataScience GmbH [aut, cph],
Dimitrios Geromichalos [cre] (Dr.)

cudacellr.title: GPU-Aware Single-Cell Analysis Workflows
cudacellr.description:
Provides single-cell analysis primitives
for sparse count matrices, including library-size normalization,
log-normalization, highly variable feature selection, principal component
analysis, and nearest-neighbour construction. Integrates the 'cudaverse'
numerical and sparse layers while preserving matrix identifiers and
recording the computation backend for each stage.
Optional adapters preserve native 'SingleCellExperiment' and
'SeuratObject' version 5 object structures.
cudacellr.author: Yaoxiang Li [aut, cre]

daisytools.title: Reading and Visualizing Output from 'Daisy' Simulations
daisytools.description:
Read, transform, and visualize log files produced by
'Daisy' simulations. Supports importing dlf output files,
reshaping depth-dependent and time-series data, and creating
static and interactive plots for exploratory analysis and
comparison of simulation results.
daisytools.author:
Silas Ørting [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-3081-1547>)

dasklyr.title: R Interface to 'Dask'
dasklyr.description:
Run 'dplyr' verbs on 'Dask' data frames from R. Connect to a
local 'Dask' client or a remote scheduler, copy R data frames onto
the cluster, read and write Parquet and CSV, and collect results as
'tibble' objects. Computation stays in Python workers through
'reticulate'; R only builds the graph. A Python installation with
the 'dask' package is required.
dasklyr.author: Louis Li [aut, cre, cph]

datagrade.title: Data Quality Assessment on the ISO/IEC 25012 Model
datagrade.description:
A single-call data quality assessment scoring a data set on the
five inherent characteristics of the ISO/IEC 25012 data quality model
(accuracy, completeness, consistency, credibility and currentness) through
the fifteen quality properties beneath them, ISO/IEC (2008)
<https://www.iso.org/standard/35736.html>. Each property is measured as a
ratio of counted data items, the form ISO/IEC 25024 measurement functions
take, ISO/IEC (2015) <https://www.iso.org/standard/35749.html>. Six
properties are computable from a table alone; the rest compare the data
against expectations declared through a specification object, and are
reported as not applicable rather than approximated when none is supplied.
Also reports missing-data patterns, duplicates, redundant columns, outliers,
multicollinearity and distributional deviations, and returns a structured
object with plots rather than console text alone. The statistics implement
the methodology of the author's master's dissertation, Demirhan (2024)
"Assessing Data Quality Management Issues in Open-Sourced Data Sets with
Statistical Methodology"
<https://halukdemirhan.com/assets/msc-thesis-haluk-demirhan-public.pdf>.
datagrade.author: Omer Haluk Demirhan [aut, cre]

datascan.title: Scan Data for Quick Structural Summaries and Checks
datascan.description:
Scans data for checking columns that are constant, one-to-one, missing or all unique.
Users can also try to identify the columns that uniquely index the observational unit and whether
some columns are nested or complete.
datascan.author:
Emi Tanaka [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1455-259X>)

datazoom.saude.title: Download Brazilian Health Data from DATASUS
datazoom.saude.description: Provides a comprehensive set of functions to easily download, clean, and standardize various public health datasets from DATASUS <https://datasus.saude.gov.br/>, the Department of Informatics of the Brazilian Unified Health System (SUS). This package streamlines access to crucial health information, including mortality (SIM), hospital admissions (SIH), live births (SINASC), hospital beds (CNES-LT), and outpatient procedures (SIASUS), making the data ready for epidemiological and public health analyses.
datazoom.saude.author:
Laura Tavares Regadas [aut, cre],
Luana Laport Santos [aut],
João Paulo dos Santos P. Barbosa [aut],
DataZoom (PUC-Rio) [fnd],
Vanndher Amós B. A. de Souza [aut],
Daniela Petruzalek [ctb],
Mark Adler [ctb]

dbcturbo.title: High-Performance Streaming Reader for 'DATASUS' DBC Files
dbcturbo.description:
A modern, memory-efficient R package for reading and converting
DBC files produced by the Brazilian Ministry of Health's 'DATASUS' system.
DBC files are DBF databases compressed with the 'PKWare' implode algorithm.
Unlike 'read.dbc', this package processes files in streaming mode, never
loading the full dataset into RAM. It can export directly to CSV or DBF
and provides R helpers for in-memory reading and Parquet conversion.
dbcturbo.author:
Gumercindo Pimentel Peralta [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-5896-3171>),
Juliana da Silva [ths] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1089-6766>),
Mark Adler [ctb] (Author of blast.c (PKWare implode decompressor)),
Daniela Petruzalek [ctb] (Author of read.dbc, dbc2dbf.c),
Pablo Fonseca [ctb] (Author of blast-dbf)

decisionfacets.title: Decision Accuracy and Consistency for Rater-Mediated Exams
decisionfacets.description:
Answers "would this candidate have passed with a different set
of raters?" for rater-mediated exams such as oral examinations,
objective structured clinical examinations and essay scoring. Builds on
the many-facet extension of the rating scale model (Andrich, 1978,
<doi:10.1007/BF02293814>) to compute counterfactual pass probabilities
under the observed, an average-severity and a random rater panel, under
an explicit decision rule (raw total, fair average or measure), and
splits expected misclassification into measurement error and rater
assignment, extending item response theory classification accuracy
(Lee, 2010, <doi:10.1111/j.1745-3984.2009.00096.x>) to rater effects.
Supports panels in which every rater scores every task and designs in
which each case is scored by a different examiner, with rating
categories or continuous scores such as 0-100 (through a linear
many-facet model). Models can be fitted with 'TAM' or built-in
estimators.
decisionfacets.author:
Daniel Edi [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-5475-819X>)

delta.sharing.title: Client for the Delta Sharing Protocol
delta.sharing.description:
Connects R to 'Delta Sharing' servers for share discovery, table
metadata, snapshot reads, and change data feed reads.
delta.sharing.author:
Zac Davies [aut, cre],
Databricks [cph]

dgtf.title:
Variational and Monte Carlo Inference for Bayesian State-Space
Models of Count Data
dgtf.description:
Bayesian inference for a general class of state-space models
for count data, providing a unified interface to variational Bayes and
Markov chain Monte Carlo. Models are assembled from modular components
for the observation distribution, link function, gain function, lag
distribution, system equation, and system error, and support Poisson
and negative binomial observations together with seasonality terms.
The model class and the hybrid variational approximation are
described in Tang and Prado (2026) <doi:10.1016/j.csda.2026.108368>.
dgtf.author:
Meini Tang [aut, cre] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0001-5338-8772>),
Raquel Prado [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0001-6709-7191>)

divoRce.title:
Diagnosing Separation Phenomena in Latent Polyhedral Categorical
Response Models
divoRce.description: Utilities for checking and diagnosing separation phenomena (complete separation, quasi-complete separation, overlap) for latent polyhedral categorical response models including binary, nominal and ordinal data models with link construction as baseline-category, adjacent-category, cumulative, sequential (continuation-ratio), ordered stereotype and arbitrary link error distribution (including logit, probit, cauchit, cloglog, loglog, log amongst others) based on structure vectors as described in Sablica, Hornik, Rusch (2026) <doi:10.48550/arXiv.2610.08100> and Rusch, Sablica, Hornik (2026) <doi:10.48550/arXiv.2610.09951>. The package functionality includes a check for separation and a check for overlap with a linear program, a quick check for overlap, a sequential and a parallel check for overlap based on subsamples, detailed separation diagnostics such as identification of columns in the design matrix/structure vector matrix that lead to separation, identification of design matrix/structure vector matrix rows that lead to separation, the dimension of the recession cone and the structure vectors that are linearities. Calculations can be done with package 'rcdd' to employ arbitrary precision and various other linear program solvers can also be used via package 'ROI'. Implemented checks can be done before model fitting based on outcome and design matrix or structure vector matrix or via formula (pre-fit), or after model fitting for objects of class 'glm', 'multinom', 'polr', 'osm', 'clm', 'bracl', 'brmultinom'. Wrappers for other classes can be easily constructed by third parties via pre-fit functions.
divoRce.author:
Thomas Rusch [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-7773-2096>),
Lukas Sablica [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0001-9166-4563>),
Kurt Hornik [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0003-4198-9911>)

dmrfit.title: Scalable Bayesian Inference for Discrete Markov Random Fields
dmrfit.description:
Estimation of discrete Markov random fields through the pseudo-likelihood, for both Ising models
(Ising (1925) <doi:10.1007/BF02980577>) and ordinal Markov random fields (Marsman et al. (2025)
<doi:10.1017/psy.2024.4>). Point estimates, either maximum pseudo-likelihood or maximum a posteriori, are
obtained through a trust region optimization algorithm, with robust standard errors from the
Godambe-Huber-White (GHW, or sandwich) estimator, for both full and constrained network structures. Bayesian
inference corrects the pseudo-posterior through coordinate rescaling (Arena and Marsman (2026)
<doi:10.48550/arXiv.2601.17205>), which matches its covariance to the GHW covariance, and samples from it with the Fisher adaptive Metropolis-adjusted Langevin algorithm (Titsias (2024)
<doi:10.48550/arXiv.2305.14442>). For comparison, the posterior based on the full likelihood can also be
sampled, exactly for small networks or with the double Metropolis-Hastings algorithm (Liang (2010)
<doi:10.1080/00949650902882162>). Savage-Dickey Bayes factors test each pairwise interaction, computed either
by sampling importance resampling (Skare et al. (2003) <doi:10.1111/1467-9469.00360>) or from the posterior
draws.
dmrfit.author:
Giuseppe Arena [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-5204-3326>)

dominoise.title: Parsimonious Noise Perturbation for Magnitude Tables
dominoise.description:
Protects magnitude tables, such as tables of enterprise turnover,
by multiplying each total by a Gaussian noise combining a dominance-driven
component and a general-purpose one, governed by three parameters only.
Information loss and disclosure risks for three attack scenarios
(external inference, internal inference and differencing) are available in
closed form, so that calibration requires neither simulation nor
re-estimation on the data. The package guides that calibration
step by step, from the differencing noise to the dominance parameters,
with decision tables and risk-utility plots, applies the mechanism to an
aggregated table using SHA-512 hashed random keys for consistency over
time, and reports the risk and utility actually achieved. The method is
described in Jamme (2027)
<doi:10.1007/978-3-032-37883-5_9>.
dominoise.author:
Julien Jamme [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0009-9054-7053>),
Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques [cph]

doubletrs.title:
Memory-Efficient Doublet Detection for Single-Cell RNA
Sequencing
doubletrs.description:
Detects doublets in single-cell RNA sequencing data with the
'DoubletFinder' method of McGinnis, Murrow and Gartner (2019)
<doi:10.1016/j.cels.2019.03.003>, implemented in 'Rust' to use less
memory and time. Provides artificial doublet simulation, exact
nearest-neighbour search and pANN (proportion of artificial nearest
neighbours) scoring, and reproduces 'DoubletFinder' scores exactly.
doubletrs.author:
Mayank Gandhi [aut, cre, cph],
Authors of the dependency Rust crates [cph] (see inst/AUTHORS for the
bundled crates, their authors and licenses)

dragonfarm.title: Fine-Tune Small Language Models with LoRA from R
dragonfarm.description:
Fine-tune small (100M to 3B parameter) causal language models
with LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) from R. Datasets are mapped to
chat-format prompts and responses, training runs in a background
'Python' process built on Hugging Face 'transformers' and 'peft', and a
'shiny' app offers drag-and-drop dataset upload and column mapping.
'Python' dependencies are declared through 'reticulate' and resolved
automatically on first use.
dragonfarm.author: Tejas Patel [aut, cre]

driftwatch.title: Sequential Monitoring of Item Parameter Drift
driftwatch.description:
Ongoing surveillance of item parameter drift for continuous
testing programs and pre-equated item banks. Estimates item difficulty in
rolling calibration windows, runs sequential cumulative sum (CUSUM)
detection (Page, 1954, <doi:10.1093/biomet/41.1-2.100>; applied to testing
by Veerkamp and Glas, 2000, <doi:10.3102/10769986025004373>) with
change-point estimation, separates gradual drift from abrupt jumps,
tunes alarm thresholds for a bank-wide false-alarm target by simulation
on the program's own design, quantifies score and pass-rate impact, and
records recommended actions in an audit log.
driftwatch.author:
Daniel Edi [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-5475-819X>)

dsFedAte.title: Server-Side Treatment Effect Computation for Federated Studies
dsFedAte.description:
Server-side 'DataSHIELD' package that computes local average treatment
effect (ATE) statistics from arm-specific regression coefficients provided by
the analyst. Implements the server-side component of the G-formula
estimator from 'Federated Causal Inference: Multi-Study ATE Estimation
beyond Meta-Analysis' (R. Khellaf, A. Bellet and J. Josse, 2025),
enforcing 'DataSHIELD'
disclosure controls throughout.
dsFedAte.author:
Francisco Andrade [aut, cre],
Rémi Khellaf [aut],
Julie Josse [aut]

dtptite.title: Dose Transition Pathways for Time-to-Event Dose-Finding Designs
dtptite.description:
Implements the Dose Transition Pathways (DTP) look-ahead strategy
for time-to-event phase I dose-finding clinical trials with delayed or
pending toxicity outcomes. Provides a DTP decorator for the 'escalation'
framework, supporting both TITE-CRM (model-based) and TITE-BOIN
(model-assisted) base designs.
dtptite.author:
Xiaoran Lai [aut, cre],
The Institute of Cancer Research [cph],
National Institute for Health and Care Research [fnd]

edetect.title: Anytime-Valid Control Charts with E-Detectors
edetect.description:
Sequential change detection for process monitoring with
e-detectors (Shin, Ramdas and Rinaldo, 2024, <doi:10.51387/23-NEJSDS51>):
nonparametric, anytime-valid analogues of the CUSUM and Shiryaev-Roberts
charts whose average run length to a false alarm is guaranteed for every
distribution in a declared pre-change class (bounded, sub-Gaussian,
Bernoulli or Poisson observations). Phase I/Phase II workflow, individual,
p, c, u and regression charts, run-length simulation and auditable alarm
reports.
edetect.author:
André Leite [aut, cre] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-4718-9766>),
Raydonal Ospina [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-9884-9090>),
Cristiano Ferraz [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-6838-6734>)

eduResearchR.title:
A Collection of Educational Datasets for Research and
Statistical Analysis
eduResearchR.description: Curates a comprehensive and robust collection of 15 classic educational, economic, and social science datasets meticulously tailored for empirical research, project-based learning, and academic instruction in higher education. It streamlines exploratory data analysis, business intelligence modeling, regression techniques, and hypothesis testing by providing ready-to-use data structures sourced from prominent community packages (Kleiber and Zeileis (2008) <https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=AER>; Fox and Weisberg (2019) <https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=carData>).
eduResearchR.author:
Jorge Luis Marmanillo Santana [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0003-4485-0744>),
Christian Kleiber [ctb] (Author of the AER package; original source for
CASchools and CollegeDistance.),
John Fox [ctb] (Author of the carData package; original source for
EducationLiteracy, ExamScores, and FirstYearGPA.),
Douglas Bates [ctb] (Author of the MEMSS package; original source for
MathAchieve.),
Thomas Lumley [ctb] (Author of the survey package; original source for
apipop.),
Jeremy Finn [ctb] (Principal investigator; original source for STARplus
(Project STAR).),
Andrew Raudenbush [ctb] (Researcher; original source for the classroom
dataset.)

electedBR.title: Brazilian Election Winners and Sitting Members of Congress
electedBR.description:
Retrieves the candidates elected in Brazilian municipal and general
elections since 2018, consolidated from the open data of the Superior
Electoral Court (TSE, <https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/>) and distributed
as yearly Parquet files, together with the federal deputies and senators
currently serving according to the open data APIs of the Chamber of
Deputies (<https://dadosabertos.camara.leg.br/>) and the Federal Senate
(<https://www12.senado.leg.br/dados-abertos>). Election results and current
office holding are kept as distinct queries; electoral roles, service
history and provenance are preserved. Every function returns a tibble with
English column names and has a Portuguese alias.
electedBR.author:
Andre Leite [aut, cre] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-4718-9766>),
Marcos Wasiliew [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0009-0004-4694-3159>),
Hugo Vasconcelos [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0001-6249-0920>),
Carlos Amorim [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0001-6315-8305>),
Diogo Bezerra [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1216-8674>)

ellmercodex.title: 'ChatGPT' Plan Provider for 'ellmer'
ellmercodex.description:
Connects 'ellmer' chats to a 'ChatGPT' subscription through
'OpenAI''s documented "Sign in with ChatGPT" flow for open-source,
locally hosted apps
<https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source>. Provides
a stable, explicitly bounded core of the public 'ellmer' (>= 0.5.0) Chat
object, including browser sign-in with dynamic client registration,
package-scoped credential storage, redacted diagnostics, multi-turn text,
streaming, structured-output, function-tool, asynchronous, cancellation,
cloning, metadata, multimodal chat, account-specific model discovery, and
reasoning-effort selection through the public 'Responses' API. Parallel
and batch helper functions are explicitly unsupported because 'ChatGPT'
plan usage is stream-only. This independent third-party integration is
not endorsed by 'OpenAI'.
ellmercodex.author: Simon Herrera [aut, cre, cph]

enhancedTtest.title: Enhanced T-Test with Automatic Selection and APA Formatting
enhancedTtest.description:
Provides enhanced t-test functionality with automatic
assumption checking, non-parametric fallbacks, effect size calculation,
and APA-formatted tables that can be exported to Word documents. Supports
one-sample, two-sample, and paired t-tests with intelligent test selection.
Effect size interpretations follow Cohen (1988) <doi:10.4324/9780203771587>
and APA formatting follows the Publication Manual of the American
Psychological Association, 7th edition (2020) <doi:10.1037/0000165-000>.
enhancedTtest.author: Martin Nyamu [aut, cre]

enviPathR.title: Client for the 'enviPath' 'RESTful' API
enviPathR.description:
The environmental pathway database ('enviPath') is a key resource for the
functional annotation and pathway prediction of microbial communities,
providing knowledge on biotransformation pathways along with the chemical
reactions and produced compounds. This package enables the programmatic
access to 'enviPath' by porting the database 'RESTful' API from R. This
includes methods to both retrieve entries and predict pathways for custom
compounds.
enviPathR.author:
Giulio Benedetti [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-8732-7692>)

epidist.title: Estimate Epidemiological Delay Distributions with 'brms'
epidist.description:
Understanding and accurately estimating epidemiological delay
distributions is important for public health policy. These estimates
influence epidemic situational awareness, control strategies,
and resource allocation. This package provides methods to address the
key challenges in estimating these distributions, including truncation,
interval censoring, and dynamical biases, following Park et al. (2024)
<doi:10.1101/2024.01.12.24301247> and Charniga et al. (2024)
<doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1012520>. These issues are frequently
overlooked, resulting in biased conclusions. Built on top of 'brms',
it allows for flexible modelling including time-varying and spatial
effects and partially pooled estimates of demographic characteristics.
epidist.author:
Adam Howes [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0003-2386-4031>),
Sang Woo Park [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0003-2202-3361>),
Sam Abbott [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-8057-8037>),
Sebastian Funk [ctb] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-2842-3406>)

eqty.sdk.r.title: Verifiable Provenance for 'R' Workflows
eqty.sdk.r.description:
Provides an 'R' interface for building verifiable manifests around
data, models, prompts, agents, computations, and related lineage. Exposes
the public 'eqty-sdk' 'Python' package through types accessible from 'R' for
creating
assets, connecting computation inputs and outputs by content identifier,
grouping statements in contexts, and exporting manifest JSON files.
eqty.sdk.r.author: Support EQTY Lab [aut, cre]

ertte.title: Exposure-Response Tools for Time-to-Event Models
ertte.description:
Provides estimation tools for exposure-response models of
time-to-event endpoints based on the 'survival' package: parametric
accelerated failure time model fitting and prediction with
AIC-based distribution selection, stepwise covariate modelling,
and simulation-based visual predictive checks. Tested and
supported for the exponential, Weibull, log-normal, and
log-logistic distributions. For a model-agnostic mini-language to
visualise exposure-response models (including those fitted with
'ertte'), see the companion package 'erplots'.
ertte.author:
Danielle Navarro [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-7648-6578>)

esgcalc.title: Offline Environmental, Social and Governance Calculations
esgcalc.description:
Native, deterministic calculations for selected environmental,
social and governance metrics. Provides granular taxonomy criteria,
non-financial taxonomy indicators, principal adverse impact components,
portfolio calculations and configurable performance ratings. Versioned
local resources, explicit assumptions and structured results support
reproducible offline use. Does not determine legal applicability or
provide a complete regulatory reporting system. Selected methods reference
EU Regulations 2020/852, 2022/1288 and 2023/2772; exact editions and
provision locators are supplied in the bundled source contracts.
For background on the taxonomy framework, see the European Commission
<https://finance.ec.europa.eu/sustainable-finance/tools-and-standards/eu-taxonomy-sustainable-activities_en>.
esgcalc.author:
Dimitrios Geromichalos [aut, cre],
RiskDataScience GmbH [cph]

ethnoecologyR.title:
Quantitative Ethnoecology Analysis and Landscape Knowledge
Modeling
ethnoecologyR.description:
A comprehensive toolkit for quantitative ethnoecology analysis
and landscape knowledge modeling. Implements core indices including
Landscape Use (LU), Cultural Importance in Ecology (CIE), Frequency of
Citation (FC), Fidelity Level (FL), Number of Uses (NU), and Cultural
Value of Ecolandscape (CVe). Provides visualization tools for chord
diagrams, alluvial plots, and radial plots, as well as Bayesian consensus
modeling and bootstrap resampling to support reproducible research in
Local Ecological Knowledge (LEK) and participatory land-use decision
analysis. Methods are based on Tardío and Pardo-de-Santayana (2008)
<doi:10.1007/s12231-007-9004-5>,
Reyes-García et al. (2006)
<https://www.jstor.org/stable/4257061>,
and Friedman et al. (1986)
<doi:10.1037/0022-3514.51.6.1173>.
ethnoecologyR.author:
Marwan Setiawan [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-2754-0640>)

evgmrf.title: Gaussian Markov Random Field Models for Extreme Values
evgmrf.description:
Fitting extreme value distributions with parameters that vary according to
Gaussian Markov random fields (GMRFs). For details of distributions see
Coles, S.G. (2001) <doi:10.1007/978-1-4471-3675-0>, GMRFs see
Rue, H., & Held, L. (2005) <doi:10.1201/9780203492024>, and the fitting approach see
Wood, S.N., Pya, N. & Safken, B. (2016) <doi:10.1080/01621459.2016.1180986>.
evgmrf.author:
Ben Youngman [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0215-8189>),
Ayu Shabrina [aut, ctb] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-6172-5230>)

exactcond.title:
Exact Conditional Reference Distributions for Tables and
Selected Linear Models
exactcond.description:
Reference distributions that are exact at every sample size, obtained by conditioning
on a statistic sufficient for the nuisance parameter rather than by appealing to an asymptotic
approximation. Two forms of conditioning are supplied. For a two-way table the row and column totals are
sufficient for the marginal parameters, so conditioning on both margins leaves the Fisher-Yates
law, sampled here exactly by random permutation of the column labels; statistics include
Goodman's linear-by-linear association and, for nominal rows against an ordinal column, the
dispersion of the row mean scores, whose components are the group contrasts themselves. A
two-table form conditions further on the total score to cancel a common association parameter,
giving a nuisance-free test that two tables share it. For a linear model under a null in which
the tested structure is absent, a statistic invariant to the coefficients and the error scale
depends on the data only through the residual direction, which is uniform on the sphere of the
residual space; the reference stays exact when the statistic is maximised over candidate
structures, and so remains valid after a spatial weight matrix has been chosen by fit. Every
replicate draws from its own stream, so results do not depend on the thread count. The same C
sources back the 'Python' package 'exactcond'.
exactcond.author:
M. Theodor Loots [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-7722-3913>)

famnesia.title: Anonymising Familias Files
famnesia.description:
A 'shiny' application for anonymising files exported from the
'Familias' software for forensic kinship analysis (Egeland et al.
(2000) <doi:10.1016/s0379-0738(00)00147-x>). Pedigrees, marker data,
allele frequencies and mutation models can be masked or modified, with
options for preserving likelihood ratios exactly. The application is
built on the 'pedsuite' packages for pedigree analysis.
famnesia.author:
Magnus Dehli Vigeland [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-9134-4962>)

fastphylosig.title: Fast Phylogenetic Signal Statistics
fastphylosig.description:
Provides one-command and method-specific workflows for
phylogenetic signal in continuous, binary, and categorical traits. Compiled
tree-pruning algorithms implement Blomberg's K and Pagel's lambda without
constructing a dense phylogenetic covariance matrix in production.
Fritz and Purvis D retains separate random and Brownian null models, while
categorical Delta combines discrete ancestral-state likelihoods with MCMC
and permutation diagnostics. The package also provides reusable prepared
trees, explicit tree/data matching, trait-wise missing-value handling,
conservative tree diagnostics, bounded simulation memory, and structured
timing and Monte Carlo uncertainty metadata. Methods follow Blomberg,
Garland and Ives (2003) <doi:10.1111/j.0014-3820.2003.tb00285.x> for K,
Pagel (1999) <doi:10.1038/44766> for lambda, Fritz and Purvis (2010)
<doi:10.1111/j.1523-1739.2010.01455.x> for D, and Borges et al. (2019)
<doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/bty800> for categorical Delta.
fastphylosig.author: Yin Wen [aut, cre]

fdb.title: Frequentist Dynamic Borrowing for Hybrid-Control Survival Trials
fdb.description:
Implements a class of likelihood-informed frequentist dynamic
borrowing methods for hybrid-control survival trials based on penalized
Cox partial likelihood estimation. Implements four
likelihood-informed penalty structures (precision-weighted L1,
smoothed integrated-gate, information-adaptive minimax concave penalty
(MCP), and likelihood-ratio-weighted L1), together with the adaptive
lasso borrowing approach of Li et al. (2023, <doi:10.1002/bimj.202100406>).
Provides conditional model-based standard errors and local plug-in
sandwich variance approximations, with smoothed penalties. Tools for design-stage lambda calibration
via simulation, including a two-stage coarse-fine grid search, drift-level
early stopping, and per-method tuning under both inference types, are also
provided. A simulation harness for evaluating type I error and statistical
power across population drift scenarios is included.
fdb.author: Yusuke Yamaguchi [aut, cre]

fereg.title: Fast Fixed-Effects Estimation with the 'fixest' Interface
fereg.description:
Ordinary least squares, two-stage least squares, Poisson and
logit regressions with any number of high-dimensional fixed effects,
interactions of fixed effects, varying slopes, weights and iid,
heteroskedasticity-robust (HC1, HC2, HC3), multiway-clustered, CRV3,
Newey-West, Driscoll-Kraay or Conley standard errors. The formula syntax,
arguments, results and methods follow the 'fixest' package and reproduce
its estimates. The computations run in a parallel 'Rust' library that
eliminates the largest fixed effect exactly and solves for the others by
preconditioned conjugate gradient.
fereg.author:
Leo Liu [aut, cre, cph],
Authors of the bundled Rust crates [ctb, cph] (see inst/AUTHORS for
each crate's authors and license)

feols.asv.title:
Average Shared Variance (ASV) Decomposition for Multiple
Fixed-Effects Models
feols.asv.description: Conducts average shared variance to calculate individual contributions of predictors (groups) towards within R2  for Multiple Fixed-Effects Models.
feols.asv.author:
Jiangshan Lai [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0279-8816>)

fieldopt.title: Area-Frame and Dual-Frame Survey Design under Real Field Cost
fieldopt.description:
Design of agricultural and other area-frame and dual-frame
(area plus list) sample surveys that go to the field, with the real
cost of field work (travel between sampling units plus interviews)
next to the variance of the design-based estimator. Travel matrices
from coordinates or a road network; GRASP routing of the field work
for one or several teams; stratified spatially balanced (local
pivotal) or spatially ordered systematic selection of segments with
interpenetrating replicates; points inside segments with multiplicity
(expected-hits) estimation; closed, open and weighted segment
estimators; Horvitz-Thompson estimation with local-mean or replicate
variances; cost-aware allocation across strata, Hartley's dual-frame
allocation with an overlap, and two-stage allocation with a cost
function; and the cost-variance frontier of a design by simulation.
The computational engine is the Rust crate 'fieldopt-core'.
fieldopt.author:
André Leite [aut, cre] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-4718-9766>),
Raydonal Ospina [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-9884-9090>),
Cristiano Ferraz [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-6838-6734>),
The authors of the dependency Rust crates [ctb] (see inst/AUTHORS file
for details)

fkr.title: Realistic Fake Data Generator for the Philippines
fkr.description:
Generates realistic, locale-aware synthetic data for the
Philippines, covering both personal data (names, ages, birthdays,
contact details, addresses, government-ID-style numbers) and
business data (company names, industries, job titles, products,
prices, and permit numbers). Every value, including anything
formatted to resemble a government identifier, is drawn uniformly
at random for software testing, prototyping, and teaching, and
does not correspond to any real person, business, or record.
fkr.author:
Bhas Abdulsamad [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0002-5891-8124>)

flexMatch.title: Flexible Matching for Stacked Difference-in-Differences
flexMatch.description:
Tools for building stacked difference-in-differences samples in
staggered-adoption settings. The package labels valid treated and control
candidates, performs cross-sectional matching, expands matched units into
event-time stacks, and returns diagnostics for balance assessment and
visualization.
flexMatch.author: Aleksandr Kazakov [aut, cre, cph]

flexsdm.title: Flexible Species Distribution Modeling Workflow
flexsdm.description:
Provides a flexible and comprehensive workflow for species
distribution modeling, from data preparation (occurrence filtering,
calibration areas, pseudo-absence and background sampling, data
partitioning, and collinearity reduction) to model fitting, tuning,
evaluation, prediction, ensemble modeling, and post-processing. The package is
described in Velazco et al. (2022) <doi:10.1111/2041-210X.13874>.
Implemented methods include the Shape metric to measure model
extrapolation of Velazco et al. (2023) <doi:10.1111/ecog.06992>,
ensembles of small models of Breiner et al. (2015)
<doi:10.1111/2041-210X.12403> and Breiner et al. (2018)
<doi:10.1111/2041-210X.12957>, Gaussian process models of Golding and
Purse (2016) <doi:10.1111/2041-210X.12523>, and occurrence-based
constraints for post-processing predictions of Mendes et al. (2020)
<doi:10.1016/j.ecolmodel.2020.109180>.
flexsdm.author:
Santiago J.E. Velazco [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-7527-0967>),
Brooke Rose [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0001-5269-3759>),
André F.A. Andrade [aut] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-6134-3176>),
Ignacio Minoli [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-6039-6962>),
Janet Franklin [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0314-4598>)

flowz.title: Local Latent Flow Forecasting with Empirical Calibration
flowz.description:
Fits conditional flow-matching models to univariate time series.
Combines a selectable exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA),
autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA), autoregressive
fractionally integrated moving average (ARFIMA), or structural time-series
baseline with direct multi-step residual paths and a random-feature extreme
learning machine (ELM) velocity field. Spectral dispersion calibration uses
a chronological calibration block, with a separate test block for forecast
scoring. Provides simulated forecast paths and smooth marginal
distributions. Methodological background is given by Lipman et al. (2023)
<doi:10.48550/arXiv.2210.02747>, Huang et al. (2006)
<doi:10.1016/j.neucom.2005.12.126>, Hyndman and Khandakar (2008)
<doi:10.18637/jss.v027.i03>, and Haslett and Raftery (1989)
<doi:10.2307/2347679>.
flowz.author: Giancarlo Vercellino [aut, cre]

forensicR.title: Crime Scene Documentation and Reconstruction Tools
forensicR.description:
Supports crime scene investigators in documenting and
reconstructing scenes. Scene points are mapped from field measurements
(baseline, triangulation, polar). Shooting incidents are reconstructed
from bullet defects with explicit uncertainty, following the methods
described in Haag and Haag (2020, ISBN:9780128193976) and Hueske (2015,
ISBN:9781498707664). Evidence and custody are logged in a structured
form, and reproducible scene reports are rendered to Word, PDF or HTML.
forensicR.author:
Karine Quadros [aut, cre],
Allan Quadros [aut]

forecastsuite.title: Multi-Model Time Series Forecasting Toolkit and Local App
forecastsuite.description:
Fits, compares and visualizes univariate time series forecasts
through an extensible model registry built largely on the 'forecast'
package: AutoRegressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) and Seasonal
ARIMA (SARIMA) models (Hyndman and Khandakar (2008)
<doi:10.18637/jss.v027.i03>), Error, Trend, Seasonal (ETS) exponential
smoothing (Hyndman et al. (2002) <doi:10.1016/S0169-2070(01)00110-8>),
Trigonometric seasonality, Box-Cox transformation, AutoRegressive Moving
Average (ARMA) errors, Trend and Seasonal components (TBATS) models
(De Livera, Hyndman and Snyder (2011) <doi:10.1198/jasa.2011.tm09771>),
Neural Network AutoRegression (NNETAR) and Holt-Winters exponential
smoothing (Winters (1960) <doi:10.1287/mnsc.6.3.324>), plus optional
'Prophet' models via the 'prophet' package (Taylor and Letham (2018)
<doi:10.1080/00031305.2017.1380080>) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)
networks via the 'torch' package (Hochreiter and Schmidhuber (1997)
<doi:10.1162/neco.1997.9.8.1735>). Also provides grouped series with
bottom-up and top-down reconciliation, rolling-origin cross-validation,
ensembles and residual diagnostics, following Hyndman and Athanasopoulos
(2021) <https://otexts.com/fpp3/>, and a bundled local 'shiny'
application exposing every model.
forecastsuite.author:
Mukul Maheshwari [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1918-5100>)

foresightr.title: Forecasts Chosen by What Would Have Worked
foresightr.description:
Time series forecasting that replays the past before trusting a
model: a rolling-origin backtest, Tashman (2000)
<doi:10.1016/S0169-2070(00)00065-0>, refits every candidate at each
origin, the choice is made by out-of-sample error, and prediction
intervals are quantiles of the errors actually observed, for each horizon
and for totals of the next periods. Models include seasonal ARIMA by
exact maximum likelihood with automatic orders, Hyndman and Khandakar
(2008) <doi:10.18637/jss.v027.i03>; exponential smoothing in state space
form, Hyndman, Koehler, Snyder and Grose (2002)
<doi:10.1016/S0169-2070(01)00110-8>; the Theta method, Assimakopoulos
and Nikolopoulos (2000) <doi:10.1016/S0169-2070(00)00066-2>; a trend with
changepoints and events in the manner of Taylor and Letham (2018)
<doi:10.1080/00031305.2017.1380080>; TBATS, De Livera, Hyndman and Snyder
(2011) <doi:10.1198/jasa.2011.tm09771>; seasonal-trend decompositions by
LOESS for one or several seasonal periods, Bandara, Hyndman and Bergmeir
(2021) <doi:10.48550/arXiv.2107.13462>; the method of Croston (1972)
<doi:10.1057/jors.1972.50> for intermittent demand; and ensembles. The
computations are done by the 'Rust' crate 'foresight', bundled with the
package.
foresightr.author:
André Leite [aut, cre] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-4718-9766>),
Marcos Wasiliew [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0009-0004-4694-3159>),
Hugo Vasconcelos [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0001-6249-0920>),
Carlos Amorim [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0001-6315-8305>),
Diogo Bezerra [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1216-8674>),
Júlia Nascimento Barreto [aut] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0004-2851-7770>),
The authors of the dependency Rust crates [ctb] (see inst/AUTHORS file
for details)

fpoValue.title:
Farmer Producer Organisation Economics and Member Benefit
Accounting
fpoValue.description:
Tools to determine when collective marketing, aggregation,
grading and bulk input procurement through farmer producer organisations
(FPOs) and agricultural cooperatives improve member-farmer returns. The
package provides channel-level transaction cost accounting (transport,
commissions, market fees, time, rejection and payment-delay costs),
estimation of scale economies from consolidated transport, tiered bulk
input discounts and grading premiums, break-even throughput and
procurement-price analysis, and comparison of individual and collective
marketing scenarios. Its core is a member-level distributional
accounting framework that separates the total surplus generated by an
FPO from the benefits actually received by farmers through prices,
transaction cost savings, input savings and dividends, and summarises
their distribution across members with Gini and concentration indices
and farm-size group shares.
fpoValue.author: Anbukkani Perumal [aut, cre, cph]

frostlake.title: 'DBI' Backend for the 'Frostlake' Database Engine
frostlake.description:
A 'DBI'-compliant driver for 'Frostlake', a SQL engine emulating
core 'Snowflake' features. Speaks the engine's HTTP protocol against a
running 'DatabaseHttpServer': one POST per statement with a session id
the server issues on first contact, so session state (current
database/schema, transactions) persists across statements. Query results
arrive as data frames with Snowflake types mapped to R types.
frostlake.author: MLorek [aut, cre, cph]

fullmetaphone.title: Full-Length Metaphone and Double Metaphone Phonetic Codes
fullmetaphone.description:
Encodes names and words as phonetic codes, so that names
which sound alike but are spelled differently can be matched.
Implements the Metaphone algorithm of Philips (1990, Computer
Language, 7(12), 38-43) and the Double Metaphone algorithm of Philips
(2000) <https://web.archive.org/web/20250702064845/https://drdobbs.com/the-double-metaphone-search-algorithm/184401251>,
which gives a primary and an alternate code for names of many
language origins. Unlike most implementations, including 'PGRdup',
the codes are not cut to four characters, which keeps long and
multi-part names apart. Provides metaphone(), double_metaphone() and
sounds_like() for record linkage, deduplication and name search,
and includes a data set of common United States surnames.
fullmetaphone.author:
Anil Kumar Goyal [aut, cre, cph],
Atharv Tyagi [aut, cph],
Lawrence Philips [ctb] (Designer of the Metaphone and Double Metaphone
algorithms and author of their original code),
Maurice Aubrey [ctb] (Author of the C implementation of Double
Metaphone whose rules are followed here),
Kevin Atkinson [ctb] (Bug fixes to that C implementation),
The Apache Software Foundation [cph] (Apache Commons Codec, the basis
of metaphone() and of the test data)

fuzzySurvival.title:
Fuzzy Survival Analysis with Vague Event Times and Fuzzy
Censoring
fuzzySurvival.description:
Fuzzy survival analysis for data in which event times and/or
failure indicators are vague, for instance when a failure is only known to
have occurred during the second quarter of a year, or when it is uncertain
whether a subject lost to follow-up had in fact failed.  Vague information
is represented by fuzzy numbers.  The package provides a fuzzy
product-limit estimator obtained from nested alpha-cuts of the fuzzy
survival function, a fuzzy Cox proportional hazards model with fuzzy
coefficient and hazard ratio estimates, and a fuzzy log-rank test.
Type-reduction utilities for summarizing fuzzy estimates by single
numbers, a simulation engine for validation studies,
plotting, print and summary methods, and alpha-cut based confidence bands
are provided.  The bounds are computed at the alpha-cuts of the fuzzy
event times, so the alpha-cut intervals returned for the survival
function, the regression coefficients and the test statistic are nested by
construction.
fuzzySurvival.author:
Mukul Bijalwan [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0001-3040-6912>),
Gunjan Aggrwal [aut],
Mukul Jain [aut]

fvfmR.title: Chlorophyll Fluorescence (Fv/Fm) Analysis of Leaf Disc Images
fvfmR.description:
Semi-automated analysis of chlorophyll fluorescence images of
leaf discs taken with a 'Walz' 'IMAGING-PAM' fluorometer. Provides an R
interface to the 'fvfmPy' 'Python' package, which detects leaf discs,
assigns them to a grid of rows and columns, and computes the maximum
quantum efficiency of photosystem II, Fv/Fm = (Fm - Fo) / Fm, for each
disc. The interactive 'fvfmPy' window is launched from R and the results
are returned to R as a data frame.
fvfmR.author:
Josef Garen [aut, cph],
Pieter Arnold [aut, cre, cph],
Kristine Crous [aut, cph]

gaussianprocesses.title: Gaussian Processes from First Principles
gaussianprocesses.description:
Gaussian process regression, classification, and count models
with explicit covariance kernels, exact Gaussian inference, Laplace
approximations for non-Gaussian likelihoods, sparse approximations,
marginal-likelihood optimization, derivatives, posterior sampling,
calibration diagnostics, and time-series workflows. The implementation
follows the core methodology of Rasmussen and Williams (2006)
<doi:10.7551/mitpress/3206.001.0001> and emphasizes numerical stability,
transparent assumptions, and reproducible statistical workflows.
gaussianprocesses.author:
Diogo Ribeiro [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0001-2022-7072>, affiliation: Faculty of
Media Arts and Design of the Technical University of Porto)

gcloglog.title:
Methods for Fitting Binomial Models with the Generalized
Complementary Log-Log Function
gcloglog.description: Functionality for fitting a flexible link function in binomial regression based on a latent negative-binomial count. The original link function was proposed by Aranda-Ordaz (1981)<doi:10.1093/biomet/68.2.357>, and motivation via a negative-binomial latent count by van der Veen and Hui (in prep).
gcloglog.author:
Bert van der Veen [aut, cre],
Francis K.C. Hui [aut]

genevintage.title: Detect Annotation Releases and Repair Gene Names
genevintage.description:
Detects the species and the 'Ensembl' <https://www.ensembl.org>
or 'GENCODE' <https://www.gencodegenes.org> annotation release associated
with a set of gene or transcript identifiers by scoring them against
a bundled fingerprint of each release. Identifiers are then converted to
gene names using the matching release. Gene symbols that spreadsheet software
turned into dates or numbers ('SEPT9' to '9-Sep') are restored to the
spelling of the chosen release. Also retrieves genes by class (mitochondrial,
sex-linked, protein-coding, ribosomal, transfer RNA, long non-coding
RNA), exon-union gene lengths, 'Entrez' cross-references, and orthologs
in another species from 'Ensembl Compara'.
genevintage.author:
Saket Choudhary [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-5202-7633>)

geoecu.title:
Maps of the Provinces, Cantons and Parishes of Ecuador (Mapas de
Provincias, Cantones y Parroquias del Ecuador)
geoecu.description:
Provides the boundaries of the provinces, cantons and parishes
of Ecuador as 'sf' objects, identified by the codes of the national
political-administrative division (DPA, "División Político-Administrativa"),
ready to be mapped and joined with health, epidemiological surveillance or
other data. The three levels nest exactly and are offered in two
resolutions: a light one for maps and dashboards and a detailed one for
spatial analysis. The layers are derived from the open data of the
Territorial Organization of the State published by the National Committee
of Internal Boundaries (CONALI, Ministry of Government of Ecuador) under a
CC BY licence <https://www.datosabiertos.gob.ec/>, and are downloaded on
first use as 'GeoPackage' files, verified and cached locally. Includes a
catalogue of DPA codes, a table to update codes from earlier versions,
helpers to clean codes and place names, and tools to relocate the
Galapagos Islands in national maps. Documentation is in Spanish.
geoecu.author: Ronald Fabricio Salas Guerrero [aut, cre, cph]

geomattR.title: Calculate Geometric Attributes of Spatial Polygons
geomattR.description: Calculate geometric attributes of spatial polygons including area, perimeter, compactness, elongation, orientation (bearing), fractal dimension, and various shape indices. The package relies heavily on 'terra' methods and vector data objects <https://github.com/rspatial/terra>.
geomattR.author:
Gabriel Ortega-Solís [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0516-5694>)

geomorphR.title: Geometric Features and Footprint Comparison for 'sf' Objects
geomorphR.description:
Extracts reproducible geometric and urban-morphology descriptors from
polygon and multipart polygon building footprints stored as 'sf' objects,
including area, perimeter, compactness, shape, topology, convexity, orientation,
and optional building-height and floor-area metrics. Compares polygon footprints
across periods using the intersection-over-union (Jaccard) index (Jaccard,
1912) <doi:10.1111/j.1469-8137.1912.tb05611.x> to identify new constructions,
potential demolitions, and footprint changes. Supports vector file formats
readable by 'sf', including Shapefiles and GeoPackage (GPKG) vector files with
named layers, optional boundary clipping, and reprojection to a common coordinate
reference system. Returned 'sf' objects preserve source attributes and geometry
for spatial analysis and downstream workflows, with optional parallel processing
using 'future' for larger feature-extraction jobs.
geomorphR.author: Jonathan Cohen [aut, cre]

geopt.title: Tools to Access and Map Spatial Datasets of Portugal
geopt.description:
Tools to download, process, and visualize official spatial datasets
for Portugal. Get administrative boundaries at all levels and
other geographic data ready for mapping. Data from Statistics Portugal
(INE), for example retrieved with the 'ineptr2' package, can be joined to
the boundaries by place name or code, including names from earlier
boundary reforms.
geopt.author: Carlos Matos [aut, cre, cph]

geopytorch.title: R Interface to 'GeoPyTorch'
geopytorch.description:
Fits ordinary kriging and spatial linear models through
'reticulate' with the 'GeoPyTorch' 'Python' package, which is built on
'GPyTorch' and 'PyTorch'. Covariance parameters can be fixed or estimated
by maximum likelihood or restricted maximum likelihood, and predictions
include their variances. 'Python' and the required packages are installed
on first use by 'reticulate'.
geopytorch.author: Daniel Tinoco [aut, cre]

geotech.title: Geotechnical Engineering
geotech.description:
A compilation of functions for performing calculations and
creating plots that commonly arise in geotechnical engineering and soil
mechanics. The types of calculations that are currently included are:
(1) phase diagrams and index parameters, (2) grain-size distributions,
(3) plasticity, (4) soil classification, (5) compaction, (6) groundwater,
(7) subsurface stresses (geostatic and induced), (8) Mohr circle analyses,
(9) consolidation settlement and rate, (10) shear strength, (11) bearing
capacity, (12) lateral earth pressures, (13) slope stability, and (14)
subsurface explorations. Geotechnical engineering students, educators,
researchers, and practitioners will find this package useful.
geotech.author:
James Kaklamanos [aut],
Kyle Elmy [aut],
Irucka Embry [cre]

ggaltdata.title:
Data-Driven Alternative Text and Data Tables for 'ggplot2'
Charts
ggaltdata.description:
Generates alternative text that states what a 'ggplot2' chart
shows (highest and lowest values, rankings, trends, gaps between groups,
overlap of intervals), a long description and the data table, computed
from the data of the chart itself. Output for 'R Markdown', 'Quarto',
'Word', saved images and 'Shiny', in English and Italian.
ggaltdata.author: Federico Ninivaggi [aut, cre]

ggcolonviz.title: A 'ggplot2' Extension for Visualizing the Colon
ggcolonviz.description:
Provides a 'ggplot2' extension for creating clear, customizable
visualizations of the colon. Includes geometry and label layers for
plotting colon anatomy and overlaying related data, along with helpers
for converting colon segments to 'sf' polygons and generating heatmap
grids across the colon geometry.
ggcolonviz.author:
Yoni Sidi [aut, cre],
Sanofi [cph]

ggextreme.title: Bar Chart Races and Interactive Plots for Clinical Research
ggextreme.description:
Presentation quality charts built on 'ggplot2' that the package
itself does not provide. The bar chart race interpolates values on a
uniform time grid, ranks every frame on its own values and eases bars
into new positions, so a reordering field stays readable. Frames are
ordinary 'ggplot2' objects laid out on a fixed pixel grid, which keeps
the axis and label column from drifting between them, and are encoded to
GIF or MP4. Circular images, such as the bundled country flags, can be
placed at the end of each bar. Causal diagrams are drawn as directed
acyclic graphs whose nodes and arrows each carry a rationale and
references, shown on hover and opened with clickable links on click,
through 'ggiraph'; the same diagram is also available as a static
'ggplot2' object. Network plots for network meta-analysis are drawn from
arm level data, with the baseline characteristics and outcomes of every
arm shown side by side on click. Forest plots for 'metafor' and 'meta'
fits carry each study's record and risk of bias traffic lights, and
replay a cumulative meta-analysis as an animation; funnel plots shade
where each study would be significant and carry the pooled estimate
without it, trim and fill and the tests for small-study effects; league
tables for 'netmeta' fits show the direct and indirect evidence behind
every estimate. Kaplan-Meier plots read survival and the hazard ratio at
any time under the pointer, beside a risk table and proportional hazards
tests, and swimmer plots give each patient a lane with their responses,
progression and death. Nomograms of regression models, from linear and
generalized linear models to mixed, Cox, parametric survival, ordinal
and multinomial models, have a handle per predictor and compute each
prediction with its confidence interval in the page. Choropleth maps of
the world or of any 'sf' map step or play through the years, with
several measures side by side for the same year. Causal diagrams can
also show which paths between an exposure and an outcome an adjustment
set leaves open, by the backdoor criterion; Kaplan-Meier plots give the
restricted mean survival time up to a horizon the reader can move;
league tables and network plots show where each network estimate's
evidence comes from; and swimmer plots can carry a waterfall of best
change and each patient's course beside the lanes. Four explorers put a
threshold or an assumption in the reader's hands: the cutoff of a
diagnostic test, with what it means for 1,000 people at any prevalence;
the strength of unmeasured confounding, with E-values; the choices of a
multiverse of analyses; and the threshold that defines a responder.
Plots after CINeMA judge the confidence in each estimate of a network
meta-analysis in six domains, with every judgment's reason and source,
and show what lies behind them: each study's contribution, the
estimates against a movable range of little difference, direct against
indirect evidence, and a league table and a network marked with the
judgments.
ggextreme.author: Ahmad Sofi-Mahmudi [aut, cre, cph]

ggfourfold.title: Fourfold Displays for 'ggplot2'
ggfourfold.description:
Draws fourfold displays of 2 x 2 (x k) contingency tables as a
'ggplot2' layer, following Friendly (1994)
<https://datavis.ca/papers/4fold/4fold.pdf> and Friendly and Meyer (2016)
<doi:10.1201/9781315374413>. Cell frequencies are shown as quarter-circles
or squares of proportional area, with confidence rings for the
odds ratio and shading for the direction and strength of association.
Stratified tables are shown with 'ggplot2' faceting and a corresponding
'ggplot2' theme is provided.
ggfourfold.author:
Gavin Klorfine [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0003-0395-4512>),
Michael Friendly [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-3237-0941>)

ggmGraphEditor.title: Interactive Graph Layout Editor for Mixed Graphs
ggmGraphEditor.description:
Provides an interactive interface to plot and layout mixed
graphs based on the adjacency matrix defined in Sadeghi and
Marchetti (2012) <doi:10.32614/RJ-2012-015>. Uses 'shiny' and
'visNetwork' to allow dynamic node repositioning and coordinate
extraction.
ggmGraphEditor.author:
Giovanni M. Marchetti [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-4413-9349>),
Kayvan Sadeghi [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0001-7314-744X>)

glemb.title:
Multiple Imputation Using the General Location Model with the
EMB Algorithm
glemb.description:
Provides multiple imputation for mixed continuous and categorical
data using the General Location Model (Olkin and Tate (1961)
<doi:10.1214/aoms/1177705052>; Little and Schluchter (1985)
<doi:10.1093/biomet/72.3.497>) combined with the Expectation-Maximization
with Bootstrapping (EMB) algorithm of Honaker, King and Blackwell (2011)
<doi:10.18637/jss.v045.i07>. Categorical variables are specified via the
noms option; all other variables are treated as continuous. The package
wraps the EM implementation in the 'mix' package and extends it with a
bootstrap wrapper to produce proper multiple imputations in the sense of
Rubin (1987, ISBN:978-0-471-08705-2).
glemb.author: Paul Allison [aut, cre]

gllvmTMB.title: Generalised Linear Latent Variable Models
gllvmTMB.description:
Fits multivariate generalised linear latent variable models using
either long-format data or a wide data frame. Models support several
response distributions and trait covariance structures, and can estimate
correlations, shared latent axes, and trait-specific variances. Binary
presence-absence data can be used for joint species distribution analyses.
Optional animal, phylogenetic, spatial, and kernel covariance
components are available. Estimation uses 'Template Model Builder'. Spatial
effects can use sparse Gaussian Markov random field constructions. This
0.7.1 release remains experimental: evidence for estimates is model- and
regime-specific. Broad interval coverage is not certified; a 0.94 coverage
floor is documented only for one two-sided Gaussian total-variance profile
setting.
gllvmTMB.author:
Shinichi Nakagawa [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-7765-5182>)

glt.title:
Bayesian Factor Modelling via Generalized Lower Triangular
Priors
glt.description:
Sparse Bayesian factor models for multivariate data, built
around a flexible Generalized Lower Triangular (GLT) process prior on
the loading matrix by Canale and Frühwirth-Schnatter (2026)
<doi:10.48550/arXiv.2610.09762>. The number of active factors, their
sparsity pattern, and the loadings themselves are learned jointly via
a Markov chain Monte Carlo sampler implemented in C++ with 'Rcpp' and
'RcppArmadillo'.
glt.author: Antonio Canale [aut, cre]

glpsol.title: Bundled 'GLPK' Solver for 'MathProg', 'LP' and 'MPS' Models
glpsol.description:
Ships the 'glpsol' stand-alone solver of the GNU Linear
Programming Kit ('GLPK') with R and runs it as a separate process with a
time limit and an optional live log. 'glpsol' reads 'MathProg' ('GMPL')
models with separate data files, 'CPLEX' LP and MPS files, and solves them
with the simplex, interior-point or branch-and-cut methods, writing the
solution to a file. Windows and macOS binary builds carry a static copy
of 'GLPK'; other platforms link against the system library.
glpsol.author:
Oleg Lugovoy [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-5546-9875>),
Free Software Foundation, Inc. [cph] (src/glpk/glpsol.c from 'GLPK'
5.0, see inst/COPYRIGHTS)

glyospalettes.title: Color Palettes Inspired by Glyos Colorways
glyospalettes.description:
Color palettes based on the named colorways of the Glyos toy
system: Onell Design's Glyos System Series and the Glyos-compatible lines
from partner companies such as TheGodBeast, Spy Monkey Creations, Toyfinity
and the Four Horsemen. Includes 'ggplot2' color and fill scales for discrete
and continuous data, metadata linking each palette to its company and
product line, helpers to shortlist palettes that suit categorical,
color-blind-safe, sequential or diverging use, and tools to combine
palettes (one color per colorway) or pick the most distinguishable
colors from a pool for a light, dark or grayscale plot. Hex values are
approximations curated from product photography. This is a fan project and
is not affiliated with or endorsed by any of the companies.
glyospalettes.author: Brian Maitner [aut, cre]

glymotif.title: Extract Glycan Motifs from Glycan Structures
glymotif.description:
Identify, count, and match recurring substructures in glycan structures.
Supports concrete and generic monosaccharide matching, several structural
alignment modes, node-to-node mappings, and batch analysis using subgraph
isomorphism. Includes curated motif annotations derived from the
'GlycoMotif' resource <https://glycomotif.glyomics.org/>. Integrates with
'glyrepr' and 'glyparse' for structural glycomics workflows.
glymotif.author: Bin Fu [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0001-8567-2997>)

gputools.title: GPU Drop-Ins for Statistics on Wide Data
gputools.description:
GPU versions of base R statistics for data with many
variables, using the NVIDIA 'CUDA' toolkit: correlation matrices
(Pearson, Spearman and Kendall) and their tests, the strongest
correlated pairs among tens of thousands of variables without forming
the matrix, association scans with covariates as in expression
quantitative trait loci studies (Shabalin 2012
<doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/bts163>), permutation tests with
Westfall-Young maxT adjustment, distance matrices, hierarchical and
k-means clustering, Granger causality tests, B-spline mutual
information, principal components, and least-squares fits. Results
agree with the base R functions they replace. Without 'CUDA' the
package installs, and its functions explain how to get a 'CUDA' build.
Described in Buckner et al. (2010) <doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btp608>.
gputools.author:
Josh Buckner [aut, cre],
Mark Seligman [aut],
Fan Meng [aut],
Justin Wilson [ctb]

gtxlsx.title: Write 'gt' and HTML Tables into 'openxlsx2' Workbooks
gtxlsx.description:
Turns a 'gt' table into a range of cells in an 'openxlsx2'
workbook, keeping the heading, column spanners, row groups, stub,
summary rows, footnotes and the styling set through 'gt'. Numbers stay
numbers wherever a spreadsheet number format can reproduce what 'gt' shows.
A second entry point does the same for a plain HTML table, so output
from other table packages can be written to a worksheet as well; that
path needs nothing beyond 'openxlsx2'.
gtxlsx.author: Jan Marvin Garbuszus [aut, cre]
