h2oplyr.title: Tidy Data Manipulation on Remote 'H2O' Frames
h2oplyr.description:
Provides selection, filtering, mutation, aggregation, joins,
reshaping and window operations on remote 'H2O' frames. Data manipulation
is delegated to 'H2O'; no local table backend is used. Includes an English
tutorial and reproducible examples using Palmer penguin measurements.
h2oplyr.author: Carlos Ortega [aut, cre]

hal.title: Agentic Coding Assistants
hal.description:
A native R interface to agentic coding assistants. Talks
directly to local command line interfaces ('GitHub Copilot',
'Anthropic' 'Claude Code') over standard input/output and to a local
'vscode.lm' bridge inside 'Positron', providing multi-model chat,
tool calling, and in-session R evaluation. Supports a single stateful
hal() session as well as disposable hal_ask() / hal_do() pipeline
verbs, plot capture so models can see graphics, verified data
transforms, and user-defined tools.
hal.author: Mark Dippold [aut, cre]

hairline.title: Clean, Predictable Figures for Medical and Data Science
hairline.description:
A design system for 'ggplot2' figures: one frame for titles, legends,
panels and captions, a fixed spacing and type scale, colour-vision checked
palettes, brand files in the 'brand.yml' format, and print-ready export.
Produces output matching the 'hairline' Python package.
hairline.author:
Nikolas Schrader [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0001-4616-3804>)

hdrm.title: Inference for High-Dimensional Repeated Measures
hdrm.description:
Provides one-group and multiple-group tests for expectation
vectors in high-dimensional repeated-measures designs. Hypotheses can
be specified through projection matrices or by selecting predefined
effects. The multiple-group procedures cover heterogeneous and equal
covariance matrices. Centered and standardized chi-square approximations
are combined with exact or subsampling-based trace estimators. The
functions return p-values, test statistics, estimated degrees of freedom,
and convergence parameters. For further details, see Sattler and Hichert
(2025) <doi:10.48550/arXiv.2512.17478>.
hdrm.author:
Nils Hichert [aut, cre, cph],
Paavo Sattler [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0001-8731-0893>),
Markus Pauly [ctb],
Edgar Brunner [ctb],
David Ellenberger [ctb]

hestia.title: Bayesian Compartmental Infection Models from Individual Outcomes
hestia.description:
Fit Bayesian compartmental infection models (such as
susceptible-infected-recovered and multi-compartment hidden Markov
variants) from individual-level outcome data. Models are composed
from infection-process and observation-process components and fit
using Stan via 'rstan'.
hestia.author:
Claire Perrin Smith [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-1069-9460>),
Jack Goodall [aut]

heterogeneouspeereffects.title: Heterogeneous Peer Effect
heterogeneouspeereffects.description:
Heterogeneous Peer Effect Package provides two-step Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) estimators
for heterogeneous peer effects in group-level treatment models developed by Pasquier, Rossi and Wang (2026) <https://crest.science/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/2026-11.pdf>. The
package separates the direct effect of treatment from within-group and
between-group spillover effects, using a cross-fitted, semiparametric
approach that leaves the propensity score unspecified and estimates it
nonparametrically. Two identification settings are implemented: one in
which eligibility for treatment coincides with group identity, and one
in which identity is orthogonal to eligibility, allowing peer effects to
differ across subgroups (e.g. by gender). Point estimates, standard
errors, and test statistics are returned for the direct effect and for
each within- and between-group peer effect.
heterogeneouspeereffects.author:
Felix Pasquier [aut],
Laurine Meier [aut, cre],
Pauline Rossi [aut]

hilldiv3.title: Integral Analysis of Diversity Based on Hill Numbers
hilldiv3.description:
Measures and compares the diversity of biological communities
(e.g. tables of operational taxonomic units (OTUs), amplicon sequence
variants (ASVs) or metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs)) based on Hill
numbers, in a unified framework for neutral, phylogenetic and functional
diversity measurement, diversity partitioning, (dis)similarity
measurement, diversity profiles, evenness, redundancy and attribution of
Hill power-sum weight to taxa and sets. The
statistical framework encompasses richness, Shannon and Simpson
diversity, Faith's phylogenetic diversity (PD), Rao's quadratic entropy
and Sorensen- and UniFrac-type dissimilarities, all grounded in a single
Hill-number framework. Methods are described in Jost (2007)
<doi:10.1890/06-1736.1>, Chao et al. (2010)
<doi:10.1098/rstb.2010.0272>, Chiu et al. (2014) <doi:10.1890/12-0960.1>
and reviewed in Alberdi & Gilbert (2019) <doi:10.1111/1755-0998.13014>.
Optional import adapters interoperate with the Bioconductor packages
'phyloseq', 'SummarizedExperiment' and 'TreeSummarizedExperiment',
which are available from <https://bioconductor.org>.
hilldiv3.author:
Antton Alberdi [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-2875-6446>)

hpsreg.title:
Regression for Hierarchically Ordered Clinical Outcomes via
Pairwise Comparisons (Bradley-Terry-Davidson Model)
hpsreg.description:
Provides regression for hierarchically ordered clinical
outcomes via pairwise comparisons, using a covariate-adjusted
Davidson (Bradley-Terry with ties) model with U-statistic sandwich
standard errors. A hierarchy of outcomes (binary, ordinal, continuous,
and time-to-event, with eligibility guards and tie margins) is
defined; all pairs of subjects are scored lexicographically; and the
resulting win / loss / tie data are analysed. Unadjusted win statistics
(net benefit, win ratio, win odds), diagnostics, and a worked example
based on outcomes after allogeneic stem cell transplant are also
provided. The computational engine is written in 'C++' using 'Rcpp'
and 'RcppEigen'.
hpsreg.author: Ravi Varadhan [aut, cre]

hsquared.title: 'R' Interface for 'Julia'-Backed Quantitative-Genetic Models
hsquared.description:
Provides an interface for quantitative-genetic models in 'R',
backed by the 'HSquared.jl' engine for 'Julia'. Fits Gaussian pedigree animal models
by restricted maximum likelihood, using
average-information restricted maximum likelihood (AI-REML; Gilmour et al.
(1995) <doi:10.2307/2533274>) for the univariate model. Returns heritability, variance components, breeding
values, and covariance and correlation matrices for multivariate models.
Formula and pedigree validation can run without 'Julia'. Model fitting requires a local 'Julia'
and 'HSquared.jl'; use hs_control(engine = "validate") to preview the model
contract without fitting. What you may report is listed on the package
article 'Can I fit and report this?', not in validation_status(), which is
a developer evidence table. Model-specific restrictions are documented in
that article. Uncertainty intervals are not coverage-calibrated.
hsquared.author:
Shinichi Nakagawa [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-7765-5182>),
Yefeng Yang [aut, cph] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-8610-4016>),
Szymon Drobniak [aut, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-8101-6247>)

hybridclock.title:
How Long Have Hybrids Been Forming? Hybrid Population Histories
from Diagnostic Markers
hybridclock.description:
Estimates the history of hybrid populations from diagnostic
markers, with or without a genetic map: the average age of the hybrids,
how long ago the rarer species' ancestry entered, the number of
backcrosses, and whether pure animals of the rarer species are still
arriving. Population samples of
hybrid index and interspecies heterozygosity, as defined by Fitzpatrick
(2012) <doi:10.1186/1471-2148-12-131>, are compared with forward simulations
that include drift, small breeding groups, sibling mating and separate
breeding pools, so that inbreeding is not mistaken for age. Estimates
come from 'Cubist' models with split-conformal intervals. Recent hybrids
are also classified individually, and the number of markers needed to
detect backcrossed hybrids follows Boecklen and Howard (1997)
<doi:10.1890/0012-9658(1997)078[2611:GAOHZN]2.0.CO;2>.
hybridclock.author:
Paul A. Maier [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0851-8827>)

installationDriver.title: Recursively Determine and Install Missing Dependencies
installationDriver.description: For a list of specified package, we automate recursively determining and installing the missing CRAN package dependencies ("Depends", "Imports", "LinkingTo"). The main mechanisms used are tools::package_dependencies() and utils::install.packages().
installationDriver.author: Barry Zeeberg [aut, cre]

investlabr.title: Research Workflows for Macro and Cross-Asset Analysis
investlabr.description:
Reusable research workflows for macro-financial and
cross-asset analysis. The package sits on top of data packages such
as 'investdatar' and focuses on transforming existing market and
macro data into analysis-ready research tables, factor and indicator
constructions, event and regime overlays, sensitivity estimates,
scenario comparisons, and research-grade visualization outputs.
Portfolio risk-return comparisons use the mean-variance framework of
Markowitz (1952) <doi:10.1111/j.1540-6261.1952.tb01525.x>.
Research-side volatility simulations include the generalized
autoregressive conditional heteroskedasticity model of
Bollerslev (1986) <doi:10.1016/0304-4076(86)90063-1>.
investlabr.author: Oliver Zhou [aut, cre]

irelink.title: Fast Probabilistic Record Linkage
irelink.description:
Performs fast, scalable probabilistic record linkage and
deduplication using the Fellegi-Sunter model. Records lacking a shared
unique identifier are compared across configurable dimensions using
exact, fuzzy, and distance-based comparisons, with model parameters
estimated via unsupervised Expectation-Maximization. Multiple SQL
backends are supported through 'DBI', including execution via 'DuckDB'.
This package is a translation of the Python 'splink' library by Linacre
et al. (2022) <doi:10.23889/ijpds.v7i3.1794> into idiomatic R.
irelink.author:
Christopher T. Kenny [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-9386-6860>),
Robin Linacre [cph] (Lead author of splink, the Python package this is
derived from),
Sam Lindsay [cph] (Author of splink),
Theodore Manassis [cph] (Author of splink),
Tom Hepworth [cph] (Author of splink),
Andy Bond [cph] (Author of splink),
Ross Kennedy [cph] (Author of splink),
UK Ministry of Justice [cph] (Copyright holder of splink)

irw.title: Access and Analyze Data from the Item Response Warehouse
irw.description:
Find, download, and analyze datasets from the Item Response
Warehouse, a harmonized collection of item response data
from educational and psychological measurement described in Nadela et al.
(2026) <doi:10.59863/cijg4549>. Functions search tables by metadata,
fetch them in a common long format, reshape between long and wide
layouts, simulate item response data, and compare the predictive
accuracy of fitted models with the InterModel Vigorish.
irw.author:
Hansol Lee [aut, cph],
Michael Hardy [aut, cph],
Ben Domingue [aut, cre, cph]

irtlink.title:
IRT Linking and Linking Error Estimation Across Time Points and
Groups
irtlink.description:
Estimation of trends in the mean and standard deviation
of latent ability distributions across the time points of
educational assessments, and of ability distribution differences
across linked groups, for unidimensional item response theory
(IRT) models (1PL, 2PL, 3PL, partial credit, and generalized
partial credit). Groups connected through common items, with
independent or dependent person samples, are calibrated on an
internal marginal maximum likelihood EM engine, separately,
concurrently, with fixed item parameters, or with regularized
calibration. Linking methods include mean-mean and mean-geometric
mean linking, Haberman linking (Haberman, 2009,
<doi:10.1002/j.2333-8504.2009.tb02197.x>) with robust Lp loss and
a pairwise variant (Robitzsch, 2025,
<doi:10.3390/appliedmath5010007>), and the response function
methods of Haebara and Stocking-Lord. Under differential item
functioning (DIF), the linked estimates depend on the selected
common items, and the package estimates this linking error
together with the standard error by jackknife and sandwich
estimators, including bias-corrected variants (Robitzsch, 2024,
<doi:10.3390/stats7030036>). RMSD and likelihood-ratio DIF
diagnostics with iterative purification are included.
irtlink.author:
Oskar Engels [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0008-3325-0352>)

jekylldown.title:
Create, Build and Serve 'Jekyll' Websites from 'R Markdown' and
'Quarto'
jekylldown.description:
Do for 'Jekyll' what 'blogdown' does for 'Hugo': create sites
from the most popular themes ('al-folio', 'Chirpy',
'Minimal Mistakes', 'minima'), write posts in R Markdown or 'Quarto'
that are knitted to Markdown consumed natively by 'Jekyll', customize
theme colors, fonts and elements declaratively from R, migrate
'blogdown'/'Hugo' sites, build and serve the site locally with live
reload, and diagnose the Ruby/'Jekyll' toolchain. 'Jekyll' is invoked
strictly via its command line interface; no R-Ruby language bridge is
used.
jekylldown.author: Allan Quadros [aut, cre]

kbaabb.title:
Generates an Artificial Population Based on the KBAABB
Methodology
kbaabb.description:
Provides tools for generating an artificial
population based on a kNN-based approximation to the approximate Bayesian
bootstrap (KBAABB). This methodology is described in White et al. (2025) <doi:10.1093/forestry/cpaf071>.
kbaabb.author:
Grayson W. White [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-4993-2792>),
Jerzy A. Wieczorek [aut],
Leland Russell [aut],
Samantha Schroeder [aut],
Tracey S. Frescino [aut],
Kelly S. McConville [aut]

knitroff.title: Dynamic Reports in 'troff' with 'knitr'
knitroff.description:
Write reports in 'troff' with the 'ms' macros and R code chunks
between '.SS' and '.SE', the way 'eqn' and 'tbl' blocks sit in a document,
and turn them into PDF, PostScript or a terminal draft with GNU 'groff'.
'knitr' runs the code, and its results can also be placed in the text.
knitroff.author: Daniel García [aut, cre]

l1penSVMs.title: Regularization Paths of L1-Penalized SVMs
l1penSVMs.description:
Computes regularization paths for L1-penalized support vector machine (SVM) models, including
the standard SVM, receiver operating characteristic SVM (ROC-SVM), and fraud detection SVM (FD-SVM).
The package implements efficient path algorithms to obtain solutions over a wide range of regularization parameter values.
It also provides cross-validation for selecting an optimal regularization parameter, along with functions for
prediction, visualization, and summarization of the fitted models. For more details,
see Zhu et al. (2003) <https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2003/file/49d4b2faeb4b7b9e745775793141e2b2-Paper.pdf>,
Kim et al. (2021) <doi:10.1002/sta4.400>,
Park et al. (2023) <doi:10.1007/s42952-023-00207-6>.
l1penSVMs.author:
Hyungwoo Kim [aut, cre],
Minhyoung Park [aut],
Seung Jun Shin [aut]

lambdastar.title: Measurement and Linear Hypothesis Models for Lambda Star
lambdastar.description:
Estimates intrinsic and captured noncentrality from parallel
measurements and evaluates the numerical parsimony functional for an
explicitly encoded hypothesis matrix, formula, or compatible linear model.
Includes common-case model comparisons, quantized entropy capacity,
controlled temperature integration, and explicit singularity diagnostics.
Uses manuscript projection estimates by default, with an explicit alternative
population estimator. Supports common nuisance adjustment and ordinary case
or cluster percentile bootstrap intervals, with diagnostics for undefined
estimates and preserved model coding.
Provides reusable row-bound design specifications and explicit conditional
term blocks, named linear restrictions, explicit predictor-grid contrasts,
and fixed or reevaluated basis recipes under a homogeneous isotropic
measurement-fluctuation assumption. Supports explicit known-reference
mean hypotheses and paired differences from parallel measurement pairs.
Encodes fixed person-by-occasion models with parallel indicators, implicit
person adjustment and whole-person bootstrap with distinct sampled copies.
The underlying method is described in Hammes (2026)
<doi:10.5281/zenodo.22962377>.
lambdastar.author: Mike Hammes [aut, cre, cph]

land4health.title: Remote Sensing Metrics for Spatial Health Analysis
land4health.description:
Calculate and extract remote sensing metrics for spatial analysis in the field of health.
The package offers R users a quick and straightforward way to obtain areal or zonal statistics of key environmental indicators, covariates, and vector-borne disease data ideal for modeling infectious diseases within the framework of spatial epidemiology.
land4health.author:
Antony Barja [aut, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-5921-2858>),
Yomali Ferreyra [cre] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-5184-9595>),
Diego Villa [ctb]

lande.title: Tools for Evolutionary Selection Analysis
lande.description:
Estimates selection differentials and linear, quadratic and
correlational selection gradients on relative fitness following Lande and
Arnold (1983) <doi:10.1111/j.1558-5646.1983.tb00236.x>, with p-values from
the logistic model for survival and from a Poisson or negative binomial
model for counts. Fits cubic spline fitness functions as in Schluter (1988)
<doi:10.1111/j.1558-5646.1988.tb02507.x> and two-trait fitness surfaces
drawn only where there are data, and computes adaptive landscapes of mean
fitness against the population mean for one or two traits, by period and
for several groups on one surface. Includes bootstrap intervals, a
combined results table and a Shiny app.
lande.author:
Vanessa Zhou [aut] (affiliation: College of Computing, Georgia
Institute of Technology, Atlanta, GA, United States),
Ali Sean Khan [aut] (affiliation: College of Computing, Georgia
Institute of Technology, Atlanta, GA, United States),
Calvin Yu [aut] (affiliation: College of Computing, Georgia Institute
of Technology, Atlanta, GA, United States),
Taylor Papke [aut] (affiliation: College of Computing, Georgia
Institute of Technology, Atlanta, GA, United States),
Dima Al Nabhani [aut] (affiliation: College of Computing, Georgia
Institute of Technology, Atlanta, GA, United States),
Guillermo Garcia-Costoya [aut] (affiliation: School of Biological
Sciences, Georgia Institute of Technology, Atlanta, GA, United
States),
James T. Stroud [aut, cre] (affiliation: School of Biological Sciences,
Georgia Institute of Technology, Atlanta, GA, United States)

lassoinf.title: Selective Inference for the Randomized Lasso
lassoinf.description:
Confidence intervals and p-values for parameters chosen by the
(randomized) lasso, valid after selection. Implements the polyhedral
approach of Lee, Sun, Sun and Taylor (2016) <doi:10.1214/15-AOS1371>,
the randomized response of Tian and Taylor (2018) <doi:10.1214/17-AOS1564>
and the exact randomized inference of Panigrahi, Fry and Taylor (2024)
<doi:10.1093/biomet/asae019>, with the truncated bivariate normal
computations of Liu (2023) <doi:10.48550/arXiv.2308.10346>. Includes
inference for user-specified estimands, screening of inactive variables
and problems fitted by 'glmnet'. Computations use a 'C++' backend with
matrix-free linear operators for wide designs.
lassoinf.author:
Jonathan Taylor [aut, cre, cph],
Kevin Fry [aut],
Snigdha Panigrahi [aut],
Sifan Liu [ctb, cph] (truncated bivariate normal computations, see
inst/COPYRIGHTS)

latents.title: Multilevel Latent Profile, Class and Transition Models
latents.description:
Provides functions for fitting multilevel latent profile
analysis, latent class, and latent transition models for continuous,
categorical, and mixed-type variables. Models are estimated by expectation-maximization,
handle missing data, and provide standard and robust standard errors.
Model selection is supported by information criteria, entropy,
classification diagnostics, and a parametric bootstrap likelihood ratio
test. Covariates can be related to latent class membership using
three-step methods with correction for classification error. Latent
transition models estimate transitions between latent profiles across
ordered occasions and are compatible with the 'tna' package for network
and sequence analysis. The multilevel mixture formulation follows Vermunt
(2003) <doi:10.1111/j.0081-1750.2003.t01-1-00131.x>.
latents.author:
Mohammed Saqr [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-5881-3109>),
Sonsoles López-Pernas [aut] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-9621-1392>)

lczexplore.title:
Imports, Visualizes, Compares and Explores Maps of Local Climate
Zones
lczexplore.description:
Easily import and visualize local climate zone maps with standard encoding.
Compare two or more maps, and group some LCZ types according to user defined grouping vectors.
Explore their differences through circular visualization and indicators. For more Details see
Gousseff et al (2023) "lczexplore: an R package to explore Local Climate Zone classifications" <doi:10.21105/joss.05445>.
lczexplore.author:
Matthieu Gousseff [aut, cre, cph] (affiliation: Centre National de la
Recherche Scientifique, Lab-STICC, ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-7106-2677>)

ldpdist.title: Local Differential Privacy Tools for Distributional Inference
ldpdist.description:
Estimates cumulative distribution functions and quantiles under
local differential privacy. Provides isotonic and divide-and-conquer
distribution estimators, aggregation across independent surveys, online
inference for single and multiple quantiles, and asymptotic quantile
confidence sequences. Also estimates category-specific subdistribution
functions under asymmetric local privacy. Binary and categorical
randomization mechanisms support these procedures. Distribution
estimators operate on privatized reports; quantile interfaces simulate
sequential local randomization internally. Published methodological
sources include Liu et al. (2023)
<https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/liu23q.html>, Liu, Hu and Kong (2024)
<https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/liu24z.html>, Cai et al. (2025)
<doi:10.52202/085713-3818>, and Hu and Liu (2026)
<https://proceedings.mlr.press/v306/hu26ae.html>.
ldpdist.author:
Yi Liu [aut, cre],
Qirui Hu [aut]

learnr2.title: Interactive Tutorials with 'Quarto' and 'WebR'
learnr2.description:
Create interactive R tutorials that run entirely in the
browser using 'Quarto' <https://quarto.org> and 'WebR'
<https://docs.r-wasm.org/webr/latest/> via the 'quarto-live' extension.
Provides 'learnr'-style authoring conveniences -- scaffolding, exercises,
hints, solutions, and quizzes -- without 'Shiny', 'R Markdown', or a
server.
learnr2.author:
David Kane [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-6660-3934>),
Minh Vu [aut]

legiretraite.title:
Recueil De Paramètres Législatifs et Réglementaires Sur Les
Retraites Françaises
legiretraite.description:
Fournit un recueil de paramètres législatifs et réglementaires
sur les retraites françaises, ainsi que des fonctions pour rechercher ces
paramètres par génération et catégorie d'assuré et pour reconstituer les
échantillons des enquêtes interrégimes EIR et EIC de la DREES.
legiretraite.author:
Mélissa M'Piayi [aut],
Mathieu Sigal [aut],
Ambroise Warnery [aut],
Pierre Cheloudko [aut],
Arthur Katossky [cre, aut],
Direction de la recherche, des études, de l'évaluation et des
statistiques (DREES), Observation de la solidarité (OSOL), Bureau
des retraites (BRET) [cph]

lepidoptera.title:
Domain-Agnostic Causal Simulation Engine with Mixed Variable
Types
lepidoptera.description:
A domain-agnostic simulation engine for structural causal models
with heterogeneous variable types. Users define systems of continuous,
categorical, and ordinal features, declare a directed acyclic graph (DAG)
over them, attach typed generative mechanisms to each node, and simulate
synthetic populations. A pre-built mechanism library covers all nine
parent-type/child-type combinations. Vine copula mechanisms estimate full
joint dependence from observed data via pair-copula constructions
(Bedford and Cooke, 2002) <doi:10.1214/aos/1031689014>. Individual-level
counterfactual queries are supported through partial propagation, which
freezes unaffected random draws and resamples only the downstream subgraph,
enabling individual treatment effect (ITE) estimation alongside
population-level average treatment effects (ATE). Any pre-fitted predictive
model can serve as a generative mechanism through three wrapper functions.
Systems serialise to JSON for cross-language portability with the companion
Python package.
lepidoptera.author: Danilo Sarti [aut, cre]

likingInitiative.title: Access the Liking Rating Database
likingInitiative.description:
Download and work with the Liking Rating Database, a curated
collection of subjective liking ratings from published decision-making
studies, described in Fernandez, Goyal and Krajbich (2026)
<doi:10.5281/zenodo.22216442>. Data is read from versioned release files
and cached for the session, so a pinned version returns the same rows
regardless of when it is run. Provides access by dataset, by item across
studies, or as the whole corpus, together with the metadata and citations
needed to report it.
likingInitiative.author: Kianté Fernandez [aut, cre, cph]

lillardhaz.title:
Simultaneous-Equations Hazard/Probit Models with a
Gaussian-Copula Correlation
lillardhaz.description:
Fits two-equation simultaneous models in the style of
Lillard (1993) <doi:10.1016/0304-4076(93)90106-F>: a pair of processes,
each either a binary probit outcome or a continuous-time hazard
duration, linked through a single correlation parameter between their
underlying error terms and estimated jointly by maximum likelihood via
a Gaussian copula. Equation 1 may be a probit, a log-normal
accelerated-failure-time hazard, or a piecewise (linear-log-hazard)
Gompertz hazard with an arbitrary, user-specified number of segments;
equation 2 is always a hazard, log-normal or piecewise Gompertz. Models
can also be fit under independence (correlation fixed at zero), which
reduces exactly to two separate univariate fits. See the package
vignette/manual for the full likelihood derivation and a
simulation-based verification.
lillardhaz.author: Nobutaka Fukuda [aut, cre]

limestab.title:
Stable Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME,
OptiLIME, BayLIME, ALIME)
limestab.description:
Provides four local explanation methods for tabular data: LIME, OptiLIME, BayLIME, and ALIME, together with the stability metrics used to compare them across repeated explanations of the same instance: the Coefficient Stability Index (CSI), the Variable Stability Index (VSI), Median Rank Matching Stability (MRMS), Point-Based Stability Index (PCSI), and Interval Coefficient Stability Index (ICSI).
The methodology accompanies Toparlak and Purutcuoglu, "A Median-Based
Framework for Assessing the Stability in XAI Tools" (manuscript under
revision); the citation will be updated upon publication.
limestab.author:
Simay Toparlak [aut] (affiliation: Department of Biomedical
Engineering, Middle East Technical University),
Vilda Purutcuoglu [aut, cre] (affiliation: Department of Statistics,
Middle East Technical University)

localdatasus.title: Neighborhood-Level Data from Brazil's Unified Health System
localdatasus.description:
Retrieves health data from Brazil's Unified Health System
(Sistema Único de Saúde, SUS) at the neighborhood level, with 2022
Census population, rates per 10,000 inhabitants, coordinates and maps.
Simple functions return deaths, live births, notifiable diseases,
hospital admissions, outpatient consultations, emergency (SAMU) calls
and health facilities by neighborhood, choosing the data source
automatically: microdata with the patient's postal code (CEP),
downloaded with the 'microdatasus' package of Saldanha, Bastos and
Barcellos (2019) <doi:10.1590/0102-311x00032419>; files and open data
published by health departments; and regional 'TabNet' tabulators
that tabulate by neighborhood or district. Postal codes and
neighborhood names are linked to the official neighborhoods of the
Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics (IBGE) through the
National Address Register for Statistical Purposes (CNEFE) and the
2022 Census tracts, with quality rules for generic postal codes.
Function names, arguments, messages and documentation are in
Portuguese, aimed at Brazilian health researchers.
localdatasus.author:
Hendesson Alves [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0009-0342-9201>)

ltvlms.title: Linear Time-Variant Logistic Models with a Shape Parameter
ltvlms.description:
Evaluates and fits the Linear Time-Variant Logistic Model with
Shape Parameter (LTVLMS) for dynamic growth processes. The model combines
a linearly time-varying growth rate with a shape parameter for asymmetric
trajectories and includes numerically stable prediction utilities.
Methodological details are provided by Betrouni and Kernane (2026)
"Linear Time-Varying Logistic Model With Shape Parameter for Dynamic
Epidemic Modeling" <doi:10.1155/jama/4928447>.
ltvlms.author:
Redouane Betrouni [aut] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-7374-4391>),
Tewfik Kernane [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-8423-567X>),
Bander Hussein [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0007-3850-1598>)

lwpls.title: Locally-Weighted Partial Least Squares for 'tidymodels'
lwpls.description:
Locally-weighted partial least squares (LW-PLS) is a
just-in-time learning method that builds a dedicated weighted partial
least squares model around every new sample, where training samples
are weighted by their similarity to that sample (Kim et al. (2011)
<doi:10.1016/j.ijpharm.2011.10.007>). Regression (single or multiple
outcomes) and classification (locally weighted partial least
squares-discriminant analysis; Bevilacqua and Marini (2014)
<doi:10.1016/j.aca.2014.05.057>) are supported. The local models can
be robust to outliers, by partial robust M-regression (Serneels et al.
(2005) <doi:10.1016/j.chemolab.2005.04.007>), and sparse (Hoffmann et
al. (2015) <doi:10.1016/j.chemolab.2015.09.019>). The prediction kernel
is written in C++ with 'RcppArmadillo', and the model is integrated
with the 'parsnip', 'dials', 'tune' and 'yardstick' packages so it can
be used within the 'tidymodels' framework. Diagnostics of the local
models (prediction reliability, local regression vectors, robust
weights and selected predictors) come with 'ggplot2' plots designed for
spectroscopic data.
lwpls.author:
Christian L. Goueguel [aut, cre],
Hiromasa Kaneko [cph] (reference LW-PLS implementation transcribed in
the tests)

maxtwin.title: A Robust Deterministic Data Splitting Method
maxtwin.description:
Provides a deterministic method for splitting data into training
and testing sets that maximizes the distance between training and testing
points while preserving their distributions. See Joseph and Cho (in press)
for details. This work is supported by U.S. National Science Foundation
grant DMS-2310637.
maxtwin.author:
Youngseo Cho [aut, cre],
V. Roshan Joseph [aut]

metalabr.title: Access MetaLab Community-Augmented Meta-Analysis Data
metalabr.description:
Read released, versioned data from MetaLab
(<https://metalab.stanford.edu>), a database of community-augmented
meta-analyses of language acquisition and cognitive development;
validate candidate datasets against the MetaLab field specification;
compute standardized effect sizes; and draw the standard MetaLab
visualizations (scatter, violin, forest, and funnel plots) backed by
multilevel random-effects models.
metalabr.author:
Erik Iverson [aut],
Sara El-Shawa [aut],
Michael C. Frank [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-7551-4378>),
MetaLab contributors [cph]

metamixr.title: Bayesian Meta-Analytic Mixture Modelling
metamixr.description:
Fits Bayesian random-effects meta-analytic mixture models in which
the true study effects are drawn from a mixture of normal components with
component-specific means and between-study heterogeneity. The mixture model
can be combined with step-function selection models (Vevea and Hedges, 1995,
<doi:10.1007/BF02294384>) to adjust for publication bias, either with one
selection model for all studies or with separate selection models for
groups of studies. Models are estimated by Hamiltonian Monte Carlo using
'rstan' and returned as 'stanfit' objects, so posterior summaries,
posterior predictive checks and marginal likelihoods for model comparison
(via 'bridgesampling') are readily available. Also includes a data
simulator and the nudging meta-analysis data of Mertens et al. (2022)
<doi:10.1073/pnas.2107346118>.
metamixr.author:
Maximilian Maier [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-9873-6096>),
Trustees of Columbia University [cph]

metaweave.title: Spatial Ecological Network Inference
metaweave.description:
A model-agnostic framework for reconstructing and analysing
spatially explicit ecological networks from species distributions and
ecological inference models. Supports arbitrary ecological groups and
includes stochastic block and maximum-entropy inference backends,
simulation helpers, network summaries, and spatial mapping utilities.
metaweave.author: Gabriel Munoz [aut, cre, cph] (Affiliation: Concordia University)

metricT.title: Directional Fragility Diagnostics for EEG Connectivity
metricT.description:
Implements Metric-T, a permutation-based diagnostic that flags
when the reported direction of a group difference in
electroencephalography (EEG) functional connectivity depends on the
choice of metric. Direction consistency (DC)
converts the weighted phase lag index (wPLI) and magnitude-squared
coherence (MSC), both derived from the same cross-spectrum, into the
percentage of channel-pair features for which one group exceeds the
other; Metric-T is T = DC(wPLI) - DC(MSC). Significance is assessed by
aligned label permutation with marginal and Westfall-Young max-T
multiplicity control. For small samples the reference set is enumerated
completely: exact two-group tests, the complete two-group labelling
space (in which cut-points, exclusions and batches are located on one
distribution), and a stratified exact test for a continuous covariate.
Core functions use base R only; a 'shiny' graphical interface is
included. Method: Kimura (2026) <doi:10.1016/j.neuri.2026.100286>.
metricT.author:
Akira Kimura [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0220-5678>)

metrictrails.title: Processing of GNSS Streams from Sports Watches
metrictrails.description:
Tools to read, clean and standardise GNSS (Global Navigation
Satellite System) streams recorded by sports watches and similar devices,
with a focus on trail and mountain running. The pipeline reads GPX files,
applies a naming convention, sanitises coordinates (Kalman, LOESS,
Gaussian kernel or Savitzky-Golay smoothing, and red flags for implausible
readings), resamples the trajectory to a uniform spatial resolution derived
from the Nyquist criterion, and replaces elevation with values from a
Digital Elevation Model. Derived measures include speed, slope, elevation
gain and kilometre-effort, Tobler hiking function parameters fitted by
quantile regression, comparison between streams, detection of passes
along a route and map matching to a known reference trail by dynamic
programming. Methods follow Sanchez and Villena (2020)
<doi:10.1177/1754337120918975>, Sanchez et al. (2024)
<doi:10.1109/ICECET61485.2024.10698606>, Sanchez et al. (2025)
<doi:10.1177/17543371251341660> and Martinez, Sanchez and Diaz (2026)
<doi:10.1109/ICECET65726.2026.11632531>.
metrictrails.author:
Raimundo Sanchez [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-2242-1335>)

mirrorslope.title: Mirror Slope Plots for Two-Arm Clinical Trial Data
mirrorslope.description:
Creates mirrored slope plots comparing two treatment arms over a
single observation interval. Both arms share a common x-axis and converge
at a central endpoint, making the between-arm gap the primary visual
quantity. Returns standard 'ggplot2' objects for full extensibility.
The display was designed by Kati Maharry and is described in Maharry and
Sullivan (2026, manuscript in preparation); it was first used in the
supplementary appendix of McDonald and colleagues (2026)
<doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(26)01385-1>.
mirrorslope.author:
Adam Sullivan [aut, cre],
Capricor Therapeutics [fnd]

misocialr.title:
Access the Brazilian 'MDS' Social Information Matrix ('MI
Social') API from 'R'
misocialr.description:
'Tidyverse'-friendly interface to the 'MI Social' API of the Brazilian
Ministry of Development and Social Assistance ('MDS', 'SAGI')
<https://aplicacoes.mds.gov.br/sagi/servicos/misocial>. Retrieves monthly
municipal series of the 'Cadastro Unico' (registered families and people by
income bracket), the 'Bolsa Familia' programme (beneficiary families, benefits
and transfers), the 'BPC' benefit, the social assistance network ('CRAS',
'CREAS' and other units), 'SUAS' funding, 'Bolsa Familia' conditionality
monitoring and food security programmes as tidy long-format 'tibbles'.
misocialr.author:
André Leite [aut, cre] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-4718-9766>),
Marcos Wasiliew [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0009-0004-4694-3159>),
Hugo Vasconcelos [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0001-6249-0920>),
Carlos Amorim [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0001-6315-8305>),
Diogo Bezerra [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1216-8674>)

modelname.title: Parse AI Model Names into Vendor, Family and Version
modelname.description:
Splits the identifiers and display names that AI labs give
their models, such as 'claude-opus-4-1-20250805', 'gpt-4.1-mini' or
'Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview', into vendor, family, version, parameter size,
release date and tags. Old and new naming schemes from 'Anthropic',
'OpenAI', 'Google' and 'OpenRouter' land in the same family, so models
can be compared and the newest one in a family picked from a list. A
port of the 'Go' module 'modelname'
<https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/BoNour/modelname>.
modelname.author: Nour Ayman [aut, cre, cph]

mongolmaps.title: Maps and Administrative Boundaries of Mongolia and Ulaanbaatar
mongolmaps.description:
Ready-to-use 'sf' maps of Mongolia at every openly available
administrative level: country, economic regions, aimags (provinces),
soums and Ulaanbaatar districts, and Ulaanbaatar khoroos
(subdistricts), with codes and names for every bag. Provides a
crosswalk between English and Cyrillic names, common spelling
variants, ISO 3166-2 codes, humanitarian P-codes and National
Statistics Office codes; helpers to join statistics to maps; thematic
layers (settlements, rivers, lakes, roads, railways, airports,
elevation, land cover, population and protected areas); and quick
'ggplot2' and 'leaflet' maps. Boundaries derive from the Common
Operational Dataset published by the National Statistics Office of
Mongolia and the United Nations Office for the Coordination of
Humanitarian Affairs <https://data.humdata.org/dataset/cod-ab-mng>.
mongolmaps.author: Temuulen Enebish [aut, cre, cph]

mospiR.title: Client for the 'MoSPI' Microdata Portal
mospiR.description:
Download unit-level survey microdata from the Ministry of
Statistics and Programme Implementation ('MoSPI', Government of India)
Microdata Portal <https://microdata.gov.in>. Provides functions to list
datasets, list files within a dataset, and download individual files or
entire datasets through the portal's 'NADA' API.
mospiR.author:
Saket Choudhary [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-5202-7633>)

mudnester.title: Surveillance Data Cleaning and Preparation for Public Health
mudnester.description:
Clean, prepare, and aggregate surveillance data for public health analysis.
Provides structural data cleaning and standardisation (clean_the_nest()),
age categorisation against ~50 published schemes with publication-ready
labelling (preening()), time-unit aggregation with zero-filling and
seasonal awareness (roost()), joint aggregation of several linked event
dates (e.g. onset, admission, ICU, complication, fatality) into one table of
comparable rate columns (flyway()), under-ascertainment correction via a
stratified, time-varying multiplier factor supplied directly, derived by the
ratio (multiplier) method, or derived by inverting an externally sourced
severity rate (e.g. an infection-fatality-rate anchor) against an observed
severity ratio (corncrake()), comorbidity detection from ICD-10-AM
clinical coding (plumage()), vaccine coverage data construction
(brood()), hash-based de-identification (molting()), and relinking
of previously de-identified data (homing()). brood() produces a
brood_df object supporting two population models: pre-aggregated
denominators (population_model = "pre_aggregated") and record-level cohort
designs (population_model = "cohort"). The cohort model handles single
time-point coverage snapshots, interrupted time series analysis via a
built-in sweep returning monthly coverage rates (time_series = TRUE), and
birth cohort designs with person-time computation. This cohort/time-series
coverage model was applied in Roughan et al. (2026)
<doi:10.33321/cdi.2026.50.031> to estimate infant immunisation coverage
against respiratory syncytial virus over an 18-month period. Both wide
format (one row per person with dose columns, from
'starling'::murmuration()) and long format (one row per dose) are accepted.
corncrake() returns both a point-corrected count and uncertainty bounds
wherever they can be derived, including the inverse relationship between a
severity-anchored factor and the bounds of its own reference rate. Built for
Australian public health surveillance practice but not specific to it -- see
individual function documentation for notes on non-Australian use (e.g.
Northern Hemisphere season boundaries).
mudnester.author:
Nicolas Smoll [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-6923-9701>),
Moderna [fnd] (Support for this package's development was provided via
the Moderna Global Research Fellowship)

multigrain.title: Optimise Graphical Approaches to Multiple Testing Procedures
multigrain.description:
Find the optimal graphical multiple testing procedure for
confirmatory clinical trials that test several hypotheses across
endpoints, doses, or subpopulations. Choose the graph maximising an explicit
gain-function: a user-defined measure of trial success that scores each
possible set of rejected hypotheses. Given simulated p-values, search over
hypothesis weights and transition weights to maximise expected trial
success. Conventional power criteria are recovered and the family-wise error
rate is strongly controlled due to the search being confined to graphical
procedures. Described in Spiers, Grayling, Wheeler, and Mander (2026)
"Gain-function optimisation of graphical multiple testing procedures for
confirmatory clinical trials" <doi:10.48550/arXiv.2609.19994>.
multigrain.author:
Alex Spiers [aut, cre] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-8874-085X>),
Dragoș Moldovan-Grünfeld [aut],
GlaxoSmithKline Research & Development Limited [cph, fnd]

multipathaic.title: Multi-Path Stepwise Selection with AIC
multipathaic.description:
Implements a multi-path forward selection algorithm using the Akaike
Information Criterion (AIC) for both linear (Gaussian) and logistic (binomial)
regression models. Unlike traditional stepwise methods that follow a single path,
this approach explores multiple competitive model paths simultaneously by retaining
near-optimal models at each step. The package includes stability estimation via
bootstrap resampling and identifies plausible models based on AIC tolerance and
variable stability thresholds. The information criterion is described by
Akaike (1974) <doi:10.1109/TAC.1974.1100705>, and bootstrap resampling
by Efron (1979) <doi:10.1214/aos/1176344552>.
multipathaic.author: Michael Obuobi [aut, cre]

n3d.title: Speaker Diarization with 'Nemotron 3 Diarization' in R 'torch'
n3d.description:
Determines "who spoke when" in recorded or streaming audio with
a native R 'torch' implementation of the 'NVIDIA' 'Nemotron 3
Diarization' model <https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-3-Diarization>,
a Streaming 'Sortformer' that tracks up to eight speakers in order of
first arrival. Log-mel feature extraction, the transformer encoder and
the arrival-order speaker cache are implemented in R; weights are
downloaded from 'Hugging Face' with the 'hfhub' package on request.
n3d.author:
Troy Hernandez [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0005-4248-604X>),
cornball.ai [cph],
The HuggingFace Team [cph] (portions ported from the transformers
library (Apache-2.0); see inst/COPYRIGHTS)

namegender.title: Client for the 'NameGender' Name-to-Gender API
namegender.description:
Infer the likely gender of first names, email addresses and
usernames, and the country distribution of a name, through the
'NameGender' web API <https://namegender.com>. Each answer carries the
share and number of records behind it and the data version that
produced it, so results can be reported and reproduced in research.
Also returns letter salutations, checks whether a name looks like a
real person's name, runs 'CSV' and 'XLSX' files as file jobs, and
verifies the signature of 'NameGender' webhooks. An API key is needed.
namegender.author:
Anıl Pekesen [aut, cre],
NameGender [cph]

nesstarR.title: Read and Export 'Nesstar' Binary Files
nesstarR.description:
Reads '.Nesstar' binary files into data frames. '.Nesstar'
is the file format of 'Nesstar Publisher', survey documentation software
from the International Household Survey Network
<https://www.ihsn.org/node/557>. Statistical agencies, for example the
Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation ('MoSPI', India),
publish survey microdata in this format.
nesstarR.author:
Saket Choudhary [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-5202-7633>)

netmatchRI.title: Network-Constrained Matching and Randomization-Based Inference
netmatchRI.description:
Provides network-constrained matching and randomization-based
inference for observational network data with dependence and interference.
Dual-penalty matching minimizes total covariate dissimilarity while
enforcing penalties on network proximity between and within treatment arms in matched sets.
Randomization-based inference combines evidence from correlated matched sets based on this design.
The package also provides covariate-balance and network-distance diagnostics,
sensitivity analysis, and simulated example data.
The open-source 'HiGHS' solver is used by
default to solve the matching problem.
An optional interface to the commercial 'Gurobi Optimizer' is available.
Eligible academic users can request a free license at
<https://www.gurobi.com/academics/>. The optimizer can be downloaded from
<https://www.gurobi.com/product/download-center>. The associated 'gurobi'
R package is not available from CRAN; it is distributed with the optimizer
and can be installed by following the official instructions at
<https://docs.gurobi.com/projects/optimizer/en/current/reference/r/setup.html>.
netmatchRI.author: Zhejia Dong [aut, cre]

networkformat.title: Convert R Objects to Network Edgelists and Nodelists
networkformat.description:
Network analysis and plotting packages such as 'igraph',
'tidygraph', and 'ggraph' expect the edges and nodes of a graph as flat
tables. Methods are provided to build those tables from data frames
(column-pair edges chosen with 'tidyselect' semantics), tree-based model
objects ('randomForest', 'tree', 'rpart', 'xgboost', 'gbm'), lists
(recursive parent-child edges), and atomic vectors (sequential edges).
Graphs can also be constructed in one step via as.igraph() and
as_tbl_graph() methods for tree models.
networkformat.author:
Jesse Brandt [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0005-7462-075X>)

nrMCmix.title: Non-Reversible Markov Chains for Bayesian Mixture Models
nrMCmix.description: Provides Bayesian inference for finite and infinite mixture models using Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods. Supports Gaussian, multivariate Gaussian, Poisson, Binomial, and multivariate Bernoulli mixture kernels with different covariance structures and flexible prior specifications. Provides tools for data generation, posterior density evaluation, clustering and similarity analysis, and advanced MCMC sampling strategies, including reversible and non-reversible samplers: Ascolani et al. (2026) <doi:10.48550/arXiv.2510.03226>, informed proposals: Zanella (2020) <doi:10.1080/01621459.2019.1585255>, collapsed Gibbs sampling: Diebolt and Robert (1994) <doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1994.tb01985.x>, and split-and-merge samplers: Dahl and Newcomb (2021) <doi:10.1080/00949655.2021.1998502>.
nrMCmix.author:
Filippo Ascolani [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0009-0009-3899-8877>),
Paolo Manildo [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0006-7056-7012>),
Giacomo Zanella [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0001-6727-9884>)

ocupacoesBR.title:
Traduz a Ocupação Declarada ao TSE em Classificações
Padronizadas. English: Translates Occupations Declared to the
TSE into Standardized Classifications
ocupacoesBR.description:
Traduz a ocupação registrada em fontes brasileiras para a Classificação
Internacional Uniforme de Ocupações (ISCO-88 e ISCO-08) e, a partir dela,
para medidas padronizadas de posição social: o índice socioeconômico ISEI
(Ganzeboom e Treiman, 1996 <doi:10.1006/ssre.1996.0010>), o prestígio
SIOPS (Treiman, 1977, ISBN:0-12-698750-5), o esquema de classes
Erikson-Goldthorpe-Portocarero (EGP; Erikson, Goldthorpe e Portocarero,
1979 <doi:10.2307/589632>) e um esquema de classes e estratos desenhado
para o dado eleitoral. Traz ainda o ISEI-BR, uma régua estimada pelo
pacote: o procedimento de Ganzeboom, De Graaf e Treiman (1992)
<doi:10.1016/0049-089X(92)90017-B> refeito sobre a PNAD Contínua, em vez
de importado de dado estrangeiro. As decisões de medida estão justificadas
em Peixoto (2026) <doi:10.31235/osf.io/b29kg_v1>. Há duas portas de
entrada: o código de ocupação declarado nas
candidaturas ao Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) e a Classificação
Brasileira de Ocupações (CBO-2002 e CBO-94), usada na RAIS, no CAGED e no
eSocial. As tabelas de conversão derivam das sintaxes publicadas do
International Stratification and Mobility File (Ganzeboom e Treiman) e da
tábua oficial de conversão do Ministério do Trabalho, e são geradas por
script a partir dos arquivos originais, nunca transcritas manualmente. O
dicionário que leva o código do TSE à ISCO-88 é, ao lado do ISEI-BR, a outra
peça autoral: foi construído pelo autor, código a código, e é validado
contra patrimônio e escolaridade das próprias candidaturas.
English: Translates occupation as recorded in Brazilian sources into the
International Standard Classification of Occupations (ISCO-88 and
ISCO-08) and, from it, into standardized measures of social position: the
International Socio-Economic Index (ISEI; Ganzeboom and Treiman, 1996
<doi:10.1006/ssre.1996.0010>), the Standard International Occupational
Prestige Scale (SIOPS; Treiman, 1977, ISBN:0-12-698750-5), the
Erikson-Goldthorpe-Portocarero (EGP) class scheme (Erikson, Goldthorpe and
Portocarero, 1979 <doi:10.2307/589632>) and a class and strata scheme
designed for electoral data. It also provides ISEI-BR, a scale estimated
by the package itself: the procedure of Ganzeboom, De Graaf and Treiman
(1992) <doi:10.1016/0049-089X(92)90017-B> is re-estimated on Brazil's
Continuous National Household Sample Survey (PNAD Contínua) instead of
importing scores estimated on foreign data. The measurement decisions are
justified in Peixoto (2026) <doi:10.31235/osf.io/b29kg_v1>. There are two
entry points: the occupation code that candidates declare when
registering with Brazil's Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior
Eleitoral, TSE), and the Brazilian Classification of Occupations
(CBO-2002 and CBO-94), used in the RAIS, CAGED and eSocial administrative
records. The conversion tables derive from the published syntax files of
the International Stratification and Mobility File (Ganzeboom and
Treiman) and from the official conversion table of Brazil's Ministry of
Labor, and are generated by script from the original files, never
transcribed by hand. Alongside ISEI-BR, the dictionary that maps TSE
occupation codes to ISCO-88 is the package's other original contribution:
it was built by the author code by code and is validated against the
declared assets and education of the candidates themselves.
ocupacoesBR.author:
Vitor Peixoto [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-6618-3311>)

oddsrelay.title: Client for the 'OddsRelay' Sports Odds API
oddsrelay.description:
Provides one function for each read endpoint of the
'OddsRelay' web service <https://oddsrelay.io/docs>, which serves
bookmaker and exchange odds for the UK and Ireland. Requests ask for
compressed replies, send entity tags so that unchanged data is not
transferred again, wait as the service asks when it is busy, and signal
refusals as classed conditions that carry the service's error code and
request id. Replies are returned as lists and data frames, with the
token and rate limit headers attached as attributes.
oddsrelay.author:
James OddsRelay [aut, cre],
OddsRelay [cph]

oeis.tools.title: Access and Visualize Integer Sequences from the OEIS
oeis.tools.description:
Programmatic access, analysis, and visualization of integer
sequences from the On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences (OEIS)
<https://oeis.org>. Fetches sequence metadata and b-files, stores terms as
arbitrary-precision integers via 'gmp', and plots them with 'ggplot2'.
oeis.tools.author: Enrique Pérez Herrero [aut, cre]

oes.title: Optimal Effect-Size-Based Y-Axis Ranges
oes.description:
Calculates effect-size-informed y-axis recommendations for
visualizations of independent, repeated-measures, and mixed designs.
Summarizes selected error bars, estimates conditional standardized
contrasts, and generalizes range-expansion rules using constants from
single-factor, two-level studies of Cohen's d. Recommendations beyond
that studied setting have not been empirically validated.
Provides numerical results and 'ggplot2' visualizations, including
summary plots and preservation of supplied plot layouts.
Confidence-interval adjustment options follow the distinctions in
Cousineau (2017) <doi:10.5709/acp-0214-z>, including difference
adjustment and combined repeated-measures adjustment. Within-subject
base intervals use the normalization of Cousineau (2005)
<doi:10.20982/tqmp.01.1.p042> with the bias correction of Morey (2008)
<doi:10.20982/tqmp.04.2.p061>. Correlation-only intervals and intervals
with both adjustments are separate options. These references support
confidence-interval construction, not the range-expansion calibration.
oes.author:
Shuo Zang [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0000-4387-8145>, affiliation: School of
Psychology, University of Ottawa),
Denis Cousineau [aut, cph] (affiliation: School of Psychology,
University of Ottawa)

opentimsr.title: An Open-Source Loader for Bruker's timsTOF Data Files
opentimsr.description:
Reads raw data from Bruker's timsTOF mass spectrometers,
stored in analysis.tdf and analysis.tdf_bin files inside .d folders.
Frames can be selected by number or by retention time, and each peak is
reported with its scan, time-of-flight index, intensity, mass-to-charge
ratio and inverse ion mobility. Mass-to-charge ratios and ion mobilities
are computed with built-in open-source calibration, or optionally with
Bruker's proprietary library.
See Łącki et al. (2021) <doi:10.1021/acs.jproteome.0c00962>.
opentimsr.author:
Michał Piotr Startek [aut, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-5227-3447>),
Mateusz Krzysztof Łącki [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-7415-4748>),
mandreyel [ctb, cph] (Author and copyright holder of the bundled 'mio'
library (https://github.com/mandreyel/mio))

openstudyval.title: Open Validator for FDA Study-Data Submissions
openstudyval.description:
Validates clinical and nonclinical study-data packages against
publicly described FDA technical-rejection criteria, SAS XPORT constraints
from the Study Data Technical Conformance Guide, and an extensible catalog
of SDTM, SEND, and ADaM structural conformance checks. Reads a study folder
of CSV, RDS, or (when the suggested package haven is installed) SAS v5/v8
transport files, optionally checks define.xml, and writes a submission-style
HTML and CSV validation report. This package is an independent open-source
implementation. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or a copy of
Pinnacle 21, Certara, or the FDA.
openstudyval.author: Shekhar Eranna Chalwadi [aut, cre]

p3d.title: Interactive 3D Visualization of p-Value Surfaces
p3d.description:
Provides interactive three-dimensional visualization of
p-value surfaces for single-sample t-tests. Enables simultaneous
exploration of effect size, sample size, and significance level,
making the continuous nature of p-values and the moderating effect
of sample size visually apparent. Includes both interactive ('rgl',
'plotly') and static (persp()) rendering options. The p-value
surface is based on the approach of Infanger and Schmidt-Trucksäss
(2019) <doi:10.1002/sim.8293>.
p3d.author: Ahmet Kutuk [aut, cre]

palettome.title:
Hierarchy-Aware, Interactively Editable Color Palettes for
Clusters
palettome.description:
Assigns perceptually-informed color palettes to clustered data
(e.g. scRNA-seq clusters / cell subtypes from 'Seurat' or plain UMAP
coordinate tables), where clusters that belong to the same "family"
(e.g. subtypes of T cells) can be colored either harmoniously (shared
hue, varying shade) or with maximal contrast (with family membership
encoded via a secondary channel). Families can be auto-detected from
embedding-space hierarchical clustering or supplied explicitly, and
every generated color remains individually overridable, with manual
overrides preserved across regeneration. Colors are constructed in the
HCL space as in Zeileis et al. (2020) <doi:10.18637/jss.v096.i01>,
separated using the CIEDE2000 color difference of Sharma, Wu and Dalal
(2005) <doi:10.1002/col.20070>, and checked for color-vision deficiency
using the simulation of Machado, Oliveira and Fernandes (2009)
<doi:10.1109/TVCG.2009.113>. Core algorithms have no UI dependencies;
an optional interactive 'shiny' UI is provided separately.
palettome.author:
Chenbin Huang [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-2179-2217>)

paretoinfer.title:
Sequential Identification of Approximately Pareto-Optimal
Alternatives under Noise
paretoinfer.description:
Sequential identification of epsilon-Pareto-optimal alternatives
among a finite set with noisy, possibly correlated objectives. Simultaneous
anytime-valid confidence sequences for every objective of every alternative
(Waudby-Smith and Ramdas, 2024, <doi:10.1093/jrsssb/qkad009>) certify, at
any time, which alternatives are epsilon-dominated and which are not, report
the estimated frontier, the plausible Pareto set and the certified-dominated
set, propose the next alternative to evaluate, and record an auditable
result contract.
paretoinfer.author:
André Leite [aut, cre] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-4718-9766>),
Raydonal Ospina [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-9884-9090>),
Cristiano Ferraz [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-6838-6734>)

pecme.title: Penalized ECME Estimation for Censored Linear Mixed Models
pecme.description:
Fits Gaussian linear mixed models with a random intercept
when the response is subject to left, right, and/or interval
censoring, using the Expectation/Conditional Maximization Either
(ECME) algorithm of Liu and Rubin (1994) in the spirit of the
fast censored-response mixed-model algorithm of Vaida and Liu
(2009). Simultaneous estimation and variable selection is
supported through coordinate-descent penalized maximization with
Lasso, Adaptive Lasso, SCAD, MCP, Elastic Net, and Ridge
penalties (no penalty is also supported). The random intercept is
integrated out by Gauss-Hermite quadrature at every iteration, and
the two ECME conditional-maximization steps respectively maximize
the expected penalized complete-data objective (for the
regression coefficients) and the actual observed-data marginal
likelihood (for the variance components), which is the defining
feature of ECME relative to plain ECM/EM. The package provides a
single-fit engine, a sequential/parallel penalty-parameter grid
search with information-criterion or cross-validated selection,
data-dependent or user-supplied lambda grids, and an
Expectation-Maximization based treatment of a completely missing
(at random) response, sharing the same truncated-normal machinery
used for censoring. References: Liu and Rubin (1994)
"The ECME algorithm: A simple extension of EM and ECM with
faster monotone convergence" <doi:10.1093/biomet/81.4.633>;
Vaida and Liu (2009) "Fast Implementation for Normal Mixed
Effects Models With Censored Response"
<doi:10.1198/jcgs.2009.07130>.
pecme.author:
Ali Asghar Haeri-Mehrizi [aut, cre],
Arshia Haeri-Mehrizi [aut],
Adel Mohammadpour [rev]

phylopred.title: Predicting Species Interactions from Phylogenetic Distance
phylopred.description:
Tools to model and predict host-parasite (and other pairwise
species) interactions from phylogenetic distance under presence-only
data. Provides pairwise host-sharing logistic models with
cluster-aware bootstrap and slope comparison between clades,
presence-only performance metrics (a threshold efficiency metric and
a phylogenetic partial receiver operating characteristic (ROC) adapted
from Peterson, Papes and Soberon (2008)
<doi:10.1016/j.ecolmodel.2007.11.008>), positive-unlabeled
host prediction, and leave-hosts-out validation. Methods build on
Robles-Fernandez and Lira-Noriega (2017) <doi:10.3389/fams.2017.00017>.
phylopred.author:
Angel Robles [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-4674-4270>)

pnotp.title: Client for the 'PnotP' Platform
pnotp.description:
Access the 'PnotP' platform <https://pnotp.ai> from R and
'RStudio'. One account API key drives data-compliant large language
model chat, where every response carries a retention receipt; model
training with pause, resume and cancel; model deployments and live
inference; and hosted agents. Includes 'RStudio' addins to chat with the
language model from the IDE, and a bridge to 'ellmer' for tool calling
and streaming.
pnotp.author:
Vicente Alonso Gallardo Montalva [aut, cre],
PnotP [cph, fnd]

posc.title: Probability of Outcome Superiority Curves
posc.description:
Computes, plots and compares probability of outcome superiority
curves (POSCs). For two people who differ by a given amount on a
continuous predictor, a POSC gives the probability that the person with
the higher predictor score also has the higher outcome, a probabilistic
and decision-oriented alternative to reporting a correlation coefficient.
Curves can be computed from a correlation under bivariate normality, from
a correlation matrix for an optimally weighted composite of predictors,
from a fitted linear model, or estimated directly from raw data with a
flexible spline model and bootstrap confidence bands.
posc.author: Matthew B. Jané [aut, cre]

powerup.title: Power Up Your PowerPoint Presentations
powerup.description:
Programmatically interact with new or existing 'Microsoft PowerPoint' documents,
by adding new slides, updating existing slides, and inserting displays into specific locations in slides.
Users can also add transition effects to slides, and add displays to specific
locations in slides by pointing to specific placeholders or creating new ones.
Preview the slides in a local viewer.
powerup.author:
Ellis Hughes [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0637-4436>),
Shannon Haughton [aut],
Romain François [aut],
GlaxoSmithKline Research & Development Limited [cph, fnd]

powerutilities.title: Power Analysis for Linear and Generalized Linear Mixed Models
powerutilities.description:
Prospective power analysis and design planning using
the "plug-in" approach described by Piepho et al. (2022)
<doi:10.1017/S0021859622000466> and Stroup, Ptukhina and Garai (2024)
<doi:10.1201/9780429092060-24>. Expected treatment means and the proposed
experimental design are encoded in an artificial data set, and a model is
"fit" to it with random effect variances, correlations and residual
dispersion fixed at user-specified values rather than being estimated.
The resulting standard errors are used to compute the power of F-tests and
user-defined contrasts, as well as Type S (sign) and Type M (magnitude)
error rates (Gelman and Carlin, 2014 <doi:10.1177/1745691614551642>).
Models are fit with 'glmmTMB', so the approach accommodates non-normal
responses, heteroscedasticity, nested and crossed random effects,
correlated random slopes, and structured covariances such as AR(1) and
spatial correlation. Helper functions convert standard deviations and
correlations into the internal parameterization of 'glmmTMB' and report the
order in which random effect parameters must be supplied. Denominator
degrees of freedom can be computed by the Kenward-Roger, residual or
asymptotic methods (or can be specified by users), and contrasts are
specified through 'emmeans'. Vignettes cover estimated marginal means,
contrast specification, and worked examples for common agricultural designs.
powerutilities.author: Simon Riley [aut, cre] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-4833-2026>)

prime.title: Proportional Inclusive Marginal Effects
prime.description:
Implements a model-free variable importance measure based on
proportional marginal effects estimated from noisy input-output data.
See Cho and Joseph (2026) <doi:10.48550/arXiv.2610.17053> for details.
prime.author:
Youngseo Cho [aut, cre, cph],
V. Roshan Joseph [aut, cph]

progme.title: Extended Progression Models for Repeated Measures
progme.description:
Extended progression models for repeated measures in progressive
disease clinical trials. Provides nonlinear mixed-effects progression
models (linear, plateau, Emax, exponential decay), delayed treatment
onset estimation by profile likelihood, joint longitudinal-survival
models for informative dropout, competing-risks extensions,
biomarker-informed adaptive dosing rules, and simulation-based power
and sample-size calculation. The progression-model view of treatment
effects, in which effects are characterised on the underlying disease
trajectory rather than as additive shifts on the outcome scale, follows
Raket (2022) <doi:10.1002/sim.9581>. The nonlinear mixed-effects
machinery is built on the 'nlme' implementation described by Pinheiro
and Bates (2000, ISBN 978-0-387-98957-0), and the joint modelling of
longitudinal and time-to-event data follows Rizopoulos (2012,
ISBN 978-1-4398-7286-4).
progme.author:
Mukul Bijalwan [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0001-3040-6912>),
Gunjan Aggrwal [aut],
Mukul Jain [aut]

proxymix.title:
Gaussian Mixture Proxies for Densities and Characteristic
Functions
proxymix.description:
Fits multivariate Gaussian-mixture proxies to target
distributions on real Euclidean space, given by a density, by samples,
or by a characteristic function. Four fitting regimes are unified under one verb:
(i) closed-form moment matching for a single component,
(ii) classical expectation-maximisation when independent samples are
available, (iii) importance-sampled expectation-maximisation that
minimises the Kullback-Leibler divergence when the target can be
evaluated point-wise but not (cheaply) sampled, and (iv) a least-squares
fit to the characteristic function when only that is known, with
numerical bounds on the Kolmogorov distance along one-dimensional
projections. Closed-form
Gaussian-mixture operators (density, sampling, marginalisation,
conditioning, divergence) round out the toolkit. The conditioning
operator drives multiple imputation of data missing at random,
covering the multimodal and heteroscedastic cases a single-Gaussian
model cannot represent. Implements the
regime hierarchy of van der Hoek and Elliott (2024)
<doi:10.1080/07362994.2024.2372605>.
proxymix.author:
Max Moldovan [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-9680-8474>),
John van der Hoek [aut]

psdea.title:
Data Envelopment Analysis with User-Defined and Learned
Reference Sets
psdea.description:
Slacks-based data envelopment analysis for panel data in which the
reference set is an explicit argument.  A user-supplied weight matrix, or a
matrix learned from the data by penalised non-negative reconstruction,
selects the units that may enter each decision-making unit's frontier.  The
package reports the unrestricted and the restricted score, the ratio of the
two and an exact decomposition of the shortfall into the part the restricted
technology can remove and the part it cannot.  Moran's I and local
indicators of spatial association are provided as diagnostics.  All linear
programs are solved by a two-phase simplex with Bland's rule implemented in
R, so the package needs no compiler.
psdea.author: Jiachao Peng [aut, cre]

psychds.title: Creating and Validating 'Psych-DS' Datasets
psychds.description: Provides a 'Shiny' application and helper functions for adopting 'Psych-DS' (<https://psych-ds.github.io/>), a community data standard for organizing and documenting datasets in the psychological and behavioral sciences inspired by the Brain Imaging Data Structure ('BIDS'). A guided interface walks researchers through the dataset creation process, organizing tabular data files into proper 'Psych-DS' directory structures, generating new, compliant, keyword-based filenames, and generating machine-readable 'JSON' metadata. Additional tools support building and editing data dictionaries with variable-level descriptions, validating datasets against the full 'Psych-DS' specification via a bundled 'JavaScript' validator, and exploring dataset contents interactively.
psychds.author:
Massachusetts Institute of Technology [cph],
Brian Leonard [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0005-7244-6882>),
Melissa Kline Struhl [aut] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-2217-9331>)

ptLasso.title: Pretraining the Lasso
ptLasso.description:
Implements lasso pretraining for generalized linear models for data with grouped observations; data without grouped observations, but with multinomial responses; data with multiple Gaussian responses; and data with repeated measurements over time.
The method fits a lasso model to an initial dataset and then uses its support and coefficient values to guide model fitting for a related task, which can improve performance by leveraging larger datasets and preserve interpretability by identifying features which are generally shared, and which are task specific.
See Craig et al. (2026) <doi:10.1093/jrsssb/qkaf050> for details.
Model fitting in this package is done with cv.glmnet() from the 'glmnet' package, and syntax closely follows that of 'glmnet' (Friedman, Hastie and Tibshirani (2010) <doi:10.18637/jss.v033.i01>).
ptLasso.author:
Erin Craig [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-4893-6671>),
Rob Tibshirani [aut, cph]

pubformat.title: Publication-Ready Formatting for Statistical Results
pubformat.description:
Provides tools for converting already-computed statistical results
into consistent, publication-ready character output. Supports p-values,
confidence intervals, correlation coefficients, percentages, test
statistics, and commonly reported effect sizes, with optional confidence
intervals and multiple output styles for selected statistical symbols.
The package emphasizes separation of statistical calculation,
interpretation, and publication formatting so that reporting choices do
not alter the underlying numeric results or inferential decisions.
pubformat.author: RJ Ballotti [aut, cre]

publishTC.title: Tools to Help to Publish the Trend-Cycle Component
publishTC.description:
Tools to facilitate the computation of the trend-cycle component of time series.
In particular, the computation can be performed using: the Cascade Linear Filter ('CLF', Dagum and Luati, 2008),
classical Henderson symmetric filters with surrogate Musgrave asymmetric filters, local parameterizations of
Musgrave filters (Quartier-la-Tente, 2024), and robust extensions taking into account
additive outliers and level shifts (Quartier-la-Tente, 2025). Computes confidence intervals
and provides specialized plotting functions for publication.
publishTC.author:
Alain Quartier-la-Tente [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-7890-3857>)

publicdataau.title: Australian Government Open Data from 'publicdata.au'
publicdataau.description:
Search, filter, total and download the Australian government open
data republished at <https://publicdata.au/>, where every version of a
dataset is kept at a URL that never changes. Rows and totals come from the
site's query API as typed, labelled 'tibble' data frames, and whole tables
from its files in any of twelve formats. Map layers come as 'sf' objects,
and rows that carry the code of an area join to the Australian Bureau of
Statistics boundaries in one call. The 'DuckDB' file of any version can be
attached over the web and queried in place with 'DBI' or 'dplyr'.
Downloads can be kept in a cache, since a version never changes, the
changes between versions are listed row by row, and the source file,
fetch time and checksum of every version are on record. Every answer
carries the version it came from and the attribution the publisher's
licence requires, and citations come as 'BibTeX'. Any dataset the site
serves works by its slug, so a new dataset needs no new release.
publicdataau.author:
Cameron Young [aut, cre],
National Digital [cph, fnd]

pyrt.title: Runtime Support for Converted 'Python' Packages
pyrt.description:
Provides the 'Python' runtime semantics required by 'R' packages
generated with 'pyport', including reference-semantics containers, class
and method-resolution-order dispatch, exception hierarchies, iteration and
slicing helpers, arbitrary-precision integer arithmetic, and bit-exact
random number generation.
pyrt.author: Yee How Lau [aut, cre, cph]

qdfauction.title:
Nonparametric Quantile Density Estimation and Structural
Analysis of First-Price Auctions
qdfauction.description:
Nonparametric estimators of the quantile density function
(the derivative of the quantile function): kernel, boundary-corrected
kernel, Poisson-weight and Bernstein-polynomial smoothers, indirect
estimators (Jones (1992)
<https://www.ism.ac.jp/editsec/aism/pdf/044_4_0721.pdf>; Soni, Dewan and
Jain (2012) <doi:10.1016/j.csda.2012.04.014>; Chaubey, Dewan and Li (2024)
<doi:10.1080/03610926.2023.2222922>), and linear, hard-thresholded and
block-thresholded wavelet estimators (Chesneau, Dewan and Doosti (2016)
<doi:10.1016/j.csda.2015.08.006>; Shirazi and Doosti (2022)
<doi:10.1080/03610918.2019.1656250>), with smoothing parameters chosen by
biased, robust likelihood (Wu (2019) <doi:10.1080/07350015.2018.1424633>)
or least-squares cross-validation. The estimators are applied to the
structural analysis of first-price sealed-bid auctions: recovery of
private values for independent or affiliated values and risk-neutral or
risk-averse bidders (Doosti, Dewan and Talebian (2025)
<doi:10.1016/j.econlet.2025.112670>; Doosti (2026)
<doi:10.1016/j.econlet.2026.112837>), estimation of the private-value
density with kernel benchmarks (Hickman and Hubbard (2015)
<doi:10.1002/jae.2385>; Marmer and Shneyerov (2012)
<doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2011.09.020>; Zincenko (2024)
<doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2024.105734>) and confidence bands (Ma, Marmer and
Shneyerov (2019) <doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2019.02.006>), and estimation of
the seller's expected revenue and optimal reserve price, with tools for
simulating equilibrium bids and comparing estimators.
qdfauction.author:
Hassan Doosti [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0290-8122>, affiliation: School of
Mathematical and Physical Sciences, Macquarie University),
Yogendra P. Chaubey [ctb, cph] (original R code of the quantile density
estimators and cross-validation criteria, revised and vectorised in
R/estimators.R and R/bandwidth.R),
Isha Dewan [ctb, cph] (original R code of the quantile density
estimators and cross-validation criteria, revised and vectorised in
R/estimators.R and R/bandwidth.R),
Jun Li [ctb, cph] (original R code of the quantile density estimators
and cross-validation criteria, revised and vectorised in
R/estimators.R and R/bandwidth.R),
Brent R. Hickman [ctb, cph] (original MATLAB implementation of the
boundary-corrected kernel density estimator, translated to R in
kde_hh()),
Timothy P. Hubbard [ctb, cph] (original MATLAB implementation of the
boundary-corrected kernel density estimator, translated to R in
kde_hh()),
Brani Vidakovic [ctb, cph] (original MATLAB routines Phijk, dwtr, Idwtr
and loc_lin, translated to R in scaling_function(), phi_jk(),
dwt_periodic(), idwt_periodic() and loclin_smooth()),
Vadim Marmer [ctb, cph] (original MATLAB implementation of the
quantile-based estimator, translated to R in
density_marmer_shneyerov(); reference implementation used to
validate fpa_density_ci()),
Jun Ma [ctb] (reference implementation of inference for the GPV
estimator, used to validate fpa_density_ci()),
Artyom Shneyerov [ctb, cph] (original MATLAB implementation of the
quantile-based estimator, translated to R in
density_marmer_shneyerov()),
Federico Zincenko [ctb, cph] (original implementation of the kernel
estimator of private values with boundary extrapolation, adapted in
fpa_values(method = 'zincenko'))

quadriceps.title:
Positive-Weight Cubature Rules for the Gaussian Weight and the
Cube
quadriceps.description:
Positive-weight cubature rules in several dimensions for the
Gaussian weight (ghpos) and the uniform weight on the cube (lepos): the
smallest rules known to the author for dimensions 2 to 5, with a fallback
to the cheapest tensor product of lower-dimensional rules elsewhere. The
rules are described in Pinkse (2026) <doi:10.48550/arXiv.2609.26840>,
<doi:10.5281/zenodo.22904159>. The R
twin of the 'Julia' package 'Quadriceps.jl'.

quicopt.title: Client for the 'Quicopt' Optimization Service
quicopt.description:
Author an optimization model — including a model under
uncertainty, with random variables, expectations, conditional value at
risk and chance constraints — in a native R interface, and solve it with
the 'Quicopt' service <https://quicopt.com>. Models are encoded to the
service's wire format and solved remotely; no solver is installed
locally. Random variables carry distributions or empirical scenario
columns taken directly from a data frame, so observed history becomes a
stochastic program in one call.
quicopt.author: Tim Bode [aut, cre, cph]

rMCHSPTT.title:
Modified Chain Sampling Inspection Plan for Time-Truncated Life
Tests
rMCHSPTT.author: Harsh Tripathi [aut, cre]

rMDSPTT.title:
Multiple Dependent State Sampling Inspection Plan for Time
Truncated Life Test
rMDSPTT.author: Harsh Tripathi [aut, cre]

rTARDIS.title: Terrains and Routes Directed in Spacetime
rTARDIS.description: Implements classes and methods for constructing and analysing graph representations of complex geographic spaces at local to global scales, particularly where accessible spaces are discontinuously distributed but retain connectivity (e.g., island systems where isolation is prevalent but not necessarily absolute), and where that distribution also changes through time (e.g., habitat patch fragmentation or plate tectonic drift).
