The package (originally named TARDIS) was first described and published in: Flannery-Sutherland, J., Elsler, A., Farnsworth, A., Lunt, D., Benton, M. (2025) <doi:10.1038/s41559-025-02739-y>.
rTARDIS.author:
Joe Flannery-Sutherland [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-8232-6773>)

rWind.title:
Download, Edit and Include Wind and Sea Currents Data in
Ecological and Evolutionary Analysis
rWind.description:
Downloads and processes surface wind data from the Global Forecast System
<https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/products/weather-climate-models/global-forecast>
and sea-current data from Ocean Surface Current Analyses Real-time (OSCAR).
Converts flow speed and direction into spatial rasters and directed
movement costs and conductances for connectivity and least-cost path analyses.
rWind.author:
Javier Fernández-López [aut, cre],
Klaus Schliep [aut],
Yurena Arjona [aut]

radiatR.title: Analyse and Visualise Headings and Trajectories on the Unit Disk
radiatR.description:
A complete pipeline for analysing directional data -- headings and
trajectories on the unit disk. Supply a table of angles directly, or
reconstruct headings from movement trajectories imported from tracking
tools ('EthoVision', 'DeepLabCut', 'SLEAP', 'TRex', 'ANY-maze',
'TrackMate', 'idtracker.ai', and others) via a unified dialect-based loader
system, including multi-bodypart pose estimation with likelihood-weighted
centroid. Derives per-trial heading directions using multiple rules
(ring-crossing, distal point, pose body-axis, velocity-based, and more).
Computes circular statistics including mean direction, resultant length,
von Mises and wrapped Cauchy parametric fits, circular correlation
(circular-linear and circular-circular), circular-linear regression
(Fisher and Lee (1992) <doi:10.2307/2532334>), model selection among
orientation models (Fitak and Johnsen (2017) <doi:10.1242/jeb.167056>),
and uniformity and multi-sample hypothesis tests (Rayleigh,
Watson-Williams, Hermans-Rasson (Landler, Ruxton and Malkemper (2019)
<doi:10.1186/s12898-019-0246-8>), and others) with multiple-comparison
correction. Path tortuosity follows Benhamou (2004)
<doi:10.1016/j.jtbi.2004.03.016>. Renders publication-quality 'ggplot2'
radial plots with overlaid rose diagrams, parametric density curves,
non-parametric kernel density estimates, and circular boxplots
(Buttarazzi, Pandolfo and Porzio (2018) <doi:10.1111/biom.12889>).
Includes a browser-based 'shiny' graphical interface requiring no R coding
via launch_app().
radiatR.author:
John D. Kirwan [aut, cre, cph],
A. & M.W. Mathis Labs [cph] (test fixture
tests/testthat/fixtures/real/dlc_CollectedData_Pranav.csv, from
'DeepLabCut'),
Talmo Pereira [cph] (example file inst/extdata/sleap_example.csv, from
'SLEAP'),
The Trustees of Princeton University [cph] (example file
inst/extdata/sleap_example.csv, from 'SLEAP')

rambur.title: Design and Analysis of Intertidal Chamber Experiments
rambur.description:
Facilitates the design and analysis of intertidal chamber
experiments as described in Pham & Sokolova (2026)
<doi:10.64898/2026.09.28.754745>. It supports generating experimental
profiles for 'ElectricBlue' intertidal chambers, reading log files,
and checking actual chamber conditions against designed profiles. It
also helps read log files from 'EnvLogger' robomussels (or temperature
loggers) and 'Pulse V2' heart rate loggers, and provides an algorithm
to extract heart rates from 'Pulse V2' records. The acronym stands for
Research Assistant in Marine Biology at the University of Rostock.
rambur.author:
Duy Nghia Pham [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-1349-1710>),
Inna M. Sokolova [ctb] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-2068-4302>)

rapidxlsx.title: Fast Parallel Excel Spreadsheet Writer
rapidxlsx.description: Serializes tabular data frames to Microsoft Excel 'OpenXML' ('xlsx') workbooks using a multi-threaded Rust core with parallel Deflate compression and zero-copy columnar memory mapping.
rapidxlsx.author: Amin Fathullah [aut, cre]

rapsimng.decide.cultivar.title:
Analyse APSIM Next Generation Simulation Outputs for Cultivar
Comparison
rapsimng.decide.cultivar.description: Provides functions to analyse Agricultural Production Systems sIMulator ('APSIM') Next Generation simulation outputs to support cultivar-level comparison under specified environments and management assumptions. The package focuses on transparent, reproducible summarisation of model outputs such as yield, phenology timing, and stress exposure, without performing 'APSIM' simulations, interpreting user intent, or making normative recommendations.
rapsimng.decide.cultivar.author: Bangyou Zheng [aut, cre]

rapsimng.decide.nitrogen.title:
Analyse APSIM Next Generation Simulation Outputs for Nitrogen
Decision
rapsimng.decide.nitrogen.description: Provides functions to analyse Agricultural Production Systems sIMulator ('APSIM') Next Generation simulation outputs to support nitrogen decision under specified environments and management assumptions. The package focuses on transparent, reproducible summarisation of model outputs such as nitrogen requirements, uptake, and efficiency, without performing 'APSIM' simulations, interpreting user intent, or making normative recommendations.
rapsimng.decide.nitrogen.author: Bangyou Zheng [aut, cre]

rapsimng.decide.sowing.title:
Analyse APSIM Next Generation Simulation Outputs for Sowing
Decision
rapsimng.decide.sowing.description: Provides functions to analyse Agricultural Production Systems sIMulator ('APSIM') Next Generation simulation outputs to support sowing decision under specified environments and management assumptions. The package focuses on transparent, reproducible summarisation of model outputs such as sowing window, establishment risk, and early crop development, without performing 'APSIM' simulations, interpreting user intent, or making normative recommendations.
rapsimng.decide.sowing.author: Bangyou Zheng [aut, cre]

rcosmo.title: Cosmic Microwave Background Data Analysis
rcosmo.description:
Tools for handling and analysing spherical data on a HEALPix grid,
with applications to cosmic microwave background maps. Supports reading FITS
files, converting between spherical and Cartesian coordinates and HEALPix
ordering schemes, selecting sky regions, sampling pixels, and visualising
maps. Implements empirical covariance, correlation and variogram estimation,
covariance model fitting, angular power spectrum estimation, and
distributional and entropy-based comparisons of spherical data. The package
and its methods are described by Fryer, Li and Olenko (2020)
<doi:10.32614/RJ-2020-012>.
rcosmo.author:
Daniel Fryer [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-6032-0522>),
Andriy Olenko [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0917-7000>),
Ming Li [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1218-2804>),
Yuguang Wang [aut]

rd2dnet.title: Boundary Discontinuity Designs on Networks
rd2dnet.description:
Estimation and inference for boundary discontinuity designs on
street networks. Extends the location-based framework of 'rd2d'
(Cattaneo, Titiunik and Yu, <doi:10.48550/arXiv.2505.07989>) from
Euclidean coordinates to network-native coordinates (signed network
distance to the boundary and offset along it) and user-defined network
metrics (edge costs, travel time, road-class transition penalties,
precomputed matrices). Provides side-specific local polynomial estimates
of boundary average treatment effect curves with robust bias-corrected
inference (Calonico, Cattaneo and Titiunik, 2014,
<doi:10.3982/ECTA11757>), uniform confidence bands, weighted and largest
aggregate effects, fuzzy designs, covariates, derivative targets,
heteroskedasticity-robust, cluster and network Conley (1999,
<doi:10.1016/S0304-4076(98)00084-0>) standard errors, a port of the
'rd2d' direct plug-in bandwidth selector, and a network-normalised
version of the local polynomial density test of Cattaneo, Jansson and
Ma (2020, <doi:10.1080/01621459.2019.1635480>).
rd2dnet.author:
Zach Winship [aut, cre, cph],
Matias D. Cattaneo [ctb, cph] (author of rd2d and rddensity, from which
the bandwidth selector and density test are ported),
Rocío Titiunik [ctb, cph] (author of rd2d, from which the bandwidth
selector is ported),
Ruiqi Rae Yu [ctb, cph] (author of rd2d, from which the bandwidth
selector is ported),
Michael Jansson [ctb, cph] (author of rddensity, from which the density
test is ported),
Xinwei Ma [ctb, cph] (author of rddensity, from which the density test
is ported)

reactives.title: Keyed Collections of 'shiny' Reactives
reactives.description:
Holds 'shiny' reactive values and reactive expressions under
keys that can be added, removed and reordered, with dependencies
tracked per key. The 'shiny' package offers reactiveValues() for keyed
stored values, but it can neither remove nor reorder keys, and it has
no keyed collection of computed values.
reactives.author: Nicolas Bennett [aut, cre, cph]

reconf.title:
Confidence Intervals for Random Effect Parameters in Linear
Mixed Models
reconf.description:
Computes score-based confidence intervals and hypothesis tests
for variance and covariance parameters of random effects in linear mixed
models fitted with 'lme4'. The intervals invert a profile score
statistic on the variance-covariance scale, with nuisance parameters
estimated on an extended parameter set. The intervals have near-nominal
coverage uniformly in the parameter, including near the boundary of the
parameter space, where Wald and likelihood ratio intervals can be
unreliable. The methods are described in Shedden
and Ekvall (2026) <doi:10.48550/arXiv.2610.04181>, building on Ekvall and
Bottai (2026) <doi:10.1093/biomet/asaf079>, Zhang, Ekvall, and Molstad
(2025) <doi:10.1093/biomet/asaf010>, and Ekvall and Bottai (2022)
<doi:10.1214/22-AOS2177>.
reconf.author:
Karl Oskar Ekvall [aut, cre, cph],
Yiqiao Zhang [ctb],
Matias Shedden [ctb]

recruitlag.title:
Can Episodic Recruitment be a Delayed Consequence of Continuous
Reproduction?
recruitlag.description:
Tests whether an episodic recruitment record can be the delayed
consequence of a reproductive record, under any distributed lag. A delay
is a convolution, and a convolution is a weighted average, so the
concentration in time of expected recruitment can never exceed that of
reproduction: reproduction's own concentration is a ceiling. The package
computes that ceiling by searching families of lag weights (pure delays,
windows, geometric decay and Dirichlet draws), calibrates the pooled
comparison against negative-binomial counts to show what it can and
cannot refute, and runs the host-level (replicate-unit) test in which the
null is the lag hypothesis exactly as it is asserted: expected
recruitment on each unit is that unit's own lagged reproduction, scaled to
its own total. Uncertainty on the exceedance comes by three routes, a
cluster bootstrap over units, a Bayesian bootstrap (Rubin 1981
<doi:10.1214/aos/1176345338>) and a negative-binomial model of the counts
fitted with 'Stan' through 'cmdstanr'; recruit_triage() asks whether a
first sighting is a recruit or a plant returning from dormancy. Plotting
functions draw the ceiling strip, the lag profiles against the observed
counts, the calibration and a forest plot of the intervals. The census
data on the epiphytic orchid Lepanthes eltoroensis analysed in the
companion paper are included.
recruitlag.author:
Raymond L. Tremblay [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-8588-4372>)

regsensitivity.title: Regression Sensitivity Analysis for Omitted Variable Bias
regsensitivity.description:
Sensitivity analysis for linear regression coefficients in the
presence of omitted variables. Implements the identified-set and
breakdown-point analyses of Diegert, Masten and Poirier (2026)
<doi:10.48550/arXiv.2206.02303>, Oster (2019)
<doi:10.1080/07350015.2016.1227711> and Masten and Poirier (2026)
<doi:10.1257/aer.20230242>. Provides bounds on regression
coefficients under relaxations of the no-omitted-variables
assumption indexed by interpretable sensitivity parameters, the
breakdown point of a hypothesis about the long-regression
coefficient, and plotting helpers.
regsensitivity.author:
Mike Nguyen [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-3432-8595>)

relm.title: Local Large Language Models as Base-R Objects
relm.description:
Load and run local large language models (through a vendored,
patched 'llama.cpp') from R and work with them as plain data frames and
matrices in base-R idiom. Provides model loading and tokenization (llm(),
llm_tokens()), text generation (llm_generate()), next-token distributions
(llm_logits()), embeddings (llm_embed()), and mechanistic
interpretability tools -- activation tracing (llm_trace()), activation
steering (llm_steer()), neuron ablation (llm_ablate()), and grouped statistical
probes (llm_probe()). Vision-language
models loaded with their projector take image input in generation and
embeddings. A checksum-verified downloader (llm_download()) fetches pinned
models.
relm.author:
Alessandro Vadala [aut, cre, cph],
ggml authors [ctb, cph] (Bundled llama.cpp and ggml (MIT)),
Authors of the bundled Rust and native dependencies [ctb, cph]
(Individual authors, copyrights and licenses are listed in AUTHORS,
RUST-NOTICES and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES)

retestR.title: Model-Based Anomaly Detection for Repeat Test-Takers
retestR.description:
Flags repeat test-takers whose second-attempt performance departs
from what a growth model predicts, using independent evidence sources:
model-expected score gain (accounting for regression to the mean, time
between attempts and remediation), differential performance on exposed
versus new items (Sinharay, 2017, <doi:10.3102/1076998616673872>), and
differential response speed under a lognormal response-time model (van
der Linden, 2006, <doi:10.3102/10769986031002181>). Evidence is combined
into a risk index calibrated by parametric bootstrap under the
no-misconduct model, so flagging thresholds carry explicit false-positive
rates.
retestR.author:
Daniel Edi [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-5475-819X>)

retroglyph.title:
A Trusted Mini-Agent to Reconstruct Individual Patient Data from
Kaplan-Meier Images
retroglyph.description:
The enclosed agent reconstructs individual patient data from
published Kaplan-Meier curve images.
Relative to other Kaplan-Meier reconstruction tools,
it excels at untangling egregiously occluded Kaplan-Meier curves,
and the digitization phase achieves a high level of pixel precision.
retroglyph.author:
William Michael Landau [aut, cre],
Eli Lilly and Company [cph, fnd]

rgrind.title: Gamified Algorithmic and Data Wrangling Challenges for R
rgrind.description:
An in-console, gamified learning and practice engine for R.
Solve algorithmic and data-wrangling challenges directly in the R
console, get instant styled feedback with worked explanations, and
track your progress locally with a solving streak, attempt history,
and an activity heatmap.
rgrind.author: Uwakmfon Paul [aut, cre]

rjd3bridge.title: Bridge Between 'RJDemetra' (V2) and 'rjd3' (V3)
rjd3bridge.description:
Provides bidirectional tools to convert seasonal adjustment
models and specifications between 'RJDemetra' ('JDemetra+' v2)
and the 'rjd3' ecosystem ('JDemetra+' v3, packages 'rjd3x13' and 'rjd3tramoseats').
Facilitates workflow migration and backward compatibility analysis.
rjd3bridge.author:
Alain Quartier-la-Tente [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-7890-3857>)

rjd3filters.title: Trend-Cycle Extraction with Linear Filters with 'JDemetra+ 3.x'
rjd3filters.description:
Build and apply symmetric and asymmetric moving
averages (= linear filters) for trend-cycle extraction.
In particular, it implements several modern approaches for real-time estimates
from the viewpoint of revisions and time delay in detecting turning points.
It includes the local polynomial approach of Proietti and Luati (2008), the
Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space (RKHS) of Dagum and Bianconcini (2008) and
the Fidelity-Smoothness-Timeliness approach of Grun-Rehomme, Guggemos, and
Ladiray (2018).
It is based on 'Java' libraries developed in 'JDemetra+'
(<https://github.com/jdemetra>), time series analysis software.
rjd3filters.author:
Alain Quartier-la-Tente [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-7890-3857>),
Jean Palate [aut],
Tanguy Barthelemy [ctb],
Anna Smyk [ctb]

rjd3highfreq.title: Seasonal Adjustment of High Frequency Data with 'JDemetra+ 3.x'
rjd3highfreq.description: R interface to 'JDemetra+ 3.x' (<https://github.com/jdemetra>), the time series analysis software. It provides functions for seasonal adjustment of higher-frequency data, including those with multiple or non-integer periodicities. It includes pre-adjustment via the extended airline model and several seasonal decomposition methods: extended airline model based decomposition, extended X-11, and augmented STL.
rjd3highfreq.author:
Jean Palate [aut],
Daniel Ollech [cre, ctb],
Christiane Hofer [ctb],
Witthohn Thomas [ctb],
Lea Hengen [ctb],
Martin Stefan [ctb],
Alessandro Piovani [ctb],
Tanguy Barthelemy [ctb, art],
Karsten Webel [ctb] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0001-5538-5428>,
method: X-11 method)

rjsf.title: R Interface to Jump-Switch-Flow Simulation
rjsf.description:
An R interface to Jump-Switch-Flow (JSF), a hybrid
simulation framework for compartmental reaction models that combines
stochastic jump dynamics at low population sizes with deterministic flow
dynamics at high population sizes. Simulations are performed using the
'jsf' backend for 'Python' through 'reticulate', with structured R outputs
for inspection, summary, and plotting. The underlying methodology is
described in Germano et al. (2026)
<doi:10.1007/s00285-026-02409-y>.
rjsf.author:
Thanh Long Vu [aut, cre, cph],
Domenic Germano [aut],
Michael Lydeamore [aut]

rladybugdb.title: R Interface to the 'LadybugDB' Embedded Graph Database
rladybugdb.description:
Provides an R interface to 'LadybugDB', an embedded columnar graph
database using the 'Cypher' query language. 'LadybugDB' was formerly known
as 'Kuzu'. This package uses native 'Rcpp' bindings to
the 'LadybugDB' C library, requiring no 'Python' runtime.
rladybugdb.author: Raden Muhammad Hadi [aut, cre]

robotstxtr.title: Engine-Aware 'robots.txt' Policy with Google's Matcher Algorithm
robotstxtr.description:
Evaluates whether URLs may be crawled according to 'robots.txt'
rules. A versioned engine-aware facade keeps neutral fetch evidence,
per-engine status policy, robots product tokens, and matcher capabilities
separate, returning explicit non-decisions when policy is undocumented or
a matcher is unavailable. The available matcher is a bundled,
upstream-test-validated snapshot of Google's open-source C++ 'robots.txt'
matcher, preserving 'Googlebot' behavior. Fetches use a deterministic,
conservative policy built on 'httr2', with fetch origins constructed by
'rurl'. All network access in tests, examples, and vignettes is mocked or
served locally, so no internet connection is required to install, test, or
check the package. This matcher derives from Google's 'robotstxt'
project
<https://github.com/google/robotstxt>, distributed under the Apache License
2.0; see the package NOTICE.
robotstxtr.author:
Bart Turczynski [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-8788-7980>),
Google LLC [cph] (Bundled 'robots.txt' matcher: src/robots.cc,
src/robots.h, src/reporting_robots.cc, src/reporting_robots.h)

rpspanel.title:
US State Energy-Economy Panels with Renewable Portfolio
Standards
rpspanel.description:
Builds a documented, reproducible state-by-year panel for the 50
US states and the District of Columbia that combines energy consumption,
prices and production from the US Energy Information Administration (EIA)
State Energy Data System, electricity generation and retail sales, state
energy-related carbon dioxide emissions, and state GDP, income and
population from the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). Data are downloaded
on demand through the official APIs and cached locally, with the source,
vintage and transformation of every variable recorded in a codebook.
Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) rules are turned into standardised
annual stringency indices (adoption, nominal, coverage-adjusted and
incremental requirements, following Yin and Powers (2010)
<doi:10.1016/j.enpol.2009.10.067>, plus design-flexibility indicators).
Output works directly with the 'plm', 'fixest' and 'csdm' packages.
rpspanel.author: Moses Adebayo [aut, cre, cph]

rsDCM.title: Robust and Sparse Dynamic Causal Modelling for Functional MRI
rsDCM.description:
Provides a robust and sparse method for group-level Dynamic
Causal Modelling (DCM) of functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI)
data: Student-t weighting of subjects for robustness, combined with a
nonlocal product-moment (pMOM) spike-and-slab prior for sparse
selection of group-level effects (<doi:10.48550/arXiv.2609.06379>). The package also
provides an R implementation of single-subject DCM for fMRI using
variational Laplace inversion (Friston et al., 2003
<doi:10.1016/S1053-8119(03)00202-7>), including the bilinear neural
state equation and the Buxton-Friston hemodynamic response model,
ported from the 'SPM25' (version 25.01.02) toolbox for 'MATLAB'.
rsDCM.author:
Godfred Arhin [aut, cre, trl],
Nilotpal Sanyal [aut],
SPM25 Authors [ctb, cph] (Original MATLAB SPM25 (v25.01.02)
implementation; see LICENSE.note)

rtemis.draw.title: Schema-Driven Interactive Charts, Network Graphs, and Maps
rtemis.draw.description:
Create interactive statistical charts, network graphs and
choropleth maps. Charts are rendered with the 'ECharts' 'JavaScript'
library, networks with 'Sigma.js' and maps with 'MapLibre GL JS'.
A high-level interface of plotting functions builds a complete
visualization from data in a single call, while a low-level interface
gives full control over every option. Both are based on the same
type-checked and validated 'S7' configuration objects. Configurations
can be saved to and restored from 'JSON' files, and each chart type has
a published 'JSON Schema' that other interfaces can implement.
Visualizations display as 'htmlwidgets' that automatically adapt to
light and dark themes, work in 'R Markdown', 'Quarto' and 'shiny', and
can be exported to Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) files using
'Node.js'.
rtemis.draw.author:
E.D. Gennatas [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-9280-3609>)

rtprep.title: Screening, Trimming, and Aggregating Response Time Data
rtprep.description:
A uniform interface to common response time preprocessing decisions
that precede analysing aggregated response times or fitting an evidence
accumulation model. Screening rules from different preprocessing routines
-- absolute cutoffs, standard deviation and median absolute deviation
criteria, recursive moving criteria, and model-based mixture flagging --
all return the same per-trial object, so that consequences of a
preprocessing choice can be compared rather than assumed. The package also
provides aggregation into EZ-diffusion summary statistics, diagnostics
reporting what each rule removed and where rules disagree. Finally,
generators for response time data with contaminants of known type are
provided, so that a chosen pipeline can be tested against ground truth.
Screening criteria follow Van Selst and Jolicoeur (1994)
<doi:10.1080/14640749408401131>, the
contaminant mixture Ratcliff and Tuerlinckx (2002)
<doi:10.3758/BF03196302>, and the EZ-diffusion equations Wagenmakers,
van der Maas and Grasman (2007) <doi:10.3758/BF03194023>.
rtprep.author:
Gidon T. Frischkorn [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-5055-9764>)

rumenGP.title: Rumen Gas Production Modeling, Comparison, and Visualization
rumenGP.description:
Provides tools for importing, processing,
visualizing, fitting, comparing, and interpreting
in vitro rumen gas production data. Supports ANKOM RF
workflows, generic gas production datasets, and
pressure-based measurements. Includes multiple kinetic
models, custom nonlinear models, model comparison
workflows, treatment-level ranking, diagnostic tools,
and visualization functions for rumen fermentation
studies.
rumenGP.author:
Arlan Araujo Rodrigues [aut, cre],
Hilario Cuquetto Mantovani [aut]

sage.title: Retrieve Slices of the Small-Area Global Elections Archive
sage.description:
Downloads and subsets slices of the Small-Area Global Elections
(SAGE) archive, a harmonized collection of polling-station and
precinct-level election results, without having to read monolithic
country-level files. Reads partitioned 'Parquet' from a public bucket
(configurable through the 'SAGE_SOURCE' environment variable, the
'sage_set_source()' function, or a local copy of the archive) and exposes
a 'sage_load(country, years, columns)' function returning a 'tibble', plus
helpers for the accompanying boundary polygons and candidate-level vote
sidecars. See <https://github.com/noahdasanaike/sage> for the archive
itself.
sage.author:
Noah Dasanaike [aut, cre, cph],
Dmitry Shkolnik [ctb]

sampleone.title: Survey Sampling Methods for Teaching and Practice
sampleone.description:
Planning, selection, and estimation for surveys under the main
probability sampling designs taught in introductory sampling courses:
simple random sampling with and without replacement, stratified
sampling (proportional, Neyman, and cost-based allocation), systematic
sampling, one- and two-stage cluster sampling,
and ratio and regression estimators. Functions accept a superset of the
inputs a given formula requires and silently ignore arguments that are
not needed for the selected computation. Each function returns a
structured object with the point estimate, the associated variance and
confidence interval, a step-by-step breakdown of the calculation, and a
short pedagogical note suggesting related methods to explore, making the
package suitable both for applied survey work and for classroom use.
Methods follow Cochran (1977, ISBN:0-471-16240-X) and
Bolfarine & Bussab (2005, ISBN:8521203675), among others referenced in
each function's documentation.
sampleone.author:
Miguel Luiz de Almeida Pinto [aut, cre],
Mariano Martinez Espinosa [aut] (Author of the source course material
(course notes) this package implements)

sandwichrand.title: Sandwich Mixed Randomization for Allocation Sequence Generation
sandwichrand.description:
Generates allocation sequences for randomized controlled trials
using the sandwich mixed randomization (SMR) scheme, together with
verification, diagnostics, and release utilities.
sandwichrand.author:
Bingshun Wang [aut, cre] (Designer of the sandwich mixed randomization
scheme),
Jinliang Xie [ctb],
Wei Wang [ctb]

saydo.title: Link What People Say to What They Do with LLM-Coded Themes
saydo.description:
Measures the say-do gap in mixed-methods data: whether themes
in what people say go with differences in what they do. Codes free text
against a codebook with large language models through 'ellmer', or any
coder function, and validates the codes against a human-coded sample
with Cohen's kappa, precision and recall. Links the codes to
participants' behavioural or outcome data, aggregating segment-level
transcripts to participants where needed, and tests each theme against
each metric with Welch's t-test and multiple-comparison adjustment.
Developed by Neudata Consulting Ltd.
saydo.author:
Bernard Isekah Osangir [aut, cre],
Neudata Consulting Ltd [cph, fnd]

sbert.title: Topic Modeling with 'Sentence-BERT' Embeddings
sbert.description:
Builds semantic topic models from 'Sentence-BERT'
embeddings (Reimers and Gurevych, 2019) <doi:10.18653/v1/D19-1410>.
Sentence embeddings are computed in several modes with models run on
the Open Neural Network Exchange ('ONNX') Runtime, including
multilingual and long-context encoders and a fast static model.
Topics are labeled with class-based term weighting that can be
retuned without refitting. Candidate topic counts and document
granularities (whole documents, sentences, clauses, or phrases) can
be compared side by side, and fitted models assign topics to new
documents, give soft memberships and per-document topic mixtures.
The package offers coherence and diversity metrics and
visualizations.
sbert.author:
Mohammed Saqr [aut, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-5881-3109>),
Sonsoles López-Pernas [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-9621-1392>)

sbwadjust.title: Stable Balancing Weights for Covariate Adjustment in Trials
sbwadjust.description:
Covariate adjustment for randomized trials using stable
balancing weights (SBW), as proposed by Irish, Zubizarreta, and Luedtke
(2026) <doi:10.48550/arXiv.2609.01638>. sbw_weights() fits
exact-balance SBW for a two-arm study by a closed-form solve with a
nonnegative quadratic-programming fallback; sbw_estimate() computes a
closed menu of treatment-effect estimands (average treatment effect,
relative risk, survival ratio, Mann-Whitney, quantile contrasts) from
the fitted weights, with bootstrap confidence intervals.
sbwadjust.author: Kayla Irish [aut, cre]

scNPM.title: Single-Cell Network Propensity Matching
scNPM.description:
Estimates and compares heterogeneous gene conditional-dependence
networks from single-cell expression data. A latent Gaussian mixture and
probit observation mechanism represent cellular heterogeneity and zero
observations. Protein interaction information supplies edge-specific prior
weights, while network propensity matching links cell clusters across
conditions and guides adaptation. Staged inference fixes correspondence after adaptation,
disables adaptation feedback, and jointly models matched network edges with
a four-state spike-and-slab prior for posterior group and directional
differential edge selection. Functions assess balance,
record criterion diagnostics, and visualize within-condition and
differential networks.
scNPM.author: Tao Liu [aut, cre]

scorecraft.title: Scorecard Development and Internal Ratings-Based Risk Parameters
scorecraft.description:
Builds points scorecards for binary targets (credit risk, fraud,
propensity) on the optimal binning and weight of evidence engine of
'OptimalBinningWoE', and takes them to the risk parameters of the internal
ratings-based (IRB) approach. Variables are selected through optimal
binning, eight admission rules, hold-out revalidation with frozen bins and
a consensus of 'glmnet', 'xgboost', 'lightgbm' and 'ranger' models weighted
by out-of-sample performance; the audit funnel never drops a candidate
from the report. The scorecard is fitted with an explicit, auditable scale
alignment (a log-odds regression on the raw score composed with the
points-to-double-the-odds map); cut-offs are swept with frozen cuts;
reject inference is reported as a sensitivity band; the population and
characteristic stability indices (PSI and CSI) are monitored with both the
fixed and the sample-size-adjusted threshold; and production SQL is
generated in fourteen dialects, with the agreement between R and SQL
verified by test. The IRB layer builds the default flag; calibrates the
scorecard to a long-run default rate with rating grades, margins of
conservatism and floors to give the probability of default (PD); models
workout loss given default (LGD) in two stages with downturn and
in-default estimates; models credit conversion factors from facility
snapshots to give the exposure at default (EAD); and computes expected
loss, risk weights, regulatory capital and expected credit loss from
parameter tables selected by framework preset. The heavy numeric kernels
(rank correlation of wide weight of evidence tables, exact concordance
counts for Somers' D, streamed expected credit loss paths) are compiled
with 'RcppArmadillo'. The scorecard methodology follows Siddiqi (2017)
<doi:10.1002/9781119282396> and Thomas et al. (2017)
<doi:10.1137/1.9781611974560>.
scorecraft.author: Jose Evandeilton Lopes [aut, cre, cph]

sds.title: Spatial Data Sources
sds.description:
Descriptions of spatial data sources that can be read
directly with or without download. Most sources are readable by 'GDAL' software.
There are functions for imagery, elevation, and a variety of easily accessible
data streams including image tile servers, links to online files, and geographic
data services.
sds.author: Michael Sumner [aut, cre, cph]

selSurv.title: Inference after Cox-Lasso Variable Selection
selSurv.description:
Methods for inference after Cox-Lasso variable selection in
right-censored survival data. The package provides Cox-Lasso fitting,
support-restricted Cox refitting, sample splitting, approximately debiased
coefficient estimates, score-level bootstrap intervals, and model-based
bootstrap intervals with fixed-support or repeated-selection procedures.
The methods differ in their inferential targets and theoretical guarantees.
Relevant methodological investigations are presented in Schemet and
Friedrich-Welz (2026) <doi:10.1186/s12874-026-02887-0>, Schemet, Groll and
Friedrich-Welz (2026) <doi:10.48550/arXiv.2608.18893>, and Schemet and
Friedrich-Welz (2026) <doi:10.48550/arXiv.2608.24230>.
selSurv.author:
Lena Schemet [aut, cre],
Sarah Friedrich-Welz [aut],
Andreas Groll [aut]

seowebchecker.title:
Comprehensive Website Search Engine Optimization Audit and
Analysis Tools
seowebchecker.description:
Provides a lightweight client software development kit and utility
suite for automated website technical search engine optimization audits,
meta tag validations, Core Web Vitals checks, and optimization scoring.
Official web audit portal and tools available at
<https://seowebchecker.com/>.
seowebchecker.author:
Rahul Gupta [aut, cre],
SEOWebChecker [cph]

seqbench.title: Anytime-Valid Sequential Benchmarking of Algorithms
seqbench.description:
Sequential, anytime-valid comparison of algorithms on paired
losses with a practical-equivalence margin. Confidence sequences for
the mean paired difference, superiority/equivalence/continue
decisions, cost accounting and auditable trajectories.
seqbench.author:
André Leite [aut, cre],
Raydonal Ospina [aut],
Cristiano Ferraz [aut]

shaman.title: Sampling Hi-C Contact Matrices for Aparametric Normalization
shaman.description:
Generate expected Hi-C (genome-wide chromosome conformation
capture) data maintaining marginal coverage, and the decay in contact probability
with increasing genomic distance. Expected Hi-C data is used for normalization
and graphical presentation of statistical significance of observed Hi-C contact
enrichments. The method is described in Mendelson Cohen et al. (2017)
<doi:10.1101/187203>.
shaman.author:
Amos Tanay [aut],
Netta Mendelson Cohen [aut],
Aviezer Lifshitz [aut, cre],
Weizmann Institute of Science [cph]

shinyHierarchy.title: Hierarchical Input Component for Shiny
shinyHierarchy.description:
Hierarchical slicer-style input for Shiny applications with
multi-selection, tri-state checkboxes, search, cascading selection,
and a structured selection value for analytics workflows.
shinyHierarchy.author: Luis Rodriguez [aut, cre]

silentema.title: Dynamic Missingness Graphs and Sensitivity Analysis for EMA Data
silentema.description:
Tools for diagnosing and correcting informative nonresponse in
ecological momentary assessment (EMA) and other experience-sampling designs. Declares the assumed nonresponse
mechanism as a dynamic missingness graph built from a taxonomy of seven
motifs, following the graphical missing-data framework of Mohan and Pearl
(2021) <doi:10.1080/01621459.2021.1874961>; checks by d-separation which
within-person and between-person estimands of a two-level vector
autoregressive model remain recoverable and by which estimator; tests
whether skipped prompts were informative (the silence test and the
sensor-gap test, with cluster-robust inference after Cameron and Miller
(2015) <doi:10.3368/jhr.50.2.317>); estimates the temporal and
contemporaneous networks from answered adjacent prompts with the half-panel
jackknife of Dhaene and Jochmans (2015) <doi:10.1093/restud/rdv007>, by
inverse-probability weighting on an observed context, and by
full-information maximum likelihood with the state-space
expectation-maximization (EM) algorithm of Shumway and Stoffer (1982)
<doi:10.1111/j.1467-9892.1982.tb00349.x>;
profiles the estimates over a self-censoring sensitivity parameter
(inverse-probability weighting with a fixed probit selection model whose
intercept is calibrated to the response rate); calibrates that parameter
from passive sensors, randomized probes, or the post-skip contrast;
computes worst-case bounds for person means in the spirit of Manski (2003)
<doi:10.1007/b97478>; writes a preregistration-ready missingness
declaration; and simulates experience-sampling data under every motif.
The methods are described in Yu (2026, manuscript under review); the
accompanying materials are archived at <https://osf.io/x6d2t/>.
silentema.author:
Hsiu-Ting Yu [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-3668-8033>)

simulab.title: Simulates a Wide Variety of Data Shapes, Sizes and Distributions
simulab.description:
Generates a wide variety of data, in different shapes, sample
sizes, distributions and parameters. The parameters are either drawn at
random or set in advance, and in both cases they are stored with the
data, so they are known and their recovery can be tested. Generators cover
declared variables with treatment assignment and missing values,
correlated and clustered data, latent profile, latent class, factor and
item response models, longitudinal and multilevel processes, survival
times with competing risks, sequences of states, and static, bipartite,
multiplex, temporal and transition networks. Every generator returns
batches of reproducible data sets for the evaluation of statistical
methods, the testing of models and software, and teaching; simulated
transition networks are native 'tna' models.
simulab.author:
Mohammed Saqr [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-5881-3109>),
Sonsoles López-Pernas [aut, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-9621-1392>)

smak.title: Scalable Model Averageing Kit
smak.description:
Supports frequentist model averaging on linear
regression problems via the scalable method of
Zhu et. al. (2022) <doi:10.1080/07350015.2022.2116442>.
The scalable model averaging technique projects to
singular vectors, performs one linear regression per singular
vector, then combines the estimates to optimize either
Mallows' criterion, or the jackknife estimate of error.
smak.author:
Steven E. Pav [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-4197-6195>)

soilcnn.title: Convolutional Neural Networks for Digital Soil Mapping
soilcnn.description:
A framework, built on 'torch', for mapping a soil property from
point observations and a stack of aligned rasters with a convolutional
network that reads the neighbourhood of each point. It extracts the
patches; resamples by spatial blocks or by k-fold nearest neighbour distance
matching, after Linnenbrink et al. (2024) <doi:10.5194/gmd-17-5897-2024>;
tunes and selects under a noise floor and the one-standard-error rule;
refits the selected configuration under several seeds; and predicts
median, mean and interval maps over rasters of any extent. The map's
centre is the ensemble median over seeds; the mean corrects its
back-transformation by smearing, after Duan (1983)
<doi:10.1080/01621459.1983.10478017>. The intervals are conformal,
calibrated three ways and each checked on the test set: on the
cross-validated residuals; on a calibration set held out of every fold,
as split conformal, after Lei et al. (2018)
<doi:10.1080/01621459.2017.1307116>; or with every fold's model at each
pixel, as CV+, after Barber et al. (2021) <doi:10.1214/20-AOS1965> -- with
points, or whole groups of them, weighing alike, after Dunn et al. (2023)
<doi:10.1080/01621459.2022.2060112>. The area of applicability of Meyer
and Pebesma (2021) <doi:10.1111/2041-210X.13650> is mapped beside them. What a model learned is read by permutation, by SHAP values from
expected gradients, after Erion et al. (2021)
<doi:10.1038/s42256-021-00343-w>, by SAGE, after Covert et al. (2020)
<doi:10.48550/arXiv.2004.00668>, by accumulated local effects, after Apley
and Zhu (2020) <doi:10.1111/rssb.12377>, and by refits without each
variable. Random forest and multilayer perceptron baselines run under the
same folds.
soilcnn.author:
Cássio Marques Moquedace [aut, cre, cph],
Clara Glória Oliveira Baldi [aut, cph]

soilwatR.title: Simulation of Soil Water Flow Based on Darcy's Law
soilwatR.description:
Provides a simple model to simulate soil water content and water
flux changes at multiple soil depths. Calculations mainly follow
Allen et al. (1998, ISBN:92-5-104219-5) and Teh (2017, ISBN:9789673447626).
soilwatR.author: Minguo Liu [aut, cre]

solvency2.title: Offline Solvency II Calculations and Regulatory Parameters
solvency2.description:
Native, offline components for insurance solvency calculations
under Solvency II, including valuation, technical provisions, market and
underwriting risks, capital aggregation, own funds, groups and archived
reporting checks. Provides explicit dated rule profiles, regulatory
parameters, correlation matrices, synthetic reference cases, local discount
curve adapters and traceable analyst overrides. Implements components of
Directive 2009/138/EC, European Parliament and Council (2009)
<https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2009/138/oj>, and Delegated Regulation
(EU) 2015/35, European Commission (2014)
<https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg_del/2015/35/oj>.
Users provide portfolio inputs, market observations and model results;
no network connection or 'Python' runtime is required.
solvency2.author:
Dimitrios Geromichalos [cre],
RiskDataScience GmbH [aut, cph]

spatialcvR.title: Spatial Cross-Validation for Machine Learning
spatialcvR.description: Spatial cross-validation and model evaluation for geospatial machine learning applications. Addresses spatial dependence in observations by implementing spatial block, buffered, and clustering cross-validation methods. Includes spatial leakage detection, model performance metrics, and spatial residual diagnostics for assessing model generalization across geographic space. Methods based on Brenning (2012) <doi:10.1016/j.cageo.2012.02.001>, Pohjankukka et al. (2017) <doi:10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2017.07.001>, and Roberts et al. (2017) <doi:10.1111/ecog.02881>.
spatialcvR.author: Mamadou SOW [aut, cre]

specProc.title: Preprocessing Tools for Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy
specProc.description:
Tools for exploring, preprocessing and modeling spectroscopic
data, developed for laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) and also
applicable to other techniques such as Raman, infrared, and inductively
coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy. Covers the workflow from
raw spectra to calibrated results: peak finding and fitting, wavelength
calibration, baseline correction, normalization and scaling, orthogonal
signal correction including orthogonal partial least squares (OPLS;
Trygg and Wold (2002) <doi:10.1002/cem.695>), calibration transfer,
calibration curves and figures of merit, and plasma diagnostics
(Boltzmann and Saha-Boltzmann plots, Stark broadening). Includes robust
tools for outlier detection and exploration: robust principal component
analysis (Hubert, Rousseeuw and Vanden Branden (2005)
<doi:10.1198/004017004000000563>), detection of deviating cells
(Rousseeuw and Van den Bossche (2018)
<doi:10.1080/00401706.2017.1340909>), PCA with cellwise outliers and
missing values (MacroPCA; Hubert, Rousseeuw and Van den Bossche (2019)
<doi:10.1080/00401706.2018.1562989>), robust transformations to central
normality (Raymaekers and Rousseeuw (2021)
<doi:10.1007/s10994-021-05960-5>), and self-organizing maps (Kohonen
(1982) <doi:10.1007/BF00337288>). Preprocessing steps are also available
as 'recipes' steps for 'tidymodels' workflows. Computationally intensive
steps are implemented in 'C++' via 'Rcpp' and 'RcppEigen'.
specProc.author:
Christian L. Goueguel [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0521-3446>)

spectra2rgb.title:
Convert Spectral Signatures to sRGB and CIELAB Colour
Coordinates
spectra2rgb.description:
Converts hyperspectral reflectance signatures to device-
independent sRGB hex codes and CIE L*a*b* coordinates using the
CIE 1931 2-degree standard observer and the D65 standard illuminant.
Includes bundled reference data so the package is self-contained.
Handles missing and non-finite reflectance values via a configurable
policy.
spectra2rgb.author: Jhohan Elguera [aut, cre]

spifa.title: Bayesian Spatial Item Factor Analysis
spifa.description:
Fits spatial item factor analysis models for binary responses, following
Chacón-Montalván, E. A., Parry, L., Giorgi, E., Torres, P., Orellana, J. D. Y.,
Moraga, P., and Taylor, B. M. (2025) <doi:10.1214/25-AOAS2072>, using full Bayesian
inference via adaptive Metropolis-Hastings within Gibbs sampling and auxiliary
variables with a probit link function. The latent factors are modelled as the sum of a
predictor effect, a multivariate Gaussian process capturing spatial dependence, and a
multivariate non-spatial term, allowing users to fit and predict spatially-referenced
constructs such as food insecurity or socioeconomic indices. Standard exploratory and
confirmatory item factor analysis are supported as particular cases, simply by
dropping the spatial structure.
spifa.author:
Erick A. Chacón-Montalván [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-8068-1034>),
Emanuele Giorgi [ctb],
Benjamin M. Taylor [ctb]

splitpopsurv.title: Split-Population (Cure / Mover-Stayer) Survival Models
splitpopsurv.description:
Maximum-likelihood estimation of split-population (cure /
mover-stayer) survival models: an accelerated failure-time regression
for event timing among "movers", combined with a logistic regression
on the probability of belonging to the immune "stayer" population.
Five baseline timing distributions are provided -- log-logistic,
Weibull, log-normal, gamma, and the generalized gamma that nests the
other four -- following Schmidt & Witte (1989, Journal of Econometrics)
and Yamaguchi (1992, 1998, Sociological Methodology). This is an R
translation of a set of 'Stata' ml programs, with the log-likelihood
corrected to match the published model and verified by simulation
against known parameters.
splitpopsurv.author: Nobutaka Fukuda [aut, cre]

sppt.title: Spatial Point Pattern Test for Areal Data
sppt.description:
Implements the area-based nonparametric spatial point pattern
test of Andresen (2009) <doi:10.1016/j.apgeog.2008.12.004> for comparing
two spatial distributions of events aggregated to areal units, with the
applications and extensions reviewed in Andresen (2016)
<doi:10.1177/2059799116630659>. Unit-level inference uses bounded Monte
Carlo bootstrap p-values, with marginal confidence interval overlap
retained as an option. Global similarity is summarised by the robust S
index, accompanied by a test of whether two patterns are more different
than two realisations of a single process, and a test of the spatial
arrangement of the differences. A longitudinal extension compares each
period of a time series against a base period and classifies unit-level
trajectories. Publication-ready maps can be redrawn with user-chosen
layouts.
sppt.author:
Martin A. Andresen [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-4767-7276>)

ssurvdr.title:
Sparse Survival Dimension Reduction for High-Dimensional
Censored Data
ssurvdr.description:
Implements sparse survival sufficient dimension reduction methods
for high-dimensional censored data, including covariance-stabilised SAVE,
Maximum Entropy Covariance estimation, information-complexity-guided
variable weighting, dual-space high-dimensional SAVE computation, row-wise
post-estimation sparsification paths, and Cox proportional hazards model
selection.
ssurvdr.author: Kabir Opeyemi Olorede [aut, cre]

streamConnect.title:
Connecting Stream Mining Components Using Sockets and Web
Services
streamConnect.description: Adds functionality to connect stream mining components from the stream package using sockets and Web services. The package can be used to create distributed workflows and plumber-based Web services that can be deployed on most common cloud services.
streamConnect.author:
Michael Hahsler [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0003-2716-1405>)

sundials.title: Vendored 'SUNDIALS' Solver Suite for Linking by Other Packages
sundials.description:
Bundles the pure-C part of the 'SUNDIALS' suite (CVODE, CVODES,
ARKODE, IDA, IDAS and KINSOL with the serial vector and the dense, band and
iterative linear solvers) and builds it into a static library. Other
packages use it by adding 'sundials' to 'LinkingTo' for the headers and
calling sundials::LdFlags() from their 'Makevars' to link the library. No
'Fortran', 'MPI', GPU or external third-party-library modules are included.
'SUNDIALS' is described in Hindmarsh et al. (2005)
<doi:10.1145/1089014.1089020>.
sundials.author:
Konrad Krämer [aut, cre],
Lawrence Livermore National Security [cph] (SUNDIALS source code),
Southern Methodist University [cph] (SUNDIALS source code),
University of Maryland Baltimore County [cph] (SUNDIALS source code),
SUNDIALS contributors [aut, cph] (see inst/AUTHORS)

survHC.title: Higher Criticism Tests for Non-Proportional Hazard Deviations
survHC.description:
Implements omnibus tests for comparing two right-censored survival
samples that are powerful against sparse departures from equal hazards,
where the hazard difference is concentrated in a small and a priori unknown
subset of the follow-up. Exact hypergeometric p-values are computed for each
time interval and aggregated with the Higher Criticism statistic of Donoho
and Jin (2004) <doi:10.1214/009053604000000265>, or alternatively with the
Berk-Jones, Fisher or minimum-p statistics. Global p-values are obtained by
permuting group labels, and the intervals driving a detection can be
recovered for diagnostic plotting. Tests accept either two samples as
vectors or the usual survival formula. The method is described in Kipnis,
Galili and Yakhini (2026) <doi:10.1093/biomet/asaf075>, and the companion
application note is Kipnis, Galili and Yakhini (2026)
<doi:10.48550/arXiv.2610.07268>.
survHC.author:
Alon Kipnis [aut, cre],
Ben Galili [aut],
Zohar Yakhini [aut]

symtests.title: Symmetry Tests for Univariate Data
symtests.description:
Implements statistical tests for detecting departures from symmetry
in univariate data, including procedures based on moments, spacings, order
statistics, and triples. The functions provide straightforward tools for
assessing symmetry in empirical distributions.
symtests.author:
Isabel Parra-Frutos [aut, cre],
Lourdes Molera [aut]

sysbreak.title: Structural Breaks in a System of Equations
sysbreak.description:
Methods for detecting, estimating, and conducting inference
on multiple structural breaks in a linear system of equations, such as
multivariate linear regressions, seemingly unrelated regressions,
vector autoregressions, and network vector autoregressions. Breaks can
occur in the regression coefficients, the covariance matrix of the
errors, or both, and can be restricted to a subset of the
coefficients. The main function, sysbreak(), returns the number of
breaks detected and confidence intervals for the break dates and for
the regression coefficients. A separate function ordbreak() estimates
ordered breaks, in which a break in one subset of equations occurs
before a break in another. Specialized functions for vector
autoregressions varbreak() and network vector autoregressions
netbreak() are also provided. Reference: Qu, Z., and Perron, P.
(2007). 'Estimating and Testing Structural Changes in Multivariate
Regressions.' Econometrica, 75(2), 459-502.
sysbreak.author:
Zhongjun Qu [aut, cre],
Cheolju Kim [aut],
Pierre Perron [aut]

tabby.title: Tidy Interfaces for Tabular Deep Learning
tabby.description:
Model definitions for fitting, tuning, and predicting with
deep learning models for tabular data using the 'parsnip' and
'tidymodels' frameworks. Supported models include the 'TabPFN'
foundation model of Hollmann et al. (2025)
<doi:10.1038/s41586-024-08328-6>, 'TabICL' by Qu et al. (2025)
<doi:10.48550/arXiv.2502.05564>, 'SAINT' by Somepalli et al. (2021)
<doi:10.48550/arXiv.2106.01342>, and the tabular 'ResNet' of
Gorishniy et al. (2021) <doi:10.48550/arXiv.2106.11959>, among
others. Helper functions are also included to create space-filling
grids for tuning parameters that are defined on a per-layer basis.
These functions define the model interfaces; the computations are
carried out by separate engine packages.
tabby.author:
Max Kuhn [aut, cre] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0003-2402-136X>),
Edgar Ruiz [aut],
Posit Software, PBC [cph, fnd] (ROR: <https://ror.org/03wc8by49>)

tampaBayOpenData.title: An R Interface to Tampa Bay Public Open Data
tampaBayOpenData.description:
Provides a lightweight R interface for discovering and retrieving
public 'ArcGIS' datasets across the Tampa Bay region. Search civic datasets
and load records directly into R without manually navigating separate
portals, constructing REST API requests, or handling pagination. Supports
public data published by the City of Tampa, City of St. Petersburg, City of
Clearwater, Hillsborough County, Pinellas County, and Tampa Bay Regional
Planning Council. Discover layers in these and other public 'ArcGIS' portals
and retrieve them by their REST URLs. A publisher registry configures
discovery, while a separate dataset registry identifies layers checked by
package maintainers. Filter catalogs by source, geometry, topic, category,
and modification date. Retrieve queryable layers with validated pagination,
bounded previews, server-side filtering, typed tabular results, optional
spatial objects, and source provenance. Save large downloads as local chunks
that can be validated and resumed. Designed for analysts, researchers,
students, journalists, and civic technologists who work across separate
public data portals. Public source pages are the City of Tampa GeoHub
<https://city-tampa.opendata.arcgis.com/>, St. Petersburg ArcGIS portal
<https://csp.maps.arcgis.com/home/index.html>, Clearwater ArcGIS portal
<https://cityofclearwater.maps.arcgis.com/home/index.html>, Hillsborough
County GeoHub <https://hcfl.gov/about-hillsborough/open-data-and-gis/geohub>,
Pinellas County Enterprise GIS
<https://new-pinellas-egis.opendata.arcgis.com/>, and Tampa Bay Regional
Planning Council GeoHub <https://opendata-tbrpc.hub.arcgis.com/>.
tampaBayOpenData.author:
Jack Lenga [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0003-1153-8105>)

taruwind.title: Reduced-Mode Terrain and Surface Wind Downscaling
taruwind.description:
Constructs reusable local wind responses using a neutral
terrain-following reduced-vertical-mode adjustment and exact raster-ray
integration of finite-fetch surface memory. Explicit metric-grid inputs
separate terrain, target aerodynamic roughness and the effective source
profile. Prepared responses can be applied to wind-component time series
without target-site wind calibration. This diagnostic approximation does
not resolve turbulence or guarantee conservation of the final field.
taruwind.author:
Cem Özen [aut, cre],
Martin Reinecke [ctb] (Author of bundled PocketFFT code),
Peter Bell [ctb, cph] (Bundled PocketFFT code only),
Matteo Frigo [ctb, cph] (Odd-sized DCT-IV code in bundled PocketFFT
only),
Tan Ping Liang [ctb, cph] (Size-search code in bundled PocketFFT only),
Cris Luengo [ctb, cph] (Integer-overflow safeguards in bundled
PocketFFT only),
Max-Planck-Society [cph] (Bundled PocketFFT code only),
Massachusetts Institute of Technology [cph] (Odd-sized DCT-IV code in
bundled PocketFFT only)

termr.title: Modern Reactive Terminal Applications with Data Workflows
termr.description:
Build modern reactive terminal applications for data workflows
in R using reusable widgets, layouts, events, focus management and
themes. A virtual screen buffer and incremental rendering update changed
cells, while a headless driver supports deterministic application tests.
Includes data tables that render visible rows on demand, lazy table
sources, data inspection, SQL editing and background R workers with
progress and streamed output.
Optional database support and static text, Markdown, HTML, SVG and
JSON exports support analytical tools and reports without requiring an
interactive terminal for static output.
termr.author: Akims Mensikovs [aut, cre, cph]

theeuh.title: Write Spaces to Korean Sentences
theeuh.description:
Restores spacing in Korean sentences using a bundled neural
network model and 'ONNX Runtime' <https://onnxruntime.ai/> through 'churon'.
Inference runs locally without a web service or automatic downloads.
theeuh.author:
Chanyub Park [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-6474-2570>),
Heewon Jeon [aut] (Author of KoSpacing code and bundled model assets)

throughyear.title: Linking, Routing and Fairness for Through-Year Assessment
throughyear.description:
Treats a through-year assessment system (interims during the
year feeding a multistage summative) as the unit of analysis. Links
interims to the summative scale with a latent multivariate normal model
that carries each score's measurement error forward and handles missing
interims, estimated by the EM algorithm (Dempster, Laird and Rubin, 1977,
<doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1977.tb01600.x>) with SQUAREM acceleration
(Varadhan and Roland, 2008, <doi:10.1111/j.1467-9469.2007.00585.x>);
simulates cold-start versus prior-informed routing in a
two-stage multistage test; checks whether priors disadvantage late
enrollers, low scorers or fast growers; and evaluates decision accuracy
and consistency of through-year scores against a single summative.
throughyear.author:
Daniel Edi [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-5475-819X>)

tidycreel.title: Tidy Interface for Creel Survey Design and Analysis
tidycreel.description:
Provides a tidy, pipe-friendly interface for creel survey
design, data management, estimation, visualisation, and reporting. A creel
survey interviews anglers on site to estimate fishing effort, catch, and
harvest for a water body. Built on the 'survey' package for design-based
inference, with support for instantaneous, bus-route, ice, camera, and
aerial designs. Catch-rate estimators follow Hoenig, Jones, Pollock,
Robson and Wade (1997) <doi:10.2307/2533116>; bus-route designs follow
Kinloch, McGlennon, Nicoll and Pike (1997)
<doi:10.1016/s0165-7836(97)00068-4>.
tidycreel.author:
Christopher Chizinski [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-9294-2588>)

tidyfault.title: Tidy Fault Tree Analysis
tidyfault.description:
Fault tree analysis with tidy data. Represent a fault tree as two
tables, one of nodes (the top event, gates and basic events) and one of
edges, so the whole workflow stays in ordinary data frames. Derive the
Boolean equation of the top event, enumerate the truth table, and find
minimal cut sets with the Method of Obtaining Cut Sets (MOCUS) algorithm of
Fussell and Vesely (1972), implemented in 'R' and, by default, in C++
through 'Rcpp'. Evaluate thousands of binary or probabilistic scenarios in
one vectorized call, put uncertainty intervals around the top-event
probability, follow it over time, and rank which component fix lowers it
most. Lay out and draw the tree with 'tidygraph', 'igraph' and 'ggplot2'.
Methods follow the "Fault Tree Handbook" of Vesely, Goldberg, Roberts and
Haasl (1981) <https://www.nrc.gov/docs/ML1007/ML100780465.pdf>. A 'Python'
port with the same functions ships in the same repository.
tidyfault.author:
Timothy Fraser [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-4509-0244>),
Jingyao Tong [aut, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0009-0009-6147-756X>),
Cornell University [cph]

tidymatrix.title:
Tidyverse-Style Operations on Matrices with Row and Column
Metadata
tidymatrix.description:
Provides a unified data structure for matrices with associated row
and column metadata, enabling 'tidyverse'-style data manipulation. Following
the approach of 'tidygraph', users can activate rows, columns, or the matrix
itself and operate on it with familiar 'dplyr' verbs, while the matrix and
both metadata tables are kept consistent.
tidymatrix.author: Raivo Kolde [aut, cre]

tidymedia.title: Media File Preprocessing and Metadata for the 'tidyverse'
tidymedia.description:
Batch preprocessing and metadata extraction for audio,
video and image files, built on the command-line programs 'FFmpeg'
(<https://ffmpeg.org/>) and 'MediaInfo'
(<https://mediaarea.net/en/MediaInfo>). Trim, crop, scale, convert and
standardize files one at a time or across a whole directory, and read
container and stream metadata back as tibbles for use with the
'tidyverse'.
tidymedia.author:
Jeffrey Girard [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-7359-3746>)

toeclim.title: Time of Emergence of Climate Signals from Internal Variability
toeclim.description:
Detects when a forced climate change signal emerges from
internal variability ('time of emergence') in annual climate time series
such as temperature or precipitation. The signal is estimated with a
linear, quadratic or locally weighted smoother and compared with noise
estimated from a baseline period. Emergence is defined through
configurable signal-to-noise thresholds and persistence rules.
Uncertainty in the time of emergence is quantified by autoregressive
or moving-block bootstrap resampling. Helpers are provided for
multi-member ensembles, threshold sensitivity, anomaly and annual
aggregation, Mann-Kendall trend tests with trend-free prewhitening,
and synthetic data generation. The approach builds on Hawkins and
Sutton (2012) <doi:10.1029/2011GL050087>, Yue et al. (2002)
<doi:10.1002/hyp.1095> and Sen (1968)
<doi:10.1080/01621459.1968.10480934>.
toeclim.author:
Abul Kashem Faruki Fahim [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-8554-4730>)

tppcm.title:
Step Discriminations for the Two-Parameter Partial Credit Model
on Top of 'TAM'
tppcm.description:
In the two-parameter partial credit model (TPPCM) of Yu (1991)
<https://hdl.handle.net/2142/21459>, every step of a polytomous item has
its own discrimination. Estimation is left to existing software: 'TAM'
(tam.mml.3pl() with a step design matrix, tam.mml.2pl(), tam.mml()) and,
for the bilinear product form and non-negativity constraints, 'sirt'
(xxirt()). The package adds what these packages do not provide: standard
errors of step discriminations based on the full observed information,
step-level Wald tests, and score tests with modification indices and
expected parameter changes for moving down the model ladder saturated
TPPCM -> product form -> generalized partial credit model -> partial
credit model, limited-information fit statistics (the M2 statistic, root
mean square error of approximation, standardized root mean squared
residual, comparative fit index and Tucker-Lewis index; Maydeu-Olivares
and Joe (2006) <doi:10.1007/s11336-005-1295-9>) for any step design, step
contributions to the item information, and tests of differential step
functioning across groups: per-step Lagrange multiplier tests from one
multigroup fit (Glas (1998)
<https://www3.stat.sinica.edu.tw/statistica/j8n3/j8n32/j8n32.htm>), with
the generalized score test of Boos (1992)
<doi:10.1080/00031305.1992.10475921>, likelihood ratio tests with
configural, metric, scalar and partial multigroup designs, score-based
tests (Merkle and Zeileis (2013) <doi:10.1007/s11336-012-9302-4>) and
model-based trees (Zeileis, Hothorn and Hornik (2008)
<doi:10.1198/106186008X319331>). The generalized partial credit model of
Muraki (1992) <doi:10.1177/014662169201600206> is the special case with
equal steps within items.
tppcm.author: Jie-Wen Tsai [aut, cre]

tradesimr.title: Execution and Simulation Engine for Trading Strategies
tradesimr.description:
An R-native trading simulation package with a C++ execution core that turns
strategy intentions and explicit orders into simulated trades, positions,
cash, profit and loss, risk, and performance outputs under configurable
execution, margin, funding, and cost assumptions. The package provides
historical replay, incremental exchange stepping, durable event tables,
append-only agent command logs, registered assets, per-agent
shared-cash cross-margin live accounts, AI agent competitors, scheduled
live-feed stepping, strategy-backed AI agents with diagnostics, calibrated
and coordinated multi-asset market simulation with static covariance,
AR-GARCH, factor, and regime models, durable per-feed simulation state,
profile-aware heterogeneous inventory and margin execution with atomic
mixed-profile order groups, optional portfolio-margin enforcement through
a multi-asset C++ step kernel, local live-service APIs, import/export
helpers, separate replay, live-state, and agent dashboard exports, and installed local
orchestration scripts. It is designed to consume signals, order intents, or
target exposure decisions from compatible strategy packages and market data
from compatible adapters.
tradesimr.author: Oliver Zhou [aut, cre]

transDIF.title: Score Comparability for Translated and Adapted Exams
transDIF.description:
An adaptation-comparability workflow for small, lower-scoring
and unbalanced language groups where standard differential item
functioning (DIF) tools (Magis, Beland, Tuerlinckx and De Boeck, 2010,
<doi:10.3758/BRM.42.3.847>) break down. Calibrates the Rasch model in
each language group, links the groups robustly through the densest
cluster of items rather than assuming DIF cancels out (on anchor
selection see Kopf, Zeileis and Strobl, 2015,
<doi:10.1177/0013164414529792>), detects small-sample DIF with an
empirical-Bayes spike-and-slab model and local false discovery rates
(Efron, 2004, <doi:10.1198/016214504000000089>), quantifies whether
item-level DIF accumulates into different pass rates, explains DIF by
item features to give translators actionable guidance, and drafts a
comparability report.
transDIF.author:
Daniel Edi [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-5475-819X>)

transformerpalettes.title:
Color Palettes Inspired by Transformers Toys, Cartoons and
Comics
transformerpalettes.description:
Color palettes drawn from the Transformers franchise, centered
on the 1984-1989 Generation 1 toys and extending to their Generation 2
re-releases, the cartoon animation models and the Marvel comics. Covers
the leaders, every member and combined form of the
combiner teams (Aerialbots, Protectobots, Technobots, Constructicons,
Stunticons, Combaticons, Terrorcons, Predacons, Seacons, Pretender
Monsters and Breastforce), the Dinobots, the Seeker jets, Soundwave and
the cassettes, the Insecticons, the 1984 Autobot cars and Mini Vehicles
and the 1986 movie cast, with separate palettes for the toy, the cartoon
animation model, the Marvel comic coloring and the Generation 2
re-release where each exists.
Includes 'ggplot2' color and fill scales for discrete and
continuous data, team palettes that take one color from each member of a
combiner team, metadata linking each palette to its character, faction,
team and reference page, and helpers to shortlist palettes that suit
categorical, color-blind-safe, sequential or diverging use. Hex values
are approximations of the toys' plastic and paint colors; the package is
a fan project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Hasbro or
Takara Tomy.
transformerpalettes.author: Brian Maitner [aut, cre]

traveltime.title: Calculate Travel Times Over Space
traveltime.description:
Calculate travel time across a landscape from a set of
user-specified locations, over a friction surface describing the time
taken to cross each cell. Implements the least-cost travel time approach
of Weiss et al. (2018) <doi:10.1038/nature25181> and Weiss et al. (2020)
<doi:10.1038/s41591-020-1059-1>, and provides convenient access to their
global walking and motorised friction surfaces via the 'malariaAtlas'
package. Travel times are computed with 'terra'. See Ryan et al. (2025)
<doi:10.12688/gatesopenres.16356.1> for further details.
traveltime.author:
Gerry Ryan [aut, cre] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0183-7630>),
Daniel Weiss [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-6175-5648>),
Nicholas Tierney [ctb] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0003-1460-8722>)

treehunt.title: Evolutionary Search for Optimal Node Combinations in Trees
treehunt.description:
Provides Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling and genetic
algorithms for searching combinations of nodes in hierarchical trees.
Includes scores for binary outcomes, continuous outcomes, and recurrent
events, with applications to pharmacovigilance and hospital data.
Importance weighting estimates uniform combination score references from
tempered MCMC samples and reports weight-based effective sample sizes.
Computational routines are implemented in C++ via 'Rcpp'.
treehunt.author: Jules Bangard [aut, cre]

trialfigs.title: Efficacy and Safety Graphics for Clinical Review Packages
trialfigs.description:
Builds submission-style efficacy and safety figures used in
clinical review packages, with one simulator for each therapeutic area.
Oncology figures include Kaplan-Meier curves, RECIST waterfalls, swimmer
plots and spider plots. Cardiovascular, endocrine, immunology, infectious
disease and neuroscience figures include time-to-event curves, mean change
from baseline and responder rates. Shared safety figures include an
adverse-event dot plot, an eDISH liver plot, a laboratory shift plot and
an exposure plot. Reference lines follow RECIST 1.1 and the FDA
drug-induced liver injury guidance. This is not an FDA product and does
not guarantee regulatory acceptance.
trialfigs.author: Shekhar [aut, cre]

truedist.title: Estimating the Distribution of True Effects from Noisy Estimates
truedist.description:
Estimates the distribution of true effects (or any latent
parameter) from estimates that each have a known, possibly different,
standard error. The main function, em_smooth(), implements the smoothed
EM (EMS) algorithm of Silverman, Jones, Wilson and Nychka (1990)
<doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1990.tb01788.x> for a nonparametric mixing
distribution on a grid. The smoothing uses one constant standard
deviation, set from the typical standard error and the sample size.
truedist.author: Paul von Hippel [aut, cre]

tsahr.title: Trial Sequential Analysis for Meta-Analyses of Hazard Ratios
tsahr.description:
Performs Trial Sequential Analysis (TSA) for meta-analyses of
time-to-event outcomes reported as hazard ratios. Implements the
Schoenfeld required-events sample-size formula generalised for unequal
allocation, the Diversity (D-squared) heterogeneity adjustment of
Wetterslev et al. (2009), and O'Brien-Fleming-type alpha- and
beta-spending trial sequential monitoring boundaries computed at the
inverse-variance information based on observed study-level log-HR
standard errors (not merely event counts), via
a compiled (C++) recursive numerical integration engine ported from
the R package 'RTSA' (Soerensen, Olsen, Lange and Gluud; an R
implementation of the Trial Sequential Analysis software of the Copenhagen
Trial Unit, <https://ctu.dk/tools>), with no fixed software-imposed limit
on the number of looks (subject to available computational resources). Produces a cumulative
Z-curve plot with efficacy, futility, and conventional significance
boundaries. Methodology follows Miladinovic et al. (2013)
<doi:10.1016/j.jclinepi.2012.11.007> and Wetterslev et al. (2009)
<doi:10.1186/1471-2288-9-86>.
tsahr.author:
Tarak Dhaouadi [aut, cre],
Anne Lyngholm Soerensen [ctb, cph] (author of the RTSA package, from
which the boundary engine is ported),
Markus Harboe Olsen [ctb, cph] (author of the RTSA package, from which
the boundary engine is ported),
Theis Lange [ctb, cph] (author of the RTSA package, from which the
boundary engine is ported),
Christian Gluud [ctb, cph] (author of the RTSA package, from which the
boundary engine is ported)

tsexplorer.title: Exploratory and Diagnostic Tools for Time Series and Forecasts
tsexplorer.description:
Exploratory, descriptive and diagnostic tools for univariate
and multivariate time series and tools to evaluate and compare
forecasts: summary statistics and gaussianity tests; sample
autocorrelation functions with the Ljung and Box (1978)
<doi:10.1093/biomet/65.2.297> and Monti (1994) <doi:10.2307/2337080>
tests; information criteria and Granger (1969) <doi:10.2307/1912791>
causality; unit root tests of Dickey and Fuller (1979)
<doi:10.1080/01621459.1979.10482531> and Phillips and Perron (1988)
<doi:10.1093/biomet/75.2.335>; the cointegration test of Johansen (1988)
<doi:10.1016/0165-1889(88)90041-3>; heteroskedasticity tests;
non-linearity tests of McLeod and Li (1983)
<doi:10.1111/j.1467-9892.1983.tb00373.x>, Tsay (1986)
<doi:10.1093/biomet/73.2.461> and Brock, Dechert, Scheinkman and LeBaron
(1996) <doi:10.1080/07474939608800353>; spectral analysis; and forecast
accuracy measures with the Diebold and Mariano (1995)
<doi:10.1080/07350015.1995.10524599>, sign and Wilcoxon tests. Every
tool is a pure function returning an object with print and plot
methods; the graphical interfaces tooltest() and toolforecast()
('Tcl/Tk' windows or 'shiny' applications) give interactive access to
all of them.
tsexplorer.author:
Diego J. Pedregal [aut, cre, cph],
Ludwig Kanzler [ctb] (Original BDS test algorithm)

tsspiral.title: Spiral Visualisation for Time Series
tsspiral.description: Provides a grammar of graphics geometry for visualising time series using spiral layouts, with each year represented as a separate ring.
tsspiral.author:
Thiyanga S. Talagala [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0656-9789>)

turfLP.title: TURF Analysis with Integer Linear Programming
turfLP.description:
Finds product portfolios that maximize TURF (total unduplicated
reach and frequency) with integer linear programming, following Serra
(2013) <doi:10.1016/j.foodqual.2012.10.001>. The maximum reach problem
is the maximal covering location problem of Church and ReVelle (1974)
<doi:10.1007/BF01942293>. The package solves it as an integer linear
program, so it finds exact optima without enumerating every portfolio.
Ties on reach are broken by frequency and then by the harmonic mean of
the individual product reaches. The package also finds the smallest
portfolio that reaches every reachable respondent. For related work on
TURF for large data sets, see Ennis, Fayle, and Ennis (2012)
<doi:10.1016/j.foodqual.2011.06.004>.
turfLP.author:
John Ennis [aut, cre],
Aigora [cph, fnd]

twoPhaseSens.title:
Sensitivity Analysis for Covariates Observed in Two-Phase
Samples
twoPhaseSens.description:
Provides a structured method-comparison sensitivity-analysis
workflow for linear regression when important continuous adjustment
covariates are observed only in a Phase-2 subsample. Implements naive
analysis, complete-case analysis, fully conditional specification multiple
imputation, joint-model multiple imputation, inverse probability
weighting, and augmented inverse probability weighting, with standardized
tables, diagnostics, and publication-style forest plots. Methodological
background is provided by Little and Rubin (2019)
<doi:10.1002/9781119482260> for general missing-data methods, White and
Carlin (2010) <doi:10.1002/sim.3944> for complete-case analysis with
missing covariates, White, Royston and Wood (2011)
<doi:10.1002/sim.4067> and van Buuren and Groothuis-Oudshoorn (2011)
<doi:10.18637/jss.v045.i03> for chained-equations multiple imputation,
Quartagno, Grund and Carpenter (2019) <doi:10.32614/RJ-2019-028> for
joint-model multiple imputation, Robins, Rotnitzky and Zhao (1994)
<doi:10.1080/01621459.1994.10476818> for inverse-probability weighting
with missing regressors, and Bang and Robins (2005)
<doi:10.1111/j.1541-0420.2005.00377.x> for doubly robust estimation.
twoPhaseSens.author:
Rophence Ojiambo [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-6798-9066>),
Jemar Bather [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0285-3678>)

umg.title: Unified Model Graphs for Statistical Models in Psychology
umg.description:
Constructs, validates, lays out, and renders Unified Model
Graphs (UMG), a formal graphical grammar for statistical models in
psychology. Vertices are typed by observability, support, and
inferential role; edges distinguish stochastic, symmetric,
deterministic, and mixing dependence; plates encode replication and
hierarchy. Diagrams can be themed and rendered with base 'grid'
graphics, with 'ggplot2', as 'TikZ' code, or as 'Graphviz' DOT, and
can be constructed either from one-line motif builders for many
model families or automatically from 'lavaan', 'lme4', 'mirt',
'blavaan', 'brms', 'OpenMx', and 'qgraph' model objects. A diagram
can be inspected as a data frame, summarised, and exported back to
'lavaan' model syntax, making the model-diagram correspondence
operational in both directions. Each diagram also exposes
identification diagnostics (scaling checks, a graphical counting
rule, and a d-separation reader) and generates the exploratory
display scaffolds implied by the model-data duality. The notation
builds on established results for graphical and structural equation
models: plate notation follows Buntine (1994) <doi:10.1613/jair.62>;
the counting rule and scaling checks follow Bollen (1989)
<doi:10.1002/9781118619179>; and the independence reader implements
the d-separation criterion of Geiger, Verma and Pearl (1990)
<doi:10.1002/net.3230200504> through the equivalent ancestral graph
criterion of Lauritzen, Dawid, Larsen and Leimer (1990)
<doi:10.1002/net.3230200503>.
umg.author:
Hsiu-Ting Yu [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-3668-8033>)

varunayan.title: Download and Process 'ERA5', IMD, 'HadEX3' and 'CRU TS' Data
varunayan.description:
Download climate data for a bounding box, polygon or point and
return tidy tables. Sources are the 'ERA5' reanalysis (Hersbach et al.
(2020) <doi:10.1002/qj.3803>) from the 'Copernicus' Climate Data Store
<https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/>, India Meteorological Department
(IMD) gridded rainfall and temperature (Pai et al. (2014)
<doi:10.54302/mausam.v65i1.851>), 'HadEX3' climate extremes (Dunn et al.
(2020) <doi:10.1029/2019JD032263>) and 'CRU TS' (Harris et al. (2020)
<doi:10.1038/s41597-020-0453-3>). Computes heat stress indices,
including wet-bulb globe temperature (Liljegren et al. (2008)
<doi:10.1080/15459620802310770>) and the Universal Thermal Climate Index
(Bröde et al. (2012) <doi:10.1007/s00484-011-0454-1>), and heatwave
indicators, including the Excess Heat Factor (Nairn and Fawcett (2015)
<doi:10.3390/ijerph120100227>).
varunayan.author:
Saket Choudhary [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0001-5202-7633>),
Darakhshan Nehal [aut],
James C. Liljegren [ctb] (Author of the original WBGT C code),
UChicago Argonne, LLC [cph] (Copyright holder of the original WBGT C
code)

vizintel.title: Visualization Intelligence Toolkit
vizintel.description:
Provides automated data profiling and visualization recommendation
tools for exploratory data analysis (EDA). The package inspects a data frame,
classifies each variable as numeric, categorical, or datetime, and computes
distributional statistics including skewness, excess kurtosis, Shapiro-Wilk
normality test p-values (Royston 1995) <doi:10.2307/2986146>, and cardinality.
Based on these profiles, the package scores and ranks candidate chart types
(histogram, density, boxplot, violin, bar, lollipop, scatter, hexbin, line,
heatmap) using an internal taxonomy that accounts for variable types, analysis
goal, skewness, cardinality, and data size. Additional functions audit existing
