ggplot objects for common visualization integrity problems such as truncated
axes, lie factors, overplotting, and dual y-axes following principles described
in Tufte (1983, ISBN:0961392142) and Wilke (2019)
<https://clauswilke.com/dataviz/>. The package also checks visualizations for
accessibility issues and suggests alternative chart types for a given plot.
vizintel.author:
Pooja Thirumal [aut, cre],
Ronesha Navaneethan [aut],
Amrit Pal [ctb] (Supervisor)

webformscore.title: 'WebForms Core'
webformscore.description: A stateless server-driven user interface technology for building web interfaces through server-side user interface manipulation. 'WebForms Core' provides a common structure across multiple programming languages. The server-side class acts as a commander that generates commands, while 'WebFormsJS' serves as the client-side executor that applies them. Commands range from atomic operations, such as adding elements and modifying text and attributes, to higher-level operations such as iterative processing and render. See <https://github.com/webforms-core>.
webformscore.author: Mohammad Rabie [aut, cre]

whence.title: Explain Where a Number Came from in 'shiny' Apps
whence.description:
Lets the viewer of a 'shiny' dashboard click a number, a row
of a summary table or a bar of a 'ggplot2' plot, and see where it came
from. The pipeline that makes the result is split into its steps. Each
step is run in turn, and the number of rows after each step is
recorded. The result is an attrition waterfall that shows how many
rows each step removed, and what share of the rows that was, together
with code that reproduces the result. The steps are found from the
expression alone, so the pipeline does not need to be rewritten. The
rows that contribute to a result, and the rows that a step removed, are
found only when the viewer asks for them.
whence.author: Tanmay Chanda [aut, cre, cph]

windscape.title: Model Landscape Connectivity by Wind
windscape.description:
Model landscape connectivity by wind for ecological and
evolutionary analyses. Summarize long time series of gridded wind data,
downloaded from reanalyses or supplied by the user, into wind roses
describing directional conductance between neighboring grid cells. Model
dispersal through them with least-cost path and random walk algorithms, to
map windsheds around sites and estimate pairwise connectivity among them,
test hypotheses relating wind to ecological data, and visualize wind and
connectivity with 'ggplot2'. The approach builds on Kling and Ackerly
(2020) <doi:10.1038/s41558-020-0848-3> and Kling and Ackerly (2021)
<doi:10.1073/pnas.2017317118>.
windscape.author: Matthew Kling [aut, cre, cph]

wordbankr.title: Accessing the 'Wordbank' Database
wordbankr.description:
Connecting to 'Wordbank' <https://wordbank.stanford.edu>, an open
repository for developmental vocabulary data from the MacArthur-Bates
Communicative Development Inventories (Frank et al. 2017
<doi:10.1017/S0305000916000209>). Data are read from a versioned dataset
hosted on 'Redivis', so analyses can be pinned to a specific release.
wordbankr.author:
Mika Braginsky [aut, cre, cph],
Daniel Yurovsky [ctb],
Michael Frank [ctb],
Danielle Kellier [ctb],
Alvin Tan [ctb]

writeLog.title: Write Printed Output of R Objects to Log Files
writeLog.description:
Provides writeLog(), a small helper that writes the printed
output of a named list of R objects to a text file in a log directory,
one element after another, each preceded by its list name as a heading.
Supports versioned file names and appending to an existing log file.
writeLog.author: Jeff Wu [aut, cre]

xbioclim.title: Bioclimatic Variables from Monthly Climate Data
xbioclim.description:
Computes the 19 standard bioclimatic variables (BIO01-BIO19) from
monthly climate data. The variable set was originally proposed by Nix
(1986, ISBN:978-0-644-04887-3) for the BIOCLIM modelling system and is
also distributed with the CHELSA climatologies (Karger et al., 2017
<doi:10.1038/sdata.2017.122>). Provides both individual variable
functions and a unified interface to compute all 19 variables at once.
Designed as an R implementation of the 'xbioclim' C++ library (Robles
Fernandez, 2026 <https://github.com/alrobles/xbioclimcpp>). Supports
single-pixel vectors and block-based raster processing via 'terra' for
memory-efficient handling of large spatial datasets. Includes helpers
to transform ERA5-Land hourly reanalysis data (Muñoz-Sabater et al.,
2021 <doi:10.5194/essd-13-4349-2021>) into monthly climate inputs.
xbioclim.author: Angel Luis Robles Fernandez [aut, cre]

xlamisc.title: Helper Functions for 'r-xla'
xlamisc.description:
Frequently used generics and helper functions used in 'anvl'
and its companion packages 'stablehlo' and 'pjrt'. Comes with S3
generics to query arrays (shape, data type, device) and to convert
them to R arrays and raw vectors, as well as a class for data types.
xlamisc.author:
Sebastian Fischer [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-9609-3197>),
Daniel Falbel [aut] (ORCID: <https://orcid.org/0009-0006-0143-2392>)

xyt.title: Extract Raster Time Series Values at Points in Space and Time
xyt.description:
Extract values from a time series of rasters at points that each
carry their own date-time. The series is described by a reader function
rather than by data held in memory, so only the time slices actually
needed are read. Values are taken from the slice nearest in time, or
interpolated linearly between the two slices that bracket each point. Derived from the extract()
method of package 'raadtools'.
xyt.author:
Michael D. Sumner [aut, cre, cph] (ORCID:

yaleBraille.title: Generate Braille-Enabled Graphics
yaleBraille.description:
Provides tools for rendering and visualizing
Braille patterns in R, using the 'liblouis' translation library.
For more information see <https://github.com/wininger/yaleBraille>.
yaleBraille.author:
Mike Wininger [aut, cre] (ORCID:
<https://orcid.org/0000-0002-7871-3292>),
liblouis contributors [ctb, cph] (Authors of the bundled liblouis C
library (https://liblouis.io))

zigimports.title: Call 'Zig' Code from R
zigimports.description:
Loads shared libraries compiled from 'Zig' ('.so' files on Linux,
'.dll' files on Windows) and binds their exported functions to R
functions. Arguments are passed by value using the native calling
convention, so functions with mixed integer, double, logical, string and
vector arguments and with return values can be called. Also compiles and
runs 'Zig' code directly from R. Compiling code requires the 'Zig'
compiler.
zigimports.author:
Lakshya Sharma [aut, cre],
Amrit Pal [aut]

zinbcdpmm.title: Bayesian ZINB-Ordinal Joint Model with CDPMM Random Effects
zinbcdpmm.description:
Fits a Bayesian joint model for longitudinal zero-inflated
negative binomial (ZINB) and ordinal outcomes with shared random effects
under a centered Dirichlet process mixture model (CDPMM) prior.  Provides
a blocked Gibbs sampler with Polya-Gamma (PG) and Chinese restaurant table
data augmentation, plus helpers for simulation and posterior summaries
based on the deviance information criterion (DIC), the widely applicable
information criterion (WAIC) and the leave-one-out information criterion
(LOOIC).  The PG augmentation follows Polson, Scott and Windle (2013)
<doi:10.1080/01621459.2013.829001>, the zero-inflated negative binomial
construction follows Neelon (2019) <doi:10.1214/18-BA1132>, and the
centered Dirichlet process mixture prior follows Tang, Tang and Pan (2014)
<doi:10.1016/j.csda.2014.02.015>.
zinbcdpmm.author:
Shuqing Liang [aut, cre],
Jiang Du [aut]

zstd.title: Zstandard Compression
zstd.description:
Compress and decompress data with the 'Zstandard'
algorithm <https://meta.github.io/zstd/>, a fast lossless
compression format. Works on raw vectors in memory and on files, and
can create and extract 'zstd' compressed 'tar' archives. Supports
compression levels, multithreaded compression, long distance
matching, content checksums, and training dictionaries for better
compression of small, similar inputs.
zstd.author:
Gábor Csárdi [aut, cre],
Posit Software, PBC [cph, fnd] (ROR: <https://ror.org/03wc8by49>),
Yann Collet [aut] (Zstandard author),
Meta Platforms, Inc. and affiliates. [cph] (Zstandard copyright holder),
rxi [aut, cph] (microtar author)

zucrypt.title: Cryptography Without System Dependencies
zucrypt.description:
Cryptographic functions over raw vectors, including message
digests of in-memory data, files and connections, keyed-hash message
authentication codes (HMAC), Advanced Encryption Standard (AES)
encryption, constant-time comparison and hexadecimal encoding, backed
by a bundled and pinned copy of the 'Mbed TLS' project's cryptography
library, 'TF-PSA-Crypto' (<https://github.com/Mbed-TLS/TF-PSA-Crypto>).
No system cryptographic library, 'Java' or 'Python' is required at
install or run time. Algorithm names are matched exactly, and failures
are reported as structured conditions. The same primitives, and secure
erasure of native buffers, are published to other packages as a static
archive and as a registered C interface, so that a package can call
them from C without going through R.

Simon Tatham [ctb, cph] (author of the Arm-accelerated SHA-512 code,

zucbor.title: Deterministic and Secure CBOR Encoding and Decoding
zucbor.description:
Encodes R values as Concise Binary Object Representation
(CBOR, RFC 8949; Bormann and Hoffman (2020)
<doi:10.17487/RFC8949>) and decodes CBOR into ordinary R vectors and
lists.
Decoding checks the whole input against configurable depth, size and
item limits before any R object is built, so untrusted input from
network peers and devices cannot drive large allocations. Encoding is
deterministic: identical R objects always produce identical bytes.
Uses a bundled copy of the 'TinyCBOR' library
(<https://github.com/intel/tinycbor>), so no system library is
required.
zucbor.author:
Pedro Baltazar [aut, cre, cph],
Thiago Macieira [aut] (Author of the bundled TinyCBOR library),
Intel Corporation [cph] (TinyCBOR, bundled in src/vendor/tinycbor)

zucsv.title: Read CSV Files Using the 'zsv' Parser
zucsv.description:
Reads comma-separated and other delimited text files into base R
data frames using the 'zsv' C parser <https://github.com/liquidaty/zsv> as
its native backend. Handles quoted fields, embedded delimiters and
newlines, escaped quotes, and both LF and CRLF line endings, and infers
logical, integer, double, and character column types. Column types can
also be given explicitly, in which case a value that cannot be converted
is an error rather than a silently missing value. The 'zsv' sources are
bundled, so there are no runtime dependencies.

zufft.title: Fast Fourier, Cosine and Sine Transforms
zufft.description:
Computes discrete Fourier transforms (complex,
real-to-complex and complex-to-real) and discrete cosine and sine
transforms of types one to four over any axes of an array, with the
fast Fourier transform (FFT) code of 'ducc0'
(<https://github.com/mreineck/ducc>) bundled in the BSD-licensed
subset that 'SciPy' uses. Transforms of any length run in O(n log n)
time, real input uses true real transforms, and several threads can
share one transform.

SciPy Developers [cph] (fast-length search in src/zff_lengths.cpp, from
SciPy)

zufast.title: Fast Portable 'C' Primitives for Parsing and Formatting Data
zufast.description:
A header-only library of small, fast, portable 'C99' primitives
for converting external text and bytes into native values and back:
correctly rounded number parsing (from 'fast_float', through its 'C'
port 'ffc.h'), shortest round-trip number formatting (from 'Ryu'),
ISO 8601 dates and timestamps, booleans, universally unique identifiers
(UUIDs), hexadecimal and Base64, 'XXH3' hashing (from 'xxHash'),
half-precision floats, endian helpers and UTF-8 validation. Other
packages use it through 'LinkingTo' alone; the 'R' functions exist to
test, benchmark and demonstrate the 'C' layer.

Yann Collet [cph] (xxHash)

zuexact.title: Exactly Rounded Sums, Means and Dot Products
zuexact.description:
Sums of double-precision numbers computed exactly and rounded
once, so the result is the correctly rounded true sum and does not depend
on the order of the elements, the platform, or whether R was built with
long doubles. Built on the small and large superaccumulators of Neal
(2015) <doi:10.48550/arXiv.1505.05571>. Provides exactly rounded sums,
means, cumulative sums, dot products and norms, row, column and grouped
sums, accumulators that can be built in pieces and merged across
processes, and a registered 'C' interface for other packages.
zuexact.author:
Pedro Baltazar [aut, cre, cph],
Radford M. Neal [cph] (Author of the vendored 'xsum' library)

zukomp.title: Portable Byte Compression with a Pluggable Codec Registry
zukomp.description:
Compresses and decompresses raw vectors through a single
codec-neutral interface backed by a runtime registry, so the set of
available codecs is discovered rather than fixed at compile time. The
'DEFLATE' family ('gzip', 'zlib', and headerless 'DEFLATE') is built in
from vendored 'miniz' sources, requiring no system compression library.
Decompression enforces configurable output-size and expansion-ratio
limits and reports failures through structured conditions. A registered
C-callable interface lets other packages drive the codecs from C and
register codecs of their own. The formats are specified in Deutsch
(1996) <doi:10.17487/RFC1951>, Deutsch and Gailly (1996)
<doi:10.17487/RFC1950>, and Deutsch (1996) <doi:10.17487/RFC1952>.

zuhtml.title: Parse 'HTML' with a Bundled 'Gumbo' Parser
zuhtml.description:
Parses real-world 'HTML' with a bundled copy of the 'Gumbo'
parser (<https://codeberg.org/gumbo-parser/gumbo-parser>), which
follows the 'WHATWG' parsing algorithm, so that no system library is
required. Documents become immutable trees navigated with a documented
subset of 'CSS' selectors. Attributes, text, lists, tables, links,
forms and page metadata ('JSON-LD', microdata) are extracted into
ordinary character vectors, lists and data frames, and nodes convert
to 'Markdown'. Input is a string, raw bytes, a file, a URL or a
connection, and raw input is decoded as browsers decode it, from a
byte-order mark or a '<meta>' declaration. Parsing is bounded by limits on input size, native memory and nesting
depth.
zuhtml.author:
Pedro Baltazar [aut, cre, cph],
Google Inc. [cph] (Gumbo, bundled in src/vendor/gumbo),
Bjoern Hoehrmann [cph] (UTF-8 decoder in src/vendor/gumbo/utf8.c)

zujson.title: Lightweight JSON Parsing and Serialization
zujson.description:
Converts between JSON text and ordinary R vectors and lists
through a small, predictable set of functions, backed by vendored
'yyjson' <https://github.com/ibireme/yyjson> and requiring no system
JSON library. Parsing accepts character, raw and file input and reports
failures through structured conditions; serialization writes UTF-8 bytes
suitable for use directly as an HTTP request body. The type mapping is
deliberately narrow and fully documented, so what goes in and what comes
out are both predictable.
zujson.author:
Pedro Baltazar [aut, cre, cph],
YaoYuan [ctb, cph] (author of the bundled yyjson library)

zuxml.title: Small XML Parser and Document Tree
zuxml.description:
Reads, navigates, and writes XML documents using a bundled
copy of the 'Expat' parser (<https://libexpat.github.io/>), so that no
system XML library is required. Documents are parsed into a faithful
immutable tree exposed through a small vectorized navigation
interface. Parsing is strict by default: document type
declarations are rejected, external entity resolution is not compiled
in, and configurable limits bound nesting depth and memory use. A
registered C interface allows other packages to parse XML without
linking against the parser themselves, and to feed it incrementally
so that a large document need not be held in memory all at once.

zuyaml.title: Parse and Emit 'YAML' 1.2
zuyaml.description:
Converts between 'YAML' 1.2
(<https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/>) and ordinary R objects using a bundled
copy of the 'cyaml' C11 parser and emitter
(<https://github.com/andrewmd5/cyaml>), so there is no system dependency
and no runtime dependency beyond R itself. Ambiguous 'YAML' features are
handled strictly and predictably: duplicate keys are refused by default,
the 'YAML' 1.2 core schema is followed so that yes and no resolve as
strings, and integers beyond double precision are preserved rather than
silently rounded. A stream of documents and a sequence are different
things, and the interface keeps them apart. Input size, nesting depth
and the number of values materialised are all bounded, which makes the
parser usable on untrusted input.
zuyaml.author:
Pedro Baltazar [aut, cre, cph],
Andrew Sampson [ctb, cph] (author of the bundled cyaml library)
